BF7D1C90DFE601317DA168A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

BF7CC2F0DFE601317DA068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

BF7C6F40DFE601317D9F68A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

BF7C26B0DFE601317D9E68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

BF7BDE20DFE601317D9D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

BF7B9430DFE601317D9C68A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

BF7B44E0DFE601317D9B68A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

BF7AE830DFE601317D9A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

BF7A9AC0DFE601317D9968A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

BF7A4AD0DFE601317D9868A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

BF799EC0DFE601317D9668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

BF795190DFE601317D9568A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

BF78F980DFE601317D9468A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

BF786770DFE601317D9268A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

BF781F60DFE601317D9168A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

BF77D520DFE601317D9068A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

BF773980DFE601317D8E68A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

BF7652D0DFE601317D8B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

BF75F690DFE601317D8A68A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

BF7538B0DFE601317D8868A86D17958E.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

BF749710DFE601317D8668A86D17958E.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

BF742B80DFE601317D8568A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

BF737B00DFE601317D8368A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

BF732EE0DFE601317D8268A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

BF72E160DFE601317D8168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

BF71E670DFE601317D7E68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

BF7196B0DFE601317D7D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

BF713DA0DFE601317D7C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

BF709180DFE601317D7A68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

BF6FDC00DFE601317D7868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

BF6F92C0DFE601317D7768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

BF6EFCB0DFE601317D7568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

BF6E9C80DFE601317D7468A86D17958E.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

BF6E22A0DFE601317D7368A86D17958E.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

BF6DCB80DFE601317D7268A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

BF6D3340DFE601317D7068A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

BF6CE570DFE601317D6F68A86D17958E.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

BF6C8DB0DFE601317D6E68A86D17958E.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

BF6C44B0DFE601317D6D68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

BF6BFA90DFE601317D6C68A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

BF6BAD80DFE601317D6B68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

BF6B5420DFE601317D6A68A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

BF6A5130DFE601317D6768A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

BF6A0940DFE601317D6668A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

BF69C090DFE601317D6568A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

BF692500DFE601317D6368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

BF68C7F0DFE601317D6268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

BF687810DFE601317D6168A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

BF67E6D0DFE601317D5F68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

BF679C10DFE601317D5E68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

BF66AD80DFE601317D5B68A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

BF665890DFE601317D5A68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

BF660660DFE601317D5968A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

BF65A570DFE601317D5868A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

BF6534A0DFE601317D5768A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

BF64C180DFE601317D5668A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

BF637D80DFE601317D5368A86D17958E.description: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.

BF6329F0DFE601317D5268A86D17958E.description: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.

BF62DA40DFE601317D5168A86D17958E.description: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

BF628C10DFE601317D5068A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

BF624310DFE601317D4F68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

BF61F8F0DFE601317D4E68A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.

BF61A4C0DFE601317D4D68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

BF6156A0DFE601317D4C68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.

BF610D20DFE601317D4B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

BF60C230DFE601317D4A68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

BF607210DFE601317D4968A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.

BF6013C0DFE601317D4868A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

BF5F9380DFE601317D4768A86D17958E.description: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.

BF5F1AF0DFE601317D4668A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.

BF5DFF90DFE601317D4368A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

BF5D68B0DFE601317D4168A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

BF5D1C20DFE601317D4068A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

BF5CD390DFE601317D3F68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

BF5C8610DFE601317D3E68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

BF5C2E70DFE601317D3D68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

BF5BE700DFE601317D3C68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

BF5BA040DFE601317D3B68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

BF5B1010DFE601317D3968A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

BF5ABB10DFE601317D3868A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

BF5A72B0DFE601317D3768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

BF59DA10DFE601317D3568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

BF598400DFE601317D3468A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

BF592560DFE601317D3368A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

BF58C850DFE601317D3268A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

BF587BC0DFE601317D3168A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

BF56F220DFE601317D2D68A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.

BF56A730DFE601317D2C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.

BF565B40DFE601317D2B68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

BF557210DFE601317D2868A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

BF551900DFE601317D2768A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BF54CC00DFE601317D2668A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.

BF547200DFE601317D2568A86D17958E.description: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).

BF541820DFE601317D2468A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

BF536070DFE601317D2268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.

BF531460DFE601317D2168A86D17958E.description: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.

BF52C590DFE601317D2068A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

BF521D90DFE601317D1E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

BF51B6C0DFE601317D1D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

BF515D20DFE601317D1C68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

BF506D10DFE601317D1968A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

BF500C50DFE601317D1868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BF4F61C0DFE601317D1668A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).

BF4F0B30DFE601317D1568A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).

BF4E6410DFE601317D1368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.

BF4E0AF0DFE601317D1268A86D17958E.description: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.

BF4DBE60DFE601317D1168A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.

BF4D2850DFE601317D0F68A86D17958E.description: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.

BF4CDB70DFE601317D0E68A86D17958E.description: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.

BF4C7D20DFE601317D0D68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

BF4B8770DFE601317D0A68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

BF4B4060DFE601317D0968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BF4AF790DFE601317D0868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

BF4AA820DFE601317D0768A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

BF4A5120DFE601317D0668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

BF49C250DFE601317D0468A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

BF4979A0DFE601317D0368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

BF4931D0DFE601317D0268A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

BF488760DFE601317D0068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

BF483510DFE601317CFF68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

BEE21490DFE601317C6468A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

BEE1B720DFE601317C6368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

BEE15610DFE601317C6268A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

BEE0F230DFE601317C6168A86D17958E.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

BEE0A880DFE601317C6068A86D17958E.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

BEE05D90DFE601317C5F68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

BEE00B40DFE601317C5E68A86D17958E.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

BEDF9160DFE601317C5D68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

BEDF2F20DFE601317C5C68A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

BEDEE220DFE601317C5B68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

BEDDAEC0DFE601317C5768A86D17958E.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

BEDD4D10DFE601317C5668A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

BEDD00C0DFE601317C5568A86D17958E.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

BEDC51A0DFE601317C5368A86D17958E.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

BEDBF3D0DFE601317C5268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

BEDBA200DFE601317C5168A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

BEDB4C10DFE601317C5068A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

BEDAB1E0DFE601317C4E68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

BED9E460DFE601317C4C68A86D17958E.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

BED983D0DFE601317C4B68A86D17958E.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).

BED939E0DFE601317C4A68A86D17958E.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

BED8EE10DFE601317C4968A86D17958E.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

BED8A130DFE601317C4868A86D17958E.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

BED84E30DFE601317C4768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

BED74DC0DFE601317C4468A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

BED6F780DFE601317C4368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

BED6A700DFE601317C4268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

BED5FF50DFE601317C4068A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

BED56CD0DFE601317C3E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

BED52270DFE601317C3D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

BED47400DFE601317C3B68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

BED42590DFE601317C3A68A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

BED3DE90DFE601317C3968A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

BED396B0DFE601317C3868A86D17958E.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

BED2FC10DFE601317C3668A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.

BED2A770DFE601317C3568A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

BED25B00DFE601317C3468A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

BED210F0DFE601317C3368A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

BED1C540DFE601317C3268A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

BED16EA0DFE601317C3168A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups

BED08070DFE601317C2E68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

BED02F00DFE601317C2D68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

BECFD750DFE601317C2C68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

BECF12B0DFE601317C2A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

BECEA0F0DFE601317C2968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

BECE4610DFE601317C2868A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

BECDB0A0DFE601317C2668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

BECC89B0DFE601317C2268A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

BECC3ED0DFE601317C2168A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

BECBEEC0DFE601317C2068A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

BECB46C0DFE601317C1E68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

BECAF470DFE601317C1D68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

BECA32D0DFE601317C1B68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

BEC9DE30DFE601317C1A68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

BEC992C0DFE601317C1968A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

BEC89CC0DFE601317C1668A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

BEC7E7B0DFE601317C1468A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

BEC79610DFE601317C1368A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

BEC73DF0DFE601317C1268A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

BEC6D8A0DFE601317C1168A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

BEC67200DFE601317C1068A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

BEC624F0DFE601317C0F68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

BEC5CD20DFE601317C0E68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

BEC508C0DFE601317C0C68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

BEC4AB10DFE601317C0B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

BEC45FC0DFE601317C0A68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

BEC3C220DFE601317C0868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

BEC35470DFE601317C0768A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

BEC2E850DFE601317C0668A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

BEC29DA0DFE601317C0568A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

BEC25150DFE601317C0468A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

BEC1B320DFE601317C0268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

BEC10850DFE601317C0068A86D17958E.description: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.

BEC0B1B0DFE601317BFF68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.

BEC05F60DFE601317BFE68A86D17958E.description: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.

BEBFBB20DFE601317BFC68A86D17958E.description: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.

BEBF69D0DFE601317BFB68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

BEBEC1A0DFE601317BF968A86D17958E.description: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).

BEBE7550DFE601317BF868A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.

BEBE2480DFE601317BF768A86D17958E.description: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.

BEBDBD20DFE601317BF668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

BEBD58C0DFE601317BF568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

BEBCC550DFE601317BF368A86D17958E.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

BEBC7A70DFE601317BF268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

BEBB7BE0DFE601317BEF68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

BEBB2270DFE601317BEE68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BEBACA50DFE601317BED68A86D17958E.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

BEBA7D50DFE601317BEC68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

BEBA2F80DFE601317BEB68A86D17958E.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

BEB992A0DFE601317BE968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.

BEB945F0DFE601317BE868A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

BEB8F860DFE601317BE768A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.

BEB85560DFE601317BE568A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

BEB7DAA0DFE601317BE468A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

BEB781B0DFE601317BE368A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

BEB6A050DFE601317BE068A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.

BEB651D0DFE601317BDF68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BEB5F9D0DFE601317BDE68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

BEB5AF00DFE601317BDD68A86D17958E.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

BEB4CC80DFE601317BDA68A86D17958E.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

BEB47E80DFE601317BD968A86D17958E.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.

BEB42360DFE601317BD868A86D17958E.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

BEB37410DFE601317BD668A86D17958E.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

BEB32480DFE601317BD568A86D17958E.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

BEB2D880DFE601317BD468A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

BEB1DD50DFE601317BD168A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

BEB192F0DFE601317BD068A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BEB14880DFE601317BCF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

BEB0FC40DFE601317BCE68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

BEB0AAA0DFE601317BCD68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

BEAFFF10DFE601317BCB68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

BEAFA7D0DFE601317BCA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

BEAF5B50DFE601317BC968A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

BEAE8400DFE601317BC768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

BEAE2770DFE601317BC668A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

BEADCF30DFE601317BC568A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: New Jersey Core Curriculum Content Standards for Visual and Performing Arts

E65BBC7614B241D1B3A9148EE9E890B3.description: Recognize the making subject or theme in works of dance, music, theatre, and visual art.

142D6B8069D74AC4A7242FFFB27162CE.description: Contextual clues are embedded in works of art and provide insight into artistic intent.

B6467FC7981D446BB5BB28C7A07A8B24.description: Apply the principles of positive critique in giving and receiving responses to performances.

93BEB21DE723420AADBDE2CA129F6C8E.description: Constructive criticism is an important evaluative tool that enables artists to communicate more effectively.

6EFE0BCBED464A718127139F80C6307D.description: Observe the basic arts elements in performances and exhibitions and use them to formulate objective assessments of artworks in dance, music, theatre, and visual art.

887F6E0C388444CF9A9840403413B678.description: Relative merits of works of art can be qualitatively and quantitatively assessed using observable criteria.

885DE35DA6ED454293B96FECFD20D133.description: Distinguish patterns in nature found in works of dance, music, theatre, and visual art.

8695EB3B526F495CBAD24E880AA1A8EC.description: Use imagination to create a story based on an arts experience that communicated an emotion or feeling, and tell the story through each of the four arts disciplines (dance, music, theatre, and visual art).

768FB08B042940238A3414A98C18CE83.description: Compare and contrast culturally and historically diverse works of dance, music, theatre, and visual art that evoke emotion and that communicate cultural meaning.

DE119B0B72C14D77AAE27CF433BE031D.description: Identify aesthetic qualities of exemplary works of art in dance, music, theatre, and visual art, and identify characteristics of the artists who created them (e.g., gender, age, absence or presence of training, style, etc.).

EDF66AEC2F7D4D87AFE014B46365AEFD.description: Each arts discipline (dance, music, theatre, and visual art) has distinct characteristics, as do the artists who create them.

276C98F2598E4C5580230F5D26ED7571.description: Aesthetic Responses & Critique Methodologies: All students will demonstrate and apply an understanding of arts philosophies, judgment, and analysis to works of art in dance, music, theatre, and visual art.

96C7CE3878934F889E9A5C4FFED4329E.description: Create works of art that are based on observations of the physical world and that illustrate how art is part of everyday life, using a variety of art mediums and art media.

D3951339AB4C4A8087339EA28DDB97D3.description: Visual awareness stems from acute observational skills and interest in visual objects, spaces, and the relationship of objects to the world.

0A361D52B43F439793C26B920C349F6B.description: Explore the use of a wide array of art mediums and select tools that are appropriate to the production of works of art in a variety of art media.

9EA1B59C3782460194FE2386522AFAAE.description: Knowledge of visual art media necessitates an understanding of a variety of traditional and nontraditional tools, applications, possibilities, and limitations.

2DD6DD87E8B64B92BEA1B74CA7C5FDB7.description: Employ basic verbal and visual art vocabulary to demonstrate knowledge of the materials, tools, and methodologies used to create and tell visual stories.

4B0157C59B4E43D2B50C65BFFCA28513.description: Each of the visual art forms uses various materials, tools, and techniques that are associated with unique verbal and visual vocabularies.

3570F6AA716440F299614CA4C001BBA2.description: Use symbols to create personal works of art based on selected age-appropriate themes, using oral stories as a basis for pictorial representation.

56944492A33343B1BB244A98DBD87DFC.description: Symbols convey meaning agreed upon by a group or culture. Manipulation of the basic elements of art and principles of design for personal expression results in visual communication that may be relevant in a variety of settings.

8824E9722A32480AA0BE385B0273D7BD.description: Create two- and three-dimensional works of art using the basic elements of color, line, shape, form, texture, and space, as well as a variety of art mediums and application methods.

A9C7FB5E09D74BD98AAB7F9D155CC130.description: Visual statements in art are derived from the basic elements of art regardless of the format and medium used to create the art. There are also a wide variety of art media, each having its own materials, processes, and technical application methods for exploring solutions to creative problems.

387B959CD7374834AE743BD884A0201E.description: Develop awareness of vocal range, personal space, and character-specific vocal and creative movement choices.

19E3EB1C5FB84129979E42629363FFCC.description: Voice and movement have broad ranges of expressive potential.

3864DD98295140D6B4FC77255E652473.description: Use voice and movement in solo, paired, and group pantomimes and improvisations.

B23197821D28402CB7BDF4C68F19C3A5.description: Actors use voice and movement as tools for storytelling.

37A66C5898274BC882C350E214C75E83.description: Portray characters when given specifics about circumstances, plot, and thematic intent, demonstrating logical story sequence and informed character choices.

C7CD558832814B2F87E771C5E93FB458.description: Plays may use narrative structures to communicate themes.

6BB6184A2BDB42AD8A7CF48C4BFEC67D.description: Blend unison and harmonic parts and vocal or instrumental timbres while matching dynamic levels in response to a conductor's cues.

8F6517B0380747869B2DE6ED24569684.description: Basic conducting patterns and gestures provide cues about how and when to execute changes in dynamics, timbre, and timing.

55945478644B4537A2A9C41A85F3E603.description: Sing or play simple melodies or rhythmic accompaniments in AB and ABA forms independently and in groups, and sight-read rhythmic and music notation up to and including eighth notes and rests in a major scale.

81EDD6AD3E2545BDA7520232D2BD393C.description: Prescribed forms and rules govern music composition, rhythmic accompaniment, and the harmonizing of parts.

06A85B4664014DC8A78007D24D5C6E9D.description: Improvise short tonal and rhythmic patterns over ostinatos, and modify melodic or rhythmic patterns using selected notes and/or scales to create expressive ideas.

E33B548F317A478AA5F51EDD4780E1E9.description: Improvisation is a foundational skill for music composition.

BCF6E50BA978493AA39520808DE8C99D.description: Vocalize the home tone of familiar and unfamiliar songs, and demonstrate appropriate posture and breathing technique while performing songs, rounds, or canons in unison and with a partner.

39AF44595C034BFD968CFAAB3919CCC2.description: Proper breathing technique and correct posture improve the timbre of the voice and protect the voice when singing.

64B16AAF22C042B1A35841842C638C7E.description: Demonstrate correct playing techniques for Orff instruments or equivalent homemade instruments.

D038E9EE2EC743BEB14CE36101EB19AC.description: Playing techniques for Orff instruments develop foundational skills used for hand percussion and melodic percussion instruments.

4016C293F2244C479EFDA0DE68734CA2.description: Demonstrate developmentally appropriate vocal production/vocal placement and breathing technique.

F66AE556E6FC44F3853F680BB1A4B4C3.description: Proper vocal production/vocal placement requires an understanding of basic anatomy and the physical properties of sound.

ED61D5205DE0483BB520EC8D89D25CA7.description: Clap, sing, or play on pitch from basic notation in the treble clef, with consideration of pitch, rhythm, dynamics, and tempo.

411EC4120B4648968A513DD47189EC4E.description: The ability to read music notation correlates with musical fluency and literacy. Notation systems are complex symbolic languages that indicate pitch, rhythm, dynamics, and tempo.

880A9256782345A580B1EA2DE6976124.description: Create and perform original movement sequences alone and with a partner using locomotor and non-locomotor movements at various levels in space.

423AD55DAE9E4338BD252E3D0F870BAA.description: Locomotor and non-locomotor movements may contribute equally to the thematic content of solo and ensemble dances.

E8A525A4295040ABBA7F45D6B31D0F73.description: Define and maintain personal space, concentrate, and appropriately direct focus while performing movement skills.

F30D3AB1B8ED4909B123495E8EA93BC2.description: The integrity of choreographed sequences is maintained by personal and group spatial relationships. Dance movement skills also require concentration and the intentional direction of focus during performance.

13A7E5F4E4FC41949D4EB1255AF7AB9E.description: Create and perform planned and improvised movement sequences, alone and in small groups, with variations in tempo, meter, rhythm, spatial level (i.e., low, middle, and high), and spatial pathway.

127B5C24C2624F0498E9157F7BE10EEF.description: The creation of an original dance composition often begins with improvisation. Movement sequences change when applying the elements of dance.

D819CE68EE9741C69B940D2F3E95A1A7.description: Create and perform planned and improvised movement sequences using the elements of dance, with and without musical accompaniment, to communicate meaning around a variety of themes.

9DE280875DD64CB7A270E0E394F4E8E6.description: The elements of dance are time, space, and energy. Improvisational structures facilitate movement invention. Musical or non-musical accompaniment is a choice. Dance can communicate meaning around a variety of themes.

E1E6CCBC317E4AC89B6CCA9C784690C4.description: Performance: All students will synthesize those skills, media, methods, and technologies appropriate to creating, performing, and/or presenting works of art in dance, music, theatre, and visual art.

5B283502A9624BD3A7D2C02241F95FB5.description: Identify how artists and specific works of dance, music, theatre, and visual art reflect, and are affected by, past and present cultures.

0A2F0B3F60BA4857872971D4299098DF.description: The function and purpose of art-making across cultures is a reflection of societal values and beliefs.

888BAC0C7ED741858462BD9C78D7E7BC.description: Identify characteristic theme-based works of dance, music, theatre, and visual art, such as artworks based on the themes of family and community, from various historical periods and world cultures.

E73857BEB45A43BCBE8227065F6B14F8.description: Dance, music, theatre, and visual artwork from diverse cultures and historical eras have distinct characteristics and common themes that are revealed by contextual clues within the works of art.

1A246E6B7BBF4C69A9BCB66F2041D2BD.description: History of the Arts and Culture

7C6087F7177044A0A39BE805EAB523D2.description: History of the Arts and Culture: All students will understand the role, development, and influence of the arts throughout history and across cultures.

577F36178CE340AD84ADB39C5D65B512.description: Identify elements of art and principles of design in specific works of art and explain how they are used.

75F7C171F4F74C0AB3F2932A3279C2CE.description: Recognizing the elements of art and principles of design in artworks of known and emerging artists, as well as peers, is an initial step toward visual literacy.

3399BB3CE9184369B9E3A03E8276FA74.description: Identify the basic elements of art and principles of design in diverse types of artwork.

8A440C484EDE4A7A938C8621C563B413.description: The basic elements of art and principles of design govern art creation and composition.

BE083700DFE601317A8268A86D17958E.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). BE076E10DFE601317A8068A86D17958E.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

BE06FD20DFE601317A7F68A86D17958E.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

BE0694E0DFE601317A7E68A86D17958E.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.
comments: Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

BE063480DFE601317A7D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context

BE05D880DFE601317A7C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.
comments: For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.

BE057D40DFE601317A7B68A86D17958E.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

BE051980DFE601317A7A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

BE04C1F0DFE601317A7968A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

9FD07EA593914ACBB34DA921C48036A8.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

1D4FE6A341024C5FADA1CCEFCA15EF4B.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

717855DDCA6143C6952242C4126AA9A5.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

D5DF8F1F6EEB4AF3AD09EA2CFB165BCB.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

8FE1266ECC5F4494A068508542F7C408.description: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

7D50DB2D23DF424B9E7A4CD0C14C621B.description: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

CA18E85E21EE4F2880B9B5334AAECF2C.description: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.

49C98195DD794C23B351109D43EF8AAD.description: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of solutions could include designing an earthquake resistant building and improving monitoring of volcanic activity.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to earthquakes, floods, tsunamis, and volcanic eruptions.

68834C51F8684E4A8B6839575417BDF4.description: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of renewable energy resources could include wind energy, water behind dams, and sunlight; non-renewable energy resources are fossil fuels and fissile materials. Examples of environmental effects could include loss of habitat due to dams, loss of habitat due to surface mining, and air pollution from burning of fossil fuels.
Clarification Statement: Maps can include topographic maps of Earth's land and ocean floor, as well as maps of the locations of mountains, continental boundaries, volcanoes, and earthquakes.
1834762236D742E8BDEC510F68BAEBD3.description: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of variables to test could include angle of slope in the downhill movement of water, amount of vegetation, speed of wind, relative rate of deposition, cycles of freezing and thawing of water, cycles of heating and cooling, and volume of water flow.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to a single form of weathering or erosion.
F9DB0512D3FB40B59748CD364F94E719.description: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.

7A309F891DDF488F96DEC81939564F4B.description: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence from patterns could include rock layers with marine shell fossils above rock layers with plant fossils and no shells, indicating a change from land to water over time; and, a canyon with different rock layers in the walls and a river in the bottom, indicating that over time a river cut through the rock.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include specific knowledge of the mechanism of rock formation or memorization of specific rock formations and layers. Assessment is limited to relative time.

76738D6680914F4EA9154C2A9961BD55.description: Use a model to describe that animals' receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information in different ways.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on systems of information transfer.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include the mechanisms by which the brain stores and recalls information or the mechanisms of how sensory receptors function.

68EBB81E51F04E43A1FDED6FE6BFDBF0.description: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of structures could include thorns, stems, roots, colored petals, heart, stomach, lung, brain, and skin.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to macroscopic structures within plant and animal systems.

069D71EDB32E46F687BDAA7E7CCCC8F1.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

AF6372DDF90B42EE97FBB71E9C1762AD.description: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of solutions could include drums sending coded information through sound waves, using a grid of 1's and 0's representing black and white to send information about a picture, and using Morse code to send text.

414E1595FCF94229A4982D720B04AB7C.description: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include knowledge of specific colors reflected and seen, the cellular mechanisms of vision, or how the retina works.
Clarification Statement: Examples of models could include diagrams, analogies, and physical models using wire to illustrate wavelength and amplitude of waves.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include interference effects, electromagnetic waves, non-periodic waves, or quantitative models of amplitude and wavelength.
316695B963984FD8A9434AB53540FB3D.description: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.

961F952151714A4C8DB4B3953CF0CADF.description: Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of devices could include electric circuits that convert electrical energy into motion energy of a vehicle, light, or sound; and, a passive solar heater that converts light into heat. Examples of constraints could include the materials, cost, or time to design the device.
Assessment Boundary: Devices should be limited to those that convert motion energy to electric energy or use stored energy to cause motion or produce light or sound.
F5EA1C54F3D1439798CBE0CC5DF7D36C.description: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.

comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the change in the energy due to the change in speed, not on the forces, as objects interact.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative measurements of energy.
D4B5539A22DE4BF49B931E567682BA41.description: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.

379BD5AB57DF44FB8CD47BD05BDB95B0.description: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative measurements of energy.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative measures of changes in the speed of an object or on any precise or quantitative definition of energy.
2BFF26B2AA6E47A88951A901F80D9689.description: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.

document.title: New Jersey Core Curriculum Content Standards for Social Studies

19FBF48AAF2C4444A1217F15BB822C06.description:
Active citizens in the 21st century:
  • Determine the credibility and value of information, while also considering context, point of view, and multiple perspectives.
  • Analyze sources of prejudice and discrimination and propose solutions to eliminate them.
  • Collaboratively evaluate possible solutions to problems and conflicts that arise in an interconnected world.
  • Critically analyze information, make ethical judgments, and responsibly address controversial issues.
  • Communicate through rational and persuasive written and oral arguments to present solutions to controversial issues.
  • Make informed and reasoned decisions and accept responsibility for the consequences of their actions and/or inactions.
  • Take actions that result in a more just and equitable society.

557D85A8783E420FBF505C155F1E8FD3.description: Active Citizenship in the 21st Century: All students will acquire the skills needed to be active, informed citizens who value diversity and promote cultural understanding by working collaboratively to address the challenges that are inherent in living in an interconnected world.

B131B4F852CE4D888EB267453390D883.description: The Era of the Great Wars: Nationalism, imperialism, industrialization, and militarism contributed to an increase in economic and military competition among European nations, the Ottoman Empire, and Japan, and led to World War I. World Wars I and II were "total wars" in which nations mobilized entire populations and economies and employed new military tactics that resulted in unprecedented death and destruction, as well as drastic changes in political boundaries. World Wars I and II challenged economic and political power structures and gave rise to a new balance of power in the world. Economic, technological, and military power and bureaucracies have been used by nations to deliberately and systematically destroy ethnic/racial, political, and cultural groups.

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards.
