comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (¼), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (¼).

565B6E67073540408292C4F45F57F9BC.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

B15A59A4D87B4BB1B6FC2A342C3C1B1C.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

B75B4B1229EA4D42AEBA6ED168966251.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

E07A6A9F234345C3B38FD59C379AA136.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

25FF2BB788944206A29A2D91C3B196FE.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

F8BCE8EB0E1B4D20A59C5F606A6ADFC1.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

9E3E60C92EEB420D8CC7E9DAE6AD24BA.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

1352DE30B94C4370BFF9D7E480A25DCE.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

0F125F9193D14EF6A2794B55F7839CD4.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

A1DFE067FFCA4F49B6874EFD4D68CE7B.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

AA36CC94A4C14E1187A98C83A5446332.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

88DA6B31C325492594249E72A05CC61C.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

49B969CABBB7410D8CB1D38B6FD1556B.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

153555530A36477680CF440D7DBAAD31.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

996EA87938444B7486D10FBA3C7E68F6.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

E23E24D39DB8476FA436420B16CE82F7.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

48D5E4E22F9347EA95EC246DB0B82BA8.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

B10BEAA8769047A2905BCDAEE6A5CAEC.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

7BF14D982A1540118FEFAE5779DABC43.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

7137980CF6A54DB595DBBBA18B80D307.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

53617D034A3143E5BC506D053047825F.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

BCA9A75FFD854CD18EA1B56F1F565582.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

0478550C25744D8B85B1C9EEA713CF9B.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

923626AC53C04A6487918E5E6AE62C4F.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm. mm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), ...

40D46F07ED754614A8FFF0342EF81D49.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

10C16923209D47E6A666730E74E0D5E1.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

0FE908FD21364574B38B9A51AD649B35.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

355486A6B4AE414284A0EBE867923476.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

228F661654EE4169B1226F76A55CEC6E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

1B92E3B7BF094EC68B5877CF10FD5D77.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

CB3684D65D0D4965B1E9F4870685EF32.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

7FD6200BFAEA414C9F5FE31FC14F94ED.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

8577008910E44782B065C2F091521752.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

8D8F4FC1EB4C4E148ADF96CC53766403.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

924759876DF644D3BD333097CFE726A2.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

B8C62CA5D15C4F59AD58BB0B15CC654B.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1– 100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

FD4FDB74DD9F4B499EEC2DC3C99671C2.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

7E7C0401E7DE40298A967DD63BC5AD1D.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

DCDD3505F3B145948F25AAEDABF4A6C4.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

52E8261968024578A67C3DB99D915412.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

0622DD68EBDD47519E06606F933CB1E8.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

89BE4BF6E0B4420DB82D6B9DADF349AA.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3DD2486FAEC548DCA6A908E7B1646E4E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

1A1C71C28ED946D1A956955EAA5B0701.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

B481F563DD6441C5A838397E008841D5.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Mathematics

7F40937672E54A10A30E2A86D359BCE4.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.
comments: For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?

671C034361F240E3B3CCB301FF4623A6.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

3725513BC2A14D9EAB00B7DBE32DB983.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

9AE1E060B5314707AF62342E0DE8FB5B.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

50378D73665844A2B6BC9D87BA6A42B2.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.
comments: For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

60BCE9DE894D4F9CAFCEFFB053856FC4.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
comments: For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.

E067DFA593344C43B88A9BAAE584CF48.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

C6DD3BECDC3C4362ABAA9356B8870457.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
comments: For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

8C74CC20517C4F308FCB3D1E06CDC248.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

6FE627B707124D459EC34B9B0E03126F.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

7992C7B4C9244063912D6597C2B0F181.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
comments: For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

A9C05EB1454445EDB8A15C78423487CB.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.
comments: For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.

5B2D8422ECE94E0CB81DF9F634ADDFA7.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

8557C8245CA149BBBE398CC889B37DA9.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
comments: For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

B85DE046D370498F9462926DE5C70A10.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

EA2A7A4F3C1346DA8D722DF7254ABEDB.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

7D26A976D6184A4FBC73E2D9D679B7F3.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
comments: For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

CED15175DAC54271A7D8483FADC816C3.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
comments: For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

94C252D469E24833A4E95D6D877F5F5C.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

9EA237A84A7744899B5BE81DF72F7927.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.
comments: For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9¾ inches long in the center of a door that is 27½ inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

6447FEC33B684A0A810EC46FEFEE185F.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

DF5A140AC1CC414DA1111030902667B0.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.
comments: For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

10124962963843318145211C14A5FF9E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

12622ED841A64703B6477C3CD76686CF.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

6DF62992A7CC4162B41F0FC1670A28BA.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

D41D9E9FC22A473EB6AC813ADE492DB3.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

6C5A37E19A3A45BD9995DE8438BC3A5C.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

E66545A1A25F442EB1C8CF37033EA7A0.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real world contexts.

D3B8379097524A68BAD8BB2951EBE3B7.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

FDBBCC5D9C4F4E52B0F0DE08B732EF4B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

90619441AA5148219012A5D2D11A44BB.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

1F81F5EAC13049FDA46A7F634283A96D.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

2B30B64F2F424DDEB5BC368D9AA136A9.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

D27465EE75A24B6081A6E4595F0669A6.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.
comments: For example, in the first round of a game, Maria scored 20 points. In the second round of the same game, she lost 20 points. What is her score at the end of the second round?

B2CF966CEEA54BD296961E85948FCAB1.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

32BC8A2B24A44D7DBDE8F52383E34FA9.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

AF6C7D16363244C5A5CB6C8EC505D5DF.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.
comments: Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

A55E6493124B4F62909C2D90AA707B60.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

comments: For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

76FA374AE22F464EA001FE348867CD60.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

F93EE71C124E4BE2B37A906E302414C1.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

09D7594FC44E4AE792EA42950A02DF2D.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

D893A925DE3D49D1A8165AD008D0F7CF.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.
comments: For example, if a person walks ½ mile in each ¼ hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2/1/4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.

3CC124453D734517A1C68D8942181291.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

8DFD93881AEE438180940A577DA650E5.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

322ADA56805A466781FCD3BC57BF55CE.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

5F533DA9DFB04F25B5C1C4ADB1667B04.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

6306B90F03D14EC7949FF7DD9E4CB8FB.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

F37262BAE52746CEBBC357C438578FA0.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

A8F1A244E67148598CCC47A50F473498.description: Draw (with technology, with ruler and protractor, as well as freehand) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

5D2F7CC12A9C47BEB8F4BC7D712B7EC3.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

204DF0DF4D3445A995CC07CE43A89229.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

ACD2DA8CDE2340E0AA31DAB49AC72DCF.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

27E6AFB6E2364019A3FDDDDE7D082F5C.description: Look for and make use of structure.

980C96589B704A928D54DD9D91349809.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

C2E2F4F91F8943B6AC222306F4FC0CC3.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Mathematics

05A65A3E156D4180AEE7582B71A2A79D.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

900A87133BAB4FBFBF734C56AB445F26.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.

082426242037470587283242600C747E.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

B8C448A683A74B8BB49545487E23A511.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

9DDE4B9250454150AD48534104DEB593.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

975A7D93027E4136940B8BFA06EF6708.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

7A322408A2934E71A992038770042303.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.
comments: Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

4A53EA42AC3A4BEAB51DA8EC0579008B.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

8DFA502C7EDF45DEB644B22F33320943.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

EE1310543B5246D0A5A7164A85A87ED4.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

35E54BFDAE504303AD27353268588050.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

DC09F85522B44CCDAC65E306AE6A06F1.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models (e.g., base ten blocks) or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

4B6EBC67A14E4FFDB4C0943FE21E0CD5.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

8AAFC87BCD6E423F99ACE26BC00BFC78.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

2540A4F9E33A4726B30CC016450753D4.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

ADF62C5D25044D4592A7577787CD6ED4.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

E137BC0F409846A39FDC5BBE4FE3CA24.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten."

03E716C163E24420AD264C794B8BA254.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

B5C30956F9644784B8DF32F3615979D5.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

233029F29650428C86957A6508B2ADE1.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

DFD6999A56EB42BC97A594F18F4F198C.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating to three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 5 = – 3, 6 + 6 = .

E1BDC69380724181981B27FD4F3038F6.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
comments: For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 – 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.

583B517F46754A3C93318791F2150A8B.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

F2452627CD084DB784BAA3F9940B3EAC.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

A685A9B700534977B756F1E4010AC201.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

86F8BD6ABCFF4E0787FDCAE086A338D2.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
comments: For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

FCB6BCD3DF214A92A10AB3790444FA6D.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.
comments: Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.) To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.) {Students need not use formal terms for these properties}

5746A089DAC243B69E6739DFDD22CEE8.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

991F0658946D4E479A7A3707D944E58E.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

13F804F986A64E43B73E9C9A063EE7FD.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

E22BBAE7CEC94264B7ADCF4C1E3F5612.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

0CEE66BB3F6A41DAB103F24F94DD5738.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

454277BEB4E9431C906ED40123957D83.description: Look for and make use of structure.

3B760B9B95B9479E99D08F3B9BE4E019.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

91667CC972E744F28EECBEF95C15A158.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Mathematics

BDB8A4081915462D888DBB950242685E.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, how much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share ½ lb of chocolate equally? How many 1/3-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?

D4490EBD171D43569768E6931D392FAD.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5), and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.

A238CDFAB63C4237BC15F63F6578FC5E.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4, and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.

81DA7165FB3E47BB8CBFFE37B44A969D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

FFFE01259AB342308D8F85F60078F4A9.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

D87C4B60E87042868B332520D5C1CE4F.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a)/(n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

40AED2252D2D48A4993B8DBE2BDF90D6.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

63A8275DE9B44A46889B3FD5AC8D46D3.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

1575C60C60A047D4AF5B48148F1AA3D9.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15. (In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.)

F6AC76E1621F4BACBB2CCA7F5455F1DF.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

28066AE6F653402E878B04850657FCC8.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, interpret ¾ as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that ¾ multiplied by 4 equals 3, and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size ¾. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

F6DB1AE8A13E41BBB8531FFA7F566E79.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

AE4423448FE04066AD5D47F691119ED2.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.
comments: For example, recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + ½ = 3/7, by observing that 3/7 < ½.

927C91BFC1094301926328E67E748EFE.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.
comments: For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.)

E9B8C7B0568548E69C6D41351B0A22E9.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

6C3CB3C0912349D684B66F23D8B5C471.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

F87EE6D25BB647A2A570531C05C16B58.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
comments: For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles.

3D7B7F88D0894022B77FBC32C06C08EF.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

5F55CE3C2B0D44378080DBFAD67153AA.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

D6657FF62C8944319CFE050941DC4904.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

62F338AF1A2C4DE88E0F9638D7362C1B.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

3F19C14A8CEB4623B56D7C44BA6EFCC0.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

E7808D71DDE040C1A5A27EDF30B952F1.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = B × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

B389A82CE8724DF594CBA4D402ED3CDD.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

642C1760322549479B12C6C0D4ACBEF3.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

0E8A17399C714E9E829C383E1B51C2BA.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and non-standard units.

CDC0563D25724B9997CAEB0DE3CB7A46.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

005D1EA930CB49DBAA7B10A9E665D974.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

09BE2215B3674314854B4103A493A71B.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

2A9BD6DC151346BEBE30251BE5D466C7.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

DABDF837EEFC440DB66F24553E2F346E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.

41E9EE73A7124FE4996A0ED1715CFB5A.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real world problems.

94E9C352F1B04A05953DB0BEF1483033.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

8BBAFDD7609C482CB821C751FD79374D.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

E43F9B64A7814CB5B2BF77C711D5CC3E.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

A9E524F267B441D1A91AC9492C58F8F0.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

C6EF46EE0BA24333AC60CED13FE09EA3.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

D7612295818343DEBAD672490B5752A3.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

F71FE01EC2B14E85A398225B0F65155C.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

6CDC34652D5146F89B56A62EF4BD8190.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).

F0FDE7F8D7EE465F9B588B59E4207727.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

ED51FD6EA851470FA28BB4A2E10E7908.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

EFC9B7AD956A4D2A9EC35D2D7BB2BDC9.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

E7ECB4DAC67F4D55875C10F9D1CA96EE.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

63E9840C7E1C4C07B17F4D7531955030.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.

B63CB84C9B424AE3A07388E850D5BC50.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
comments: For example, express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.

6B014F23527746E2AC21D3637B278DF7.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

1C58489B1C634A4B90F085234142D94F.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

DD6C387F7476433D8018559FC3D56B35.description: Look for and make use of structure.

309D9001690447B4847AE80D25EC2549.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

8C24E7F4FBE040BB96732F228AB38997.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Mathematics

769485D46A884FDF9C3B47572D3350E5.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and desc`ibe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

FD69CF4C9D9544FB9BB3E23B1EC38439.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

D48A8466245C452A8416CB4D46F25378.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

0FCE528024B645F7BD344448988D59AF.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

F4DA992EE0AD4FD0A2F2DDC55F2B0EFB.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

617D42AD3F974DB8B065AD4F1945BFE1.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

65913896BB604D208907F760BDB72FC4.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
comments: Example: If you have 2 dimes and 3 pennies, how many cents do you have?

1491300DA2B646E7ADA0391C44A48470.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

12A85F5414DC413C908565454C517A76.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

233774D9722B46838D41CA24E8212F7B.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

CC24071AB6F54598AE2C70FE38594994.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

C07A18D71AAB45DE9454EAE88FA60D99.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

4CF07CF790C8406BAA81FC9046777092.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

2B1E418D69BC46A7A2344B95B532EBD6.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

E37C9E1B8A99414AAE450717D82719D5.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

5B9B753597DE46688D59442BC5C94BD3.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

E10DEB510FAB4876A368A5DC4A1FB65F.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.

CEE150169EE94F4FA9CDA7B181036F9F.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900.

34EB9836115E4A31994D73765EE16D76.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

DC3894444095436AACD6FF94B92ACC4A.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

75D92191646E44438C6F4FE445DBD8B0.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

E7FC2A89FDA449C09492CB30800203AB.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

13CF84A7EB6947CF94D6AA509F9CA9B7.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

CD70856FC82B4E5B9B9AD60571FA3015.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

4C4484525DE847E1A7C0863D4DB8D3DA.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

77768C373F514E00B09B13EE265C4377.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a "hundred."

E96E36F78B824B369D50784F561166B7.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:

2CF2096BACC24A5FBECF4C3111C4254A.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

BE730723163340ABB0A1CE7F4BD33030.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

065EF51A833C4BD48A11343340AAED78.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

338631FB50544F86813370B4C29B2BA6.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

7DCF8FB678014840A03F34CDE2CF1E66.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

6573FAA4D44F426EBEE075E233EBF888.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

881FDA1BCAA94CE9B083C46491EC689F.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

545701A0B7BF42DEAADE71E4F59D0B9E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

9D0F616351944E82AF554DAD0763EDA1.description: Look for and make use of structure.

618EFC8A44294961A10F90CCB9D7DC90.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

A3114E4978674F09A98A43E40108F9E8.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Mathematics

C4105E2D019C4C0D8A8F91981456851C.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

6FA57AFA278546AB9D1C9A3C9A73254F.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

3BAF73C50F2D40ACAE8714E66DEDD882.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.
comments: For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.

EEDBFDD54C9047FDA05644DD7221B818.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.
comments: For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast food restaurant.

6E963FC8ECA34095A19BF72644F3C554.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

5E155E915E6E48E08622841B4B1F68DA.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions

comments: For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

9E87C8AA0E344269BAB31EF4A6F1314C.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

3DB4DBA72E934BEF8692B8B11EDD67FE.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems

22A1F6D8122448D3870E2D79C5E90CFD.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

E1A94512CDC14D40B2D506680ADA3598.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

B964C02ED4E14B4EB958F9FE7990FA33.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.

04EECE7ADF4441D9A2409BF4528FF682.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

422E1AC36C404F068A3D5CBE6343E4F4.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

7AAAE3C9E4B344DBBC182096A814FC58.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

C71FDB0CE52D429496C9D8E7BC6A507F.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

B39E7F8D3225411D8418B25FAA91D3B8.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments

E1734FDF749E4050A5556124FF88A2AC.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

37D5E94D13FA49FFAD8B76EF2BB0E75C.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals, including with the use of technology.

FC92E2E9EE6C464E9C17306E3161E60C.description: Fit a function to the data (including with the use of technology); use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and exponential models.

2DC5E110FE254320A6A7A7060BCE2EF3.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. E28FDAC190974F0D9A8BB9A199E6B2BD.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

1017BF271CC049E7AE5514E4B2A00726.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

EE8B2EBB661A4237AA2439E495134618.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable

57850F3B26EF4756AEFD13F277AF2678.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

C6896DD08792448CB5A69690950CF374.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

355B25D068F944AD82AB383D59C0BC9C.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations

D436460333F945998294E78F5ABFF40C.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

C50A7BAABAE64C31AF99E5EC3594C7C3.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

C53DD1A27E3547A58803390E35031FD3.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems

C228272DF64E4DC58D876DE7F42AE80E.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

F97F9F27D7524F079B4245D1B816651A.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

752EE48D46D74D54905A5B1B94243203.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

F96FA483CB9944228DFE860276ABB15A.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

9200C8B2812B46FB9C60BA83B5C602B8.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically

CC6158D77FBC4B9DB079D33A7D1538CD.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

7FDAA19117D54CA08CB78C87AA1AEA58.description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

F748EF8DEA544B6095AC0AEE46E362F8.description: (+) Derive the formula A = ½ ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

A9E850BA7104472C8A0A219DAD6CB5A6.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

2997AE4A05BD418686E9D4383750D71D.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

E8ABBD444594418285DE157124E40999.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

FB3BA1102CE64ABBB89A5CC9B0778C16.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles

DBA2D098C09D48BBB0F4C8DF8180653A.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. D852B792C1154C40AD0F9FBBC8A69EF7.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

9F61B14D96A045D59217899B9A4DB9B2.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. 111CCC331B5A4A2FA87B6F3B0534E236.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

14A022A4FE224677A22AD91AC771E725.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

AFF0CCDD13754D50871F80B05862377A.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

1DABAB0ABBCC42348117574D25C49F0C.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
