52C449A6D5DA458EBCB2F1A92AE19155.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

3E783D5F6FCD4B6FAD0DF2A39A27694E.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

35DB6463EACC4F1093B01032C81E7E63.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

221490BA1520435A9EA3FE7C20438A61.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

66C530967CDF41B294F7DC35C3F384F7.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

97DF79153ABE47D39F0079EE30CFCCB6.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

ADBEFEFA12FC4D32937C76DE183EC6FF.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

2AAC906391C84BCDBA2BCF734527E470.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

42B1DF30CB51454DBA559E52453A9A59.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

18C5235B4F1A49BE927D92C6630394F0.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

48CDF50FD7E142839367FC7FFE083C87.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

128E72DB7C8443B8A3D0EDB2DA78D948.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

B6F698EE37684C89B6A1719056CCD518.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

AE2ADB71C883494A95D7F3B16C5A61FD.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

30C9915B6905497787908174766DF106.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

A34BE3C1CD4F469098CC957465C15000.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

7B534AD66AAA45CFA9EA4729550CD7A8.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

7AC438311C7146C294EAF40C1E1DEB3C.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

DB507FC7439B463089BC8344E9743B79.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

8F757EFEC4474F1ABAA1F509B701A955.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

2DB86FBE20C9483A8601794FDB79BBC2.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
comments: For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

F8DA1367EEE54C3A925449C8CA6F17C0.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
comments: For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

A6FF2047BD9A4BF99B2084A5D74919B4.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

41163AF5A0CC4D5BA67F945506915F3E.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

9CF3490D8539487DA6DDEBCA4733CFB7.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

AA416B936AC34125A1DCD675F725F601.description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

AFC89DC072954DDEB25E095290ED4956.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

C1D893DD1A1C4BD59C2A15CBC8B82A60.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.

CD68229D77314E1B9BECB404BEB6CBA2.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the difference of two squares; the sum and difference of two cubes; the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

59A15D095EB14C279B126A539DF1B5E8.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems

02B3087A4FBC4A51813DDE9F11F275B5.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

72CD4B4434004F4395CB674308EEB47D.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

BDD28EC8C7EB4797A4A36EB49D58D8D7.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials

32B53F7DD445404A8B65B2C9489E51F1.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

F57592C159394495B2D5A5F86FC48E56.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

2B218646D6D84F559BF9CE160B2CF29F.description: Derive and/or explain the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.
comments: For example, calculate mortgage payments.

4D0AE469136149119EF1BDA88F177DBA.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈1.01212t to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

88A4DBDEACFF4FA197003DCA084ADBF7.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

CD2FBADE5BB94A04BE62703CC634D115.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

AAF90667A411479D962D0A8ADD7D26F0.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

89BC7305E9CE41C4A16533EED1421A79.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

8C89E172BB7B43B6BD907FDCF7DB2768.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).

E4684111D34E4E4FA0D2744DC4D13CBE.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1+r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P

3984D3D9C04C428F97DA005537503AD0.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

0A4000CFF06B47D7B086FECC818ED552.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

B453192FC24E4DD2BCABBB160083E970.description: (+)Work with 2 × 2 matrices as a transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

019E51495FE84D1A949AF3612573C924.description: (+)Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

DA8846926D054F2EB89C50AE4CD25024.description: (+)Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

90E579BB1E274991A8A9305EB2B0B76A.description: (+)Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

4EF7EB98CAD64A2AA668455C664206BB.description: (+)Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

B07C911F00B048BB977D2C5EAEBA2B99.description: (+)Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.

3FC04982F8714D12AE4B20B6E90F8C61.description: (+)Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

F0154B694C0F40A0BDDC797A226398AD.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

71508816417A4B7D8E026E51E43C27F1.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

46550CD08B674E70863CEE391DE91D47.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub>, cv<sub>y</sub>).

C235A2E131CC47519992C49A63A80EBD.description: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.

5D642B480A3D454B964323BAD07F3211.description: Understand vector subtraction v – w as v + (–w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

3B1627ACAF2042989DA2D8C2C6B91F03.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

C1FB6061D1924ABC89941BB08CA496AA.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

39D5A9ECA9A042849BF174C5DBF895F2.description: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

A60D1F35330C40E4BE4D610806140BDD.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

899D74EFD16A48F185D55E5FBBE549D2.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

EEA88FA84EB5475897C78FB6EE1975CA.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

7C5FAB3BA2A047CCACECF2065F8F6EB4.description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

6BFC5E0BC1FC42D6862B198AC40AB7D2.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
comments: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).

BDE9F9D697E945438602A613DED9CA5E.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

2FF36E1C305341139D055925825191A7.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

943D340880674FCB86FAC9C98D584F0B.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

AC06BB6C21D34B218215C0F2F14D58C4.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.
comments: For example, (‐1 + √3i)³ = 8 because (‐1+ √3i) has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

7A7A0EDA58B041C08F9693923AF886A9.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

B509DD13757042979A829A9FA83BC5C9.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

16FC68E9BCE54DD0A5B3C308A171F78E.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

F5A8D6D304094455A7F634FC872D31AB.description: Use the relation i² = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

6F1707E9648C4A6191C2D834189C7FA1.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = –1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

BA1E1B4117C34555ADC9C93AF703BAE7.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

28BD343F128A497385333CBEDCF47B1C.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

B2385D06E10746FFBF57F7F1CDA8868C.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

D467511ACA054A5691DD9524D115B502.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

94D32738BE5B42BCBC765DA58702824E.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

0C138D5B35FE4AF4B4A8900DBD545BF7.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

95BE422B4CC646829223C4ED3409B05F.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

635A67A86CBA416DAADC78C563302510.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

43834CDEA8524DCAB12FE9F889B160CB.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
comments: For example, we define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.

CF14A41C9286431EBDBAABF720306E97.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

C9CDDB9C3E4B4E26A07F9BE3384AE3D1.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

E4D9B1A1033D47869D1ECB2AC6EAC7C8.description: Look for and make use of structure.

01BB6D5967DD49769FE6E6ECEEDED0D8.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

B88B09D0B2304B47A43871730EA3D24C.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Mathematics

801B763D0A674ADFB74D11FECCF0B535.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

70F192FCA43D437FB29898CCDC46977C.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

B356CF22C17F4449AE8CB4C4DD014AAC.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

A2DCF78D2C4D4B4B8D6F2C37A8FB382B.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.
comments: For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.

60E70BDF20454E1799B6D8F2783DDAA4.description: Compare properties (e.g. rate of change, intercepts, domain and range) of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

BDBC63D0AE8949A1BCB4853E5E3525C3.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

C754DF81080D4F4C945BD2FC3AF7B659.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.
comments: For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

D4648DB6F2DC4922994A4E73267460AE.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.
comments: For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

A9FDFF387F6144D8A7A257E7D7060F98.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit (e.g. line of best fit) by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

3ABC61028B214232AB45C893A3CCDF62.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

0A1C3AB4F8CC44189405D1FD2DBCCB29.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

281C7713EC284B1B806F15717B74F607.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
comments: For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

D0F44CAA5DF743DAAF26B69F5D0CCF0D.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
comments: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

63EF2CDBA1D04014B944EA69DE789B23.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

B17058193E0849828DACA850A62541CD.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

83E9846E5C0A41B79B480D0DA94F7975.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

CE2DE675CF6B49D78736893BD87BBFE1.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

D6877D12E0544DF0A8C949B9FE0B48E9.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

B21A45222CAA4CAF89D08E03F73F1D9B.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

AFD6E6791D22488396855238B1DA99E4.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

BDF335F42F34454CBFF695E3FCF43CC5.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
comments: For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.

251F8DB699064F82B28279EAF8E29107.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

F3452EE195D94159AEF23CC41FC8B32F.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

C957363BF7C34A62BC879C88BCA4C2C1.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
comments: For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

94259BE16FF44D35B777F038F113A0BE.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

461B0FBD9BA748789D37F2B24D800595.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
comments: For example, 3² × 3<sup>–5</sup> = 3<sup>–3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27.

B41185BE6C964D478452D14F9E22328C.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

AFF6B16741BA404D9026F419C8C863C2.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).
comments: For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

5A6F3E946303412FA67F4742E9E78078.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

78702677FEA64AFDA5924628B7B48BDB.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

F1487229AA434B8EB8D40CEC37D9B9B7.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

27EF998144DE41478744DC505D706F25.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

F8EF856DCEA5424398EE4D85C4E6C843.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

FB9FE080552B4E2BA893632967CB8DCA.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

B485F6A68C6B4810A3EC0980B7DE26EC.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

8E8E85F21BC54EF29833095C453AE7DB.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

6E6455FB7469413FAF4C3124C6B93017.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
comments: For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

35BE12E0C8724F3E81D4573C4BBCD101.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

85C263384073442CB1232F475FF6D636.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

9DC4B529182A4ACBB152C95DB886ADF4.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

E0C711F6489F4071AD579640953C2EB3.description: Parallel lines are transformed to parallel lines.

5C59041E0303438F9669522ECAF5945C.description: Angles are transformed to angles of the same measure.

91221A899F0444738A930DBF8FC152CE.description: Lines are transformed to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

37D3271EE0E440C5B92D6CCE6C980B91.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

5CA8004E72D74D8AA33BD377D99AEC28.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

0C3FD95FBDCF469FB1240794676E636C.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

CA9FFAE6B2E54350B8D5C368E79E46AD.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BF5CDA4F2B8743E3871C5A45FC537C8B.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

2B41B5576095469389A81383ED87F82D.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for English Language Arts

1CA75661C4AD4B2B915AAACCE0EE5617.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, metacognition/self correction, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

0AD3175C6A364F69B5E9A7952D43CB22.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for English Language Arts

D7D3CB0B0F094D049FAD76F72B33CF8C.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

E66F4856679143F7B03DF08DE8D6E0A8.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.

A26DE86449F44101940B95DA31F5DC7D.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

5A4AC88D1A38478DB1D437735794A229.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

07B7BDD3ACEC4A9F9ED05A95C481F43A.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D00B13B73A0E4F34A3D36A8DAFAB04A2.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

A2A10486FF294866838830B7758E5D60.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

450E513722CF443098360E977EA89DF6.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4D858376C4E948EBB8C6935076AAE085.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

8E84B9F916C0405FB0F103F514D4A3FD.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

A6B14FAB55234BF4B7D33E71D79CAC52.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

C8F8B8793C6E4EE9992B0AC8DD3D51E2.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

D5AF65A585B14E6C84A3961017728FB4.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

1208216582C34BF0B4A6129465748851.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

5B983C47F69A4F6785AE9FD61B7D5F26.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).

79ECB61AFA414B7ABE54CC262F9A0530.description: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.

85706F2C83A94E6996DDCFFAE763BB70.description: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.

058EAD83A35E419E804E264497160ECD.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1768A4F944DE414199F7EC9EAD7D3B1D.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

2792ED3129FA4E65AB16DF658B6509CC.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

FDDD9EBD4E8A461EBC43634E0FADDCB2.description: Form and use the perfect (e.g., I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.

EE0A7AB6832644E2A131BCD8C262B798.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.

5CE3F07495F547299A2F51C0DA729A1D.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D8072A23230348C2A4E3FCF2C1BD0B04.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

95A46FAB9A314AD9842E191D0CB7F818.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

2F0F981A17FB4F6592A077B2BCC66E71.description: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

693F1F4EDFA34FD19F318D37B3F80B48.description: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.

15F0CBA928A14BA18D3AAEC16090BD8D.description: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and orally).

5E7407305E714DD49A02B50A55324869.description: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.

9BD22FB4BC1141868835E927F37D8635.description: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.

4BA1ADFAAD9742BA9D1BE814838685DF.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

5A6E9A16FC3C42EC87FB45B81BC8E770.description: Explicitly draw on previously read text or material and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

FF30E32B1F3447AAB78F5A5FEA1F05E5.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

1ABB0C1B57AC4467A5E176EA393CD0DE.description: Progress Indicators for Speaking and Listening

07C7C4BC25974CE3B83BC42CDDBE3FA1.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, metacognition/self-correction and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

A3AF62F45680423FBD91C158C403BEEB.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point[s]").

D72A0401353B42FD9FA180826044305C.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or a drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., how characters interact]").

EC6618DE9CA94F81AAE269BEE84CB897.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

FED250B7456E474CAB54262C4126D057.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.

587ECC3D9F51478EA7F841BA6925163A.description: Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of different perspectives of a topic.

3EDEC3780A5340A8BCDAB22B4676F5E4.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

F8384D8A4602490D9AEE0B98398664F8.description: With some guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of two pages in a single sitting.

3FB24E25ECC644BB8FB5E4E66C63A01A.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

2BE6300EBBCC4BA390DDF3953D621446.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

8F04435632634491A04A580972740225.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

F8E7C35C52874CE99163FCCF9DD29AE0.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

69A39AA9C1A24028B35ED41A05832A3B.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.

6AD43CED5E3B4EC0AC431A647F4201E6.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

A89C14A64D39468FA663079508B539C7.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

7B578CE1EE214E8FAFE2B8CFA05FA076.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

0FEFB58D72FC4768B840FE187FFE7A51.description: Provide a conclusion related to the information of explanation presented.

C9D88AD4F4DF4C3D8C127D9EC076B3BD.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

A75D58B676B34EECADBA3B47AD322B27.description: Link ideas within paragraphs and sections of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).

105E9A6FB92B443C85E7CEAA21D50E28.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

E60E8642E9A94C8CBE7B9916EB872D10.description: Introduce a topic clearly to provide a focus and group related information logically; include text features such as headings, illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

C04023D57BF3458AA55D5737DFE0BB86.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

873365F22C0244BCB5FAB56A88601E57.description: Provide a conclusion related to the opinion presented.

694F6450DA974707A3D704D8761B9C7B.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).

FA3DB4EF93CD444AB5E6B6A8D1501FFC.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details from text(s), quote directly from text when appropriate.

1EB9C4AB3BEE48379608001C01DEAACE.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.

48F3BF3D25AA41AA853E5C1531009F42.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

E00BA6CBBDE64790A9B2151DB5FADD2C.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

8460501047F246A7A5272D1B49794125.description: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

72CCAB2BF4384AC69B7D56C74284F2EC.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

E0364B0607654752AE40DA8452EACA0B.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

906F97E9B22F4286A4BE17C2D71C2A70.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

F9F19DA922CE4C51BED218AA827757C9.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding words.

6E6F21D4F18A427688E08EB7F0C96511.description: Progress Indicators for Reading Foundation Skills

5422B552F7E3468E8D3C26CAA4047939.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at grade level text-complexity or above, with scaffolding as needed.

9229410F1553471085707E6049AAD02B.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

C31DA992CD5A4D839EA13B38C53591BD.description: Integrate and reflect on (e.g. practical knowledge, historical/cultural context, and background knowledge) information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

C07C2294F28343DF933CBEB8AA0AD70F.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

D8852D1839A54FD6862A65427C9A9086.description: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.

E8F50F3851B84BCFA08D4DF0D4CFDEF2.description: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.

082144A76334473EA5157E076A83D3EC.description: Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.

AF1F3ADA12904A30A52DFFAFE267EFAD.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.

F41BAB1404BC4089A49A1445EDAE850B.description: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.

772F28F613E6490BB100E0E5EBD21CCD.description: Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.

65084F447B6843F787E74C0AC824FFEA.description: Quote accurately from a text and make relevant connections when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

3868B858FEF349A9A3716145BDF840CA.description: Progress Indicators for Reading Informational Text

14D0D44AE14E4FD4AF7DC8B5E85ACE47.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems at grade level text-complexity or above, with scaffolding as needed.

265A9E24AFEC46CFBFE8A13C4C758A43.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

16764D9C7BE845D888FBF5795D4A4444.description: Compare, contrast and reflect on (e.g. practical knowledge, historical/cultural context, and background knowledge) the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

B6377919CE694CC8AEB56928848CFF03.description: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

8961EF6DA200484D9D16DAC9C5B488CC.description: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.

4968B366DE35450C93A5A4070CD6169F.description: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

2BE02F4A533E447F9BA44901EC2729F8.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.

ABCC8080B78D47D1AE9B287CAA01787A.description: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).

ABA13BE3B4F34DC6ABEA681E6EA4D848.description: Determine the key details in a story, drama or poem to identify the theme and to summarize the text.

3C6F6EAC762B45298A2A1013522AD0CD.description: Quote accurately from a text, and make relevant connections when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

76D85684EF9D4581A915BF47AA7AA77F.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

C6C5130F00534866B6DC004CD8D379D8.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

45222545CF00437DA4867EBDFADD19DC.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

E973CBF0791A4C5884713A0D437AA9DD.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4E1CF0D7C8F04736862AC56C60D50372.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

E7A331E24D614DCD90334D201624A77C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

AE9BD512DFE24A52AB38564C8033B2AC.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

31D92F08261849BEB1F93F3282739285.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

FE51DCC68DF34F0F8AC33B2526898D5D.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D457415C8329437A8D67771E6F27362B.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

8C252717699042A989CA7814D70AB2C8.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

C35655A3FBCC48159BD9E9D29A4E4BC5.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

C5DB71821BA5460FB252FD212866757C.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

AC6431DA02AD44AEB30B31120FF3086F.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1482B476EE624DDAAAC78D510CDDF1B7.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

6408764594344E6EA00A77B7407B3FBF.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects, utilizing an inquiry-based research process, based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

891FD953BA6A45D7822DF7A38615C2BE.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DEFBAF14E3DC4C698A1F7456FA7D2FF6.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

3C6A5EAF99E94EBAB300DB8CFE3EBF27.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

4651E81D0FFB4A9997176F7B133666A6.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

FD806605AA894532BC76386EE76734B7.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

F34AE14410DB4FCAB7FCFDBBE9AC2084.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

13E94A3B6FF14D09B3C71EA1B62400D4.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

CF56FDDE87564DED9CD95E3DF075797A.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently with scaffolding as needed.

52940AAC78F04EAF95F80C9C2C3AF26C.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

C8CD1E56990A489093BCD27F8579BF90.description: Analyze and reflect on how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

3C21D61969BB41CB86952D562E9C83AC.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

9DA04AFF901C4BCFAD90DE75F1B4FD17.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

967A0D6493CC4F45BF0A77FA82037F96.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

5D4310ABD4F146778C4EF3A1FAE2CE23.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

271912FDD1924B02866100BC8BA80D64.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

9F96ACA2523440F4B44D163D1427812C.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

927E79A936D24860B3D2AEC3476F226F.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

4F1E0A2B26C44ADB8697C80DA94050D4.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences and relevant connections from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for English Language Arts

3895ABA499DE4A96AA571271903BB785.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

3212A2FD4DAF42A4A6E30A9A9679F42F.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

BB88DA2256DE42E09275B6DBF7865319.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

3AAA8D811716464AB7CD7E12146B576C.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

698BB4CD16FA4381BA23AFF8C2DBDB7B.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

4AE587B87D6E4DCE97123CAC6A6BB0BF.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

BF7BCC242B3D462BA300C82AE4797BEE.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

2732875A42A2466F846671EE65D171EE.description: Use frequently occurring affixes and inflection (e.g., -ed, -s, -ing, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of a word.

7609A1E6282242DC8DA6A9F17805BBED.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

39F64861CECC40E1B0A90D9D4859712D.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

6666017D7FB2440EA7D228DAA22BBFD8.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

BA4A165096D846268FE37663400B1C75.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

7689ADDAA5E84E0FAF587CC7C898EC46.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

F1FB1F044BF847CFB060FFDBA6D00A77.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

1FE8E8E4EE554403AC84C861EEB38D64.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

AA7886588F164FAAA6F101D019192594.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

0C1AA44E8DF140CB8C5A8D34A60AD70C.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

95F70D8DFDCC483E8CE0226D759DF5E4.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

8EE7CF0A44194E50BB60813CD861E7FF.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

EF6BEC108B85430E95922BF5ACCDA959.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their, anyone, everything).

F4723366942D465E92F70A6A2D1B57D5.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

C74E049E32BD4397B6653C690628DBEC.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

15DE886EBD0C416989C78A820DDA9807.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

094D5FC1831547EC8A9907B39C184295.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

64CE2099595C48DA83F64A0F282A09CB.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

5614A52465A340678DEF6F9B1BDD13E7.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

94D3343CDD7C444F923340B4CF4626F8.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

E7CAC113A9F849F3AE8348D8CEF6A217.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.

2FB907AEBA1B4795983C37DF236B0011.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

22F20C7B333D4370BBD453818C916ACA.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

29AD3235AFD841B6A4BA7573E20E9D2A.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

EE535B72D35B4DEE9D1DD381B65D21B0.description: Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

24C9C614CAC74F1D8840A8084EB9B4DB.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

71B55AB1BCB140888BCA9E77F2BD500A.description: Progress Indicators for Speaking and Listening

5498AE297FEE42EFB4E8F096B1C65E7B.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

B77837C86BEB4C06A936826A0CB4D0C9.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

034DF62B848A41489E89E62CF5363B20.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

24DBF78BEAFC4AFCB067AFB32F9D224B.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

7AFF3382399A4AD687C687C9A39F4D60.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and self-reflection, and add details to strengthen writing and ideas as needed.

D0363D53C3A04C30B70BDDC716799052.description: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

7E2F56DB7A9B41F88696F01AA12BC981.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

8688C5789C25440EA31EFFF1C4C74651.description: Evaluate various perspectives for actions or events; determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

CA8F185017DD4954B445191B286749C5.description: Determine the theme, central ideas, information and/or perspective(s) presented in a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of how key events, ideas and/or author's perspective(s) develop over the course of the text.

38D06F99CC9E406D8B4971534B7BBD52.description: Accurately cite strong and thorough textual evidence, (e.g., via discussion, written response, etc.), to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to develop an understanding of the text as a whole.

BFDCDD6441DA4E0F95203ABA64D04DD4.description: Progress Indicators Reading History and Social Studies

77DCAA376CB945688F1DD29CEC30143D.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7EC01FBECAB4424791F81B05DE39F7CF.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

0692B30C51AB4453880042C910FD70B6.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole, paradox) in context and analyze their role in the text.

92E722F6398E4CA5BFAE39A601D550A9.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

715360A1AFD04A399A61F80E665FE7E2.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

B989A8CBA48942119B58CE3166D24213.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

B787722CC5874388ABC9566E6ECF830F.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

0F5D2B18AE08463190933E585732E545.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

CE92F7531D02429D94DD0E1037E39D06.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 11–12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

2A4DD24FD0B3403FBA09CCE4854E16A9.description: Vary syntax for effect, apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts.

5EDC35DCAE434E0CBB3D8E5C1EBDFE23.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

D8BD30EB290D4842BE4C5D0DFC4474D5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

C8635EFC1F654986AE6563ED694F6913.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested.

BA3196F73E0E424EA603D09D358A39A8.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7A27B33B71304405B7BF5DBD7F85BBDA.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating a command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4AE44DDE0A4240AE828CC0FF6DEE41C0.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

FBFD92B9E1974AC99F22837A5857796E.description: Present information, findings and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically. The content, organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4FE38EDAE40A4A37A7BF32500480A24A.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

39791F9684E54F1299E899D54642194A.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, qualitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

7452C767F7204C209643976249D9ED4F.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

32ABF952A311426594298EE59CAEEA2F.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

47162DA00ED1438181C685B7C28086C8.description: Collaborate with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and assessments (e.g. student developed rubrics), and establish individual roles as needed.

DF008AB45BF04F21A235E46469148787.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well reasoned exchange of ideas.

C747F960E7E8405488C7EB2ED7D233E6.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with peers on grades 11–12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

1408A18308B247B6897D9B86C1FD855F.description: Progress Indicators for Speaking and Listening

85E9BCA8699949D4B42CD4D82DC591A2.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

B50F97CF22DC424E94684EBFF02A692E.description: Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy [e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses]").

43E654C7A8EB4D1A8A3CA3ACC8519BF5.description: Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

E8F7F8D3763849E9B7860CAB9A4A8D3A.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

B6E8273CBC88433597538593BF7CE116.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation. (MLA or APA Style Manuals).

CB71B236846046258F04B0BCDBC356D0.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4A08B93476314152B8E692C669DDE8A2.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

5CABBCD4786440BCAFBCE448415B3010.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, share, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

D8B8408B374B47B9AF8704C29610689E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, trying a new approach, or consulting a style manual (such as MLA or APA Style), focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

ADD0EF0DAF5A432E92F6FF0652C09F35.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9AD487CF35024AFE962CD1A68F045960.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

ACA65149AB8D486AAEBF743D29442F33.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

76BD66E31C3540C2AD616BD605A7CF1D.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

67B57951218740B2B5A4A5A241BD0CF9.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

13B47C40C1DF4AB2A770D8EE1C3E608D.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

0FDCF92C3B454C7887DF9618DF44A05D.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

2F3D221EEC0A4D0CA093B81FDA4B6663.description: Provide a concluding paragraph or section that supports the argument presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

848C37CE80CB45CEB93C4CB783ADD08A.description: Establish and maintain a style and tone appropriate to the audience and purpose (e.g. formal and objective for academic writing) while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

24A3D164BC404705B094EF2829D41D22.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

E3B251EE9DDC45149466F86F9AD1FD49.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

D29A2CDBC11E4EB8B2AA90E9B7EA02D6.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

589B41CC067C4583A115D7C7896DFF04.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

8DFA2A4D0A7843518B71DA2A6CE5220C.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

39E292C7F39A4944A2ECE510E0278E1A.description: Provide a concluding paragraph or section that supports the argument presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

5303FA3C77B74BDA889AAB14E04F61EC.description: Establish and maintain a style and tone appropriate to the audience and purpose (e.g. formal and objective for academic writing) while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

0584D30AF15340F584AA15E57AFC8B13.description: Use transitions (e.g. words, phrases, clauses) to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

69D5C64C44A64953B466A8DE6C48EFBD.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims avoiding common logical fallacies and using sound reasoning and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

EDAAB70869D748E9A5F7C0CB8D570496.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

3C4FB2BA6840409393E942A01FA7934F.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

837AEA39F2C2455D84879F075BF8D2C8.description: By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at grade level text-complexity or above with scaffolding as needed.

633CB09B53F347E39975114381DB414D.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

B718C37278E7471EAA1EC67119F11B4C.description: Analyze and reflect on (e.g. practical knowledge, historical/cultural context, and background knowledge) documents of historical and literary significance for their themes, purposes and rhetorical features, including primary source documents relevant to U.S. and/or global history.

E162AC5BA2D34CC1962FFAAFA83C5F5C.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

338EB3DCBA1943E5858B9E0A3CBD735B.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

A3FADF347FFB4694B7D73AD33335CB4F.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

2EB122A9A12E4F8D9B7388407A426041.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text, and analyze their development and how they interact to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

FB19CFB0A0CC42FB98DBEB0807139810.description: Accurately cite strong and thorough textual evidence, (e.g., via discussion, written response, etc.), to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferentially, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

00B347F8836D489FACE94212F16C84CE.description: Progress Indicators for Reading Informational Text

533719CECFE54DD7AEC51FDC170B3EF1.description: By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems at grade level text-complexity or above with scaffolding as needed.

75679C381C9245B1A2EECE624CCB324D.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

778F571F3D9A4D76A36EE25BD2FCE159.description: Demonstrate knowledge of and reflect on (e.g. practical knowledge, historical/cultural context, and background knowledge) eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

9A57490A2852448595FAAB05BAB0C1C1.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (e.g., Shakespeare and other authors.)

2BEE9BE9C3F94F8BAD258AE2DEBC2011.description: Analyze a case in which grasping a point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

9F9D8CB4389742EA958618AD1B6739BD.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

3B22B7E419C641CD97907BF7D5B93572.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (e.g., Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

8AC011D6D4CF4DBD9D40C8A08656DEC4.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

5990F35EAD42400E95BD1F5597202A1F.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

C0ABF8CD8A654DDE896820D04B0674FC.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence and make relevant connections to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

1FFD796362DA480595648D55A0906B8D.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

05804353AFC64BFDBFD084C1F6603C3A.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

87FEEC6EFD1D4DA7BEB647F02420A950.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

8D72AEB57B8B4BA5BC8E575021B6B804.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

1458274F3C24405695AB9D1BE4C439F1.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D574A57C6DEC4115B3A958C8071F790A.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

29F8C2BF2E644EFBB3DA3D48C6722A9E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

A429289555924441A37E9045D8EA6040.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

0446FB29AECE4CE79B07A4E5A92501A6.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

3A4D98FEE8E7446F90853B4414F459C2.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

62B085729A3E48ED9D8E2426A59BA949.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

20FDAF3CAA154C1CBD07F211B568485F.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

8CB48414B5CF4AAAB610451CF3087AAA.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
