ABD62DA48B6C40609745295D4635A71A.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

E61FB07B70174F2AB9192D8DEA6802A5.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects, utilizing an inquiry-based research process, based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

2378115886AE4D92AED69AB2879A8A7D.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

4A788193949B4189ABA928DB280912C0.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

D44E4EF5C94B4273868F1C5A7A3A6965.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

2AD9ABF3117E4EF9894F18180BC8A89C.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences and relevant connections from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for English Language Arts

88EF710FE68F4746ACFDCE87A6D7103E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

C7BC1091D3AD42AB883BB161DCDE9072.description: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

3CF475BF60B14B6D8895493701870CDE.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D857890149D44102AEE917F9FEA646E8.description: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.

9E22EAEAEEAC408D9C38C646DA294669.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

76CEB99755ED449F9F05787990940476.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

3EE990081ED740BC8CA9B0A0E6AFF778.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

0EE4E108E4224BB498BD77ACF38F8291.description: With guidance and support from adults, strengthen writing through response and self-reflection using questions and suggestions from peers (e.g., adding details).

55A346784D9A45A4B0ADAF002B46698B.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.

75019E63E0DC40AFA663DE3A1FCD24C7.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is…).

5DB01C7FB73D46208829897DCF55C13C.description: Read emergent-readers with purpose and understanding.

35DA6F3C03074860A11D24AF47DB3F36.description: Read emergent text with one-to-one correspondence to develop fluency and comprehension skills.

41C49DDF682C47998B7229DE374DA8E5.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ (e.g., nap and tap; cat and cot).

511D9D78E8714EA4A961A7AAF724F8FD.description: Read high-frequency and sight words with automaticity.

0634F7138B00468680BED270AA37B1B0.description: Associate the long and short sounds with the common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

9B552C5C33CD47BE88073784CD2CC94A.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing many of the most frequently used sounds of each consonant.

3DF2D136F94C4F94AA2CA4D6E3AEB032.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding words.

42F760DB04B14BCC94D6964767CA1CE7.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

0FC1CC5AE63E46C89AE501B19280D71B.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel-consonant, or CVC) words.

4DB49EC2FDD04013AFA7627405070AC9.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

9C5DF7BAD4334412B109B6F1D7C25030.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

3B92E0FFFF38480BBBC121D68D74CAC1.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

19B7864E9AAF43B68F7C39BEC50FBD34.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

DAE63244861947F9BC4379606AE27285.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

3D404F97EE2D42EBB0E55984B1E5D98C.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

82565139E98C48AE95155E2CF24A3C57.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

7F3E17538B904AD9A79D57F93C945CFB.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

52E7A5E5B7B7428DA735FB00CCA3C0C1.description: Progress Indicators for Reading Foundation Skills

6EEFF952F21E480782742CC2FF589A8E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

5716E9C1AFF145B485E829B4A81DEF03.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D065879C980340D7ACE9063FF2AB1562.description: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

C7816C867257482E89D66A5F3001882E.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

3D8C64B188454454BDD2B8AC4A5F60EA.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).

B6FF0B750D66440F8F2BA2ADA69854DC.description: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.

728EBC1B9A814DF2956B120F0B2F4C3B.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

8934EAF7E296470CAC3D5AF497D1C44B.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

F06A571490AF479C93A302DEC52291D3.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

7EF1DE1FE1AA4697A5F5CE868B7776ED.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

C40F91FF39154D0D98C32CB3B3F62A8E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

D91FF30E50CB4625B2C5302946191798.description: Progress Indicators for Reading Informational Text

4AC45CBC286142838CC98555174C88E2.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

CBD4D67D7BAB4606B91C812D0819FA58.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

8959A76140E14500A7DE76E4CBC09D4A.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

218396353B4F475ABF934A8178528546.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).

11851B70198B440595FACABFF822EC1C.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.

037B3F4AE0F04857BE42ED06E1D3D3C4.description: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).

6C425133F1B24CA3BF5E65E1F950FB47.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

2C43199307D84A95B4B2C63EB67CC617.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

7EC517747E5344BDA7449792862923C2.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

149FB09B9FC64ED78D587CA86F79047A.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how)

6B8DE3442F724AF2826C5D454063836B.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

E9FDC7BE72F94218B5AB876103B3A17F.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

1487AA2C222F4CD3A88D55D734D3C9C1.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

25094D7C714A487CB2843B5EAD0C2C05.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4DF3156DB507428FA521487F118262E2.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

2D8DBEF773C64826BCF7570DDFD021BE.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9A6583230B5F4FC6B6F8C103DF939E46.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

803FD74C82824A8A8B2EDAEA0E103259.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

CAE166FF2B9F4344B285CC6C98329CFA.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

F88048550C5F4207B9872ED7EE9E46D5.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

1D7D96C3BAE54E80AA4353679F4F4039.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D5D2F957D89D4188A378F3AF279DDFDA.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

8D3797D9ED3F4B97BEA573D13C044C20.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5E3E9F9651504310B11873C297F4473A.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

3A07D506AF034B83BE1C2C881732814D.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

6AC0185162F945B3916CDBBC1A948367.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects, utilizing an inquiry-based research process, based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

AB1BF844663D4F09B390887B17551D11.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A30D96EF2820426BA1DB0839C8B29739.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

0F48C881C855491C8A6C8369759FEAB7.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

B04726E5EA68477FB9EF0181DE6D012A.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

2FBCE0852FED4E9693563DCC9BB03138.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

927296B96C064C8AA305475AAE58EB42.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

97244666FADD4D039B2A8C95BE811384.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

6765251DCA9B49E281ADE96A292E8E3D.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently with scaffolding as needed.

DE82449A0E1244ABB82A0F9E1459AAE9.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

AD3EBECD1D0D4764998864A2DC1D6C76.description: Analyze and reflect on how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

540602460A904A56A891173E779300AE.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

9E0CBBD2530D4100BF931AC0BDB7C255.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

3A7E75EDF65D4455B1574E5DA0757B11.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

143E4ABD847C44F1B0832D6E71640A30.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

89DE681D976F41E797001B332D499559.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

B2D8CDE1C9A940BC96133E0DFF046135.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

3EB2D743F88F4F40B0BE4D4B9F734DEA.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

E2254E46C7344037AA4E657C4FCCAF6F.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences and relevant connections from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: NJ DOE Preschool Teaching and Learning Standards

A5C64BEDE9E64AF78D504FE2207CB512.description: Begin to use electronic devices to gain information.

4366D19B2090475DA7C09A4D795D2A28.description: Begin to use electronic devices to communicate.

AF406F1085294AABAD9AAB52E0A195DE.description:
Children know that people use different languages (including sign
language) to communicate, and will express simple greetings, words, and
phrases in a language other than their own

BDFDEC9425384746A0E0C7DC9C7C9575.description:
Children demonstrate awareness of the cultures within their classroom and
community.

96AE773E20F9463FB0697AE80DBE388B.description: Children demonstrate knowledge of neighborhood and community.

831FFE323D4B4D4F9E86EF0724BAE417.description: Children become contributing members of the classroom community.

Children identify unique characteristics of themselves, their families, and
others

A711D6AF5E024587A4F38AEC2ACD10E5.description: Children gain experience in using technology.

1E0B94C34BE04AFF86A9425A0487BFC2.description: Children observe and investigate the Earth.

854A471E3FDC4867A2A8BEA35039DB56.description: Children observe and investigate matter and energy.

8756DE56375449679DB8244094F6EC38.description: Children develop spatial and geometric sense.

89692445BDA342529D0DFEF4F8A5DECE.description:
Children begin to conceptualize measurable attributes of objects and
how to measure them.

151849DEB3E84133B4E3A0433B25F455.description: Children demonstrate an initial understanding of numerical operations.

0B73FA9910944D508E500C0F73D6B49F.description:
Children begin to demonstrate an understanding of number and
counting.

156DF57F11E84CB59D1ED4D4126944C8.description: Children apply what they have learned to new situations.

67A5DFD7250842AAB2CA07D2CE6D61CF.description: Children demonstrate initiative, engagement, and persistence.

C83A6BA146F74134A9F212D8F677B0F1.description:
Use words and phrases acquired through conversations,
activities and read alouds.

103B66DD19E74B418930F5E705FA7537.description:
With guidance and support, explore word relationships.
a) Begin to sort familiar objects (e.g., sort a
collection of plastic animals into groups: dogs,
tigers, and bears).
b) Begin to understand opposites of simple and
familiar words.
c) Identify real-life connections between words
and their use (e.g., “Tell me the name of a place
in the classroom that is noisy or quiet.”).

656B15DE42FE4479A1F602022CE17323.description:
Begin to determine the meaning of new words and
phrases introduced through preschool reading and
content.
a) With guidance and support, generate words that
are similar in meaning (e.g., rock/stone)

216902ADA5E34FE0A06F0B9BF8EB21F5.description:
Begin to understand the simple conventions of
standard English grammar during reading and
writing experiences throughout the day.
a) (Begins in kindergarten)
b) (Begins in kindergarten)
c) Attempt to write a letter or letters by
using scribble-writing, letter-like forms,
letter-strings, and invented spelling
during writing activities throughout the
day.

CAB72EF8CC5547749AA81BAF30B73596.description:
Begin to understand the conventions of standard
English grammar when speaking during
interactions and activities.
a) Print many alphabet letters.
b) Use frequently occurring nouns and
verbs.
c) Form regular plural nouns.
d) Understand and use question words (e.g.,
who, what, where, when, why, how).
e) Use frequently occurring prepositions
(e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, by,
with).
f) Begin to speak in complete sentences.
g) Understands and can follow simple
multi-step directions.

2C12B942AA0940998B6589C5BAFB9D17.description:
With guidance and support, speak audibly and express
thoughts, feelings, and ideas.

7D16A98137A6417781A2B33986BAC817.description:
Use drawings or visual displays to add to descriptions to
provide additional detail.

CD8D3B6FF279448A91C242F1B588AAC1.description:
Begin to describe familiar people, places, things, and events
and sometimes with detail.

B3AC167CEEA343A08440DAC54A9A8189.description:
Ask and answer questions to seek help, get information, or
follow directions.

1D23A7DEFA8B46BDB8BE4BF75C78BBCB.description:
Ask and answer questions about a text or other information
read aloud or presented orally.

3411A79850884904A8FC28B73008DC32.description:
Participate in conversations and interactions with peers and
adults individually and in small and large groups.
a) Follow-agreed upon rules for discussions during
group interactions.
b) Continue a conversation through several back and
forth exchanges.

AB52A7BFA9AC42D4AB7D92F6E112C849.description:
With guidance and support, recall information from experience or
familiar topic to answer a question.

822D57303D2A4277B92378CB3744D8AF.description:
With guidance and support, participate in shared research and shared
writing projects.

DC564CD2D0A449C597048BA4295ABF00.description:
With guidance and support, use digital tools to express
ideas (e.g., taking a picture of a block structure to
document or express ideas, etc.).

14B928D9870C46ED9C7CD44EC3B88D57.description:
With guidance and support, share a drawing with
dictation, scribble-writing, letter-strings, or invented
spelling to describe an event real or imagined.

C2B1EC4C77C8474C914C7B5521277E14.description:
Use a combination of drawings, dictation, scribble writing,
letter-strings, or invented spelling to share information
during play or other activities.

FC6E63AE59B74B2BAB6AC914B414E36B.description:
Use a combination of drawings, dictation, scribble writing,
letter-strings, or invented spelling to share a preference or
opinion during play or other activities.

A2E9A2D548AF4BB7B8F7CDB833D8BDA5.description:
Begin to engage in a variety of texts with purpose and
understanding.

F4674DF98C0B48D7827790B61ECCD123.description:
Demonstrate an understanding of beginning phonics and
word skills.
a) Associates many letters (consonants and
 vowels as ready) with their names and
 their most frequent sounds.
 b) (Begins in kindergarten)
 c) Recognize their name in print as well as other
 familiar print in the environment.

C193D29A959C4DF7AA5C92BD581A3616.description:
Demonstrate understanding of spoken words and begin
to understand syllables and sounds (phonemes).
a) Recognize and produce simple rhyming
words.
b) Segment syllables in spoken words by
clapping out the number of syllables.
c) Identify many initial sounds of familiar words.

537F0E84FC9844D48777A89BBF15A3D2.description:
Begin to demonstrate understanding of basic features of
print.
a) Follow words from left to right, top to bottom,
page by page.
b) Recognize that spoken words can be written and
read.
c) Recognize that words are separated by spaces.
d) Recognize and name many upper and lower case
letters of the alphabet.

376FC2F64BE34484A83DC3954F4FC360.description:
Actively participate in read aloud experiences using age
appropriate information books individually and in small
and large groups.

84B76502BB904EA89B603E4A7ABEA931.description:
With prompting and support, tell how the illustrations
support the text (information or topic) in informational text.

DEC4CCF71ACF4B8A913296FCA45CE710.description:
With prompting and support, identify the role of author and
illustrator in presenting ideas in informational text.

3D76DA0889C6440884264716B0815C5C.description: Identify the front and back cover of a book.

D2AD17E0263A4143964B9C9A58B41FDD.description:
With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about
unfamiliar words in informational text.

A6040F8EB70449FEBE2F7DD3529C640D.description:
With prompting and support, make a connection between
pieces of essential information in a familiar text.

8BACE26B1773473D91BD8826A2C5F456.description:
With prompting and support, recall important facts from a
familiar text.

9C049A0E90874173A93F81F9010B7179.description:
With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about
key elements in a familiar text.

CB8F496EFBFF42C1B0AE56A1E745DD8B.description:
Actively participate in read aloud experiences using age
appropriate literature in individual, small and large
groups.

BC2468E8BC0642D3B7074F8F0D112404.description:
With prompting and support using a familiar storybook,
tell how adventures and experiences of characters are alike
and how they are different.

DCB2E904DFFF4A879C45632D5EE55F1E.description:
With prompting and support, using a familiar storybook,
tell how the illustrations support the story.

98A8A3AA0E2940AFAF3C704A7965EDFE.description:
With prompting and support, identify the role of author and
illustrator in telling the story.

3C28A02AB5BD49BBB0DA08BE22D0B27C.description:
Recognize common types of literature (storybooks and
poetry books).

0C06F1F9F90B40548D0894E370466438.description:
With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about
unfamiliar words in a story or poem read aloud.

9992E0191017466C931502F6F8D0EA53.description:
With prompting and support, identify characters, settings,
and major events in a familiar story.

B22E71E862CB4F978AAF9C035F75CD51.description:
With prompting and support, retell familiar stories or
poems.

1EECA6E3BDA946EC8D90F6EE95CDD3F0.description:
With prompting and support, ask and answer key elements in a
familiar story or poem.

71D40FAF050E4EBB9A203235CBE235E0.description:
Children develop competence and confidence in activities that require
gross- and fine-motor skills.

6FD5ACA8F19C48D8A11790AD7489457D.description:
Children begin to develop an awareness of potential hazards in their
environment.

C28DCA14F0E042FFABE453C312936AA6.description:
Children begin to develop the knowledge and skills necessary to make
nutritious food choices.

B5961C1012CC418199E7AC6B83106010.description: Children develop self-help and personal hygiene skills.

8E5C5DA87D1442AD9DF989CB5077CEEE.description:
Children express themselves through and develop an appreciation of the
visual arts (e.g., painting, sculpting, and drawing).

5F09481AB3F14F1B906B530C14B6214B.description:
Children express themselves through and develop an appreciation of
dramatic play and storytelling.

8BD1ADB80EB14A13BAE8131274CFA03E.description:
Children express themselves through and develop an appreciation of
music.

3FAC31F548F646DD9B6A39F8ED867ED0.description:
Children express themselves through and develop an appreciation of
creative movement and dance.

EA4AC142CCD14FDE8916E368E1C28330.description: Children exhibit positive interactions with other children and adults.

document.title: NJ Pre School Teaching & Learning Standards 2014

CB068ED003B6478F9A48103E44277545.description:
Demonstrate understanding the concept of sharing by
attempting to share.

3C46AD2C7A3242F7BDB0BA38B4072E5A.description:
Demonstrate how to enter into play when a group of children
are already involved in play.

A1E22C6DC4094F388C10F5F7CC008730.description:
Play independently and cooperatively in pairs and small
groups.

87D4149CF77144BFB85B64062FD46A48.description:
Demonstrate verbal or nonverbal problem-solving skills
without being aggressive (e.g., talk about a problem and
related feelings and negotiate solutions).

95007F095ECC4F62B7672DEF2A8902ED.description:
Express needs verbally or nonverbally to teacher and peers
without being aggressive (e.g., “I don’t like it when you call
me dummy. Stop!”).

CD055B328CF0473EB9BE384B486BF694.description:
Respect the rights of others (e.g., “This painting belongs to
Carlos.”).

6419226550EB4D8C8788A74E84F24435.description:
Demonstrate socially acceptable behavior for teachers and
peers (e.g., give hugs, get a tissue, sit next to a friend/teacher,
hold hands).

643BE287D8414BA4A430427D07CBCC3B.description:
Engage appropriately with peers and teachers in classroom
activities.

D7554168EDE445B3A196304739C54D5B.description: Children exhibit positive interactions with other children and adults.

4524AC3B5B9F4250BAD6115CF385786F.description:
Channel impulses and negative feelings, such as anger (e.g.,
taking three deep breaths, using calming words, pulling self
out of play to go to “safe spot” to relax, expressive
activities).

895F19AD6C1A4B01A02293D32F5EA67A.description:
Empathize with feelings of others (e.g., get a blanket for a
friend and comfort him/her when he/she feels sad).

8B2AA8482E01462BB4CF9650163F7FC5.description:
Recognize and describe a wide range of feelings, including
sadness, anger, fear, and happiness.

F3BC46874B4C47039353E3FECCD44B8A.description: Attend to tasks for a period of time.

52B7223D973B4DDD96E98B7BEB04ED8F.description:
Move through classroom routines and activities with minimal
teacher direction and transition easily from one activity to the
next.

1DABA1A964C74C479ABE7C256D5750D9.description:
Demonstrate self-help skills (e.g., clean up, pour juice, use
soap when washing hands, put away belongings).

18E0817D460746928A93B89BDAB05BD1.description:
Make independent choices and plans from a broad range of
diverse interest centers.

document.title: Career Ready Practices

61595CF91D6A437BB7F21FBDACB8F47F.description:
Work productively in teams while using cultural global competence.
Career-ready individuals positively contribute to every team, whether formal or informal. They apply an
awareness of cultural difference to avoid barriers to productive and positive interaction. They find ways to
increase the engagement and contribution of all team members. They plan and facilitate effective team
meetings.

03C8FB75A8D5495DA92CF6A0CAFD8D7E.description: Work productively in teams while using cultural global competence.

42ABA8EC316F42BB95BA713A5FB90D50.description:
Use technology to enhance productivity.
Career-ready individuals find and maximize the productive value of existing and new technology to accomplish
workplace tasks and solve workplace problems. They are flexible and adaptive in acquiring new technology.
They are proficient with ubiquitous technology applications. They understand the inherent risks-personal and
organizational-of technology applications, and they take actions to prevent or mitigate these risks.

FE90673F78704878B604EDCD7BEEE402.description:
Plan education and career paths aligned to personal goals.
Career-ready individuals take personal ownership of their own education and career goals, and they regularly
act on a plan to attain these goals. They understand their own career interests, preferences, goals, and
requirements. They have perspective regarding the pathways available to them and the time, effort,
experience and other requirements to pursue each, including a path of entrepreneurship. They recognize the
value of each step in the education and experiential process, and they recognize that nearly all career paths
require ongoing education and experience. They seek counselors, mentors, and other experts to assist in the
planning and execution of career and personal goals.

DF4417357AFE4BB0A5E6095156676E89.description: Plan education and career paths aligned to personal goals.

3977999CE503407FB3B8E8E16807AFC3.description:
Model integrity, ethical leadership and effective management.
Career-ready individuals consistently act in ways that align personal and community-held ideals and principles
while employing strategies to positively influence others in the workplace. They have a clear understanding of
integrity and act on this understanding in every decision. They use a variety of means to positively impact the
directions and actions of a team or organization, and they apply insights into human behavior to change
others’ action, attitudes and/or beliefs. They recognize the near-term and long-term effects that
management’s actions and attitudes can have on productivity, morals and organizational culture

45FBCCABC7E545578656A56BAA5496F3.description: Model integrity, ethical leadership and effective management.

8805A6CC4AB247ADA5BED1840D521A9D.description:
Utilize critical thinking to make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
Career-ready individuals readily recognize problems in the workplace, understand the nature of the problem,
and devise effective plans to solve the problem. They are aware of problems when they occur and take action
quickly to address the problem; they thoughtfully investigate the root cause of the problem prior to
introducing solutions. They carefully consider the options to solve the problem. Once a solution is agreed
upon, they follow through to ensure the problem is solved, whether through their own actions or the actions
of others.

DCD6BC45528B41E995139DBD3FC25D80.description: Utilize critical thinking to make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

DDF4B28C36DD411E90F9834E7CC511CF.description:
Employ valid and reliable research strategies.
Career-ready individuals are discerning in accepting and using new information to make decisions, change
practices or inform strategies. They use reliable research process to search for new information. They evaluate
the validity of sources when considering the use and adoption of external information or practices in their
workplace situation.

A0D51457A6DC4E20B6253B7F70218587.description: Employ valid and reliable research strategies.

FFC6982CD8784E5DB9332EC196C19001.description:
Demonstrate creativity and innovation.
Career-ready individuals regularly think of ideas that solve problems in new and different ways, and they
contribute those ideas in a useful and productive manner to improve their organization. They can consider
unconventional ideas and suggestions as solutions to issues, tasks or problems, and they discern which ideas
and suggestions will add greatest value. They seek new methods, practices, and ideas from a variety of sources
and seek to apply those ideas to their own workplace. They take action on their ideas and understand how to
bring innovation to an organization.

38E00DB02C6446F7A3A226D76C4E4AEA.description:
Consider the environmental, social and economic impacts of decisions.
Career-ready individuals understand the interrelated nature of their actions and regularly make decisions that
positively impact and/or mitigate negative impact on other people, organization, and the environment. They
are aware of and utilize new technologies, understandings, procedures, materials, and regulations affecting
the nature of their work as it relates to the impact on the social condition, the environment and the
profitability of the organization.

8BD86EF75F61493FA3BB504ED0263C64.description: Consider the environmental, social and economic impacts of decisions.

666DD19A1FC8498CBE26219B91D51C5C.description:
Communicate clearly and effectively and with reason.
Career-ready individuals communicate thoughts, ideas, and action plans with clarity, whether using written,
verbal, and/or visual methods. They communicate in the workplace with clarity and purpose to make
maximum use of their own and others’ time. They are excellent writers; they master conventions, word
choice, and organization, and use effective tone and presentation skills to articulate ideas. They are skilled at
interacting with others; they are active listeners and speak clearly and with purpose. Career-ready individuals
think about the audience for their communication and prepare accordingly to ensure the desired outcome.

894EB51860AE4CCA85B667CF0B7E6FC9.description: Communicate clearly and effectively and with reason.

42D4D2C245284144BE2C2ED6F8B00EAC.description:
Attend to personal health and financial well-being.
Career-ready individuals understand the relationship between personal health, workplace performance and
personal well-being; they act on that understanding to regularly practice healthy diet, exercise and mental
health activities. Career-ready individuals also take regular action to contribute to their personal financial wellbeing, understanding that personal financial security provides the peace of mind required to contribute more
fully to their own career success.

71723AD76BDA498387AE5B1878F4AEA4.description: Attend to personal health and financial well-being.

F1DE052647B24969ADBAA6D79A048319.description:
Apply appropriate academic and technical skills.
Career-ready individuals readily access and use the knowledge and skills acquired through experience and
education to be more productive. They make connections between abstract concepts with real-world
applications, and they make correct insights about when it is appropriate to apply the use of an academic skill
in a workplace situation

4C4C3FC82FD44FF1A8E98F66AE6A6684.description: Apply appropriate academic and technical skills.

C31F04515C3948B2AFDABED358606B5B.description:
Act as a responsible and contributing citizen and employee
Career-ready individuals understand the obligations and responsibilities of being a member of a community,
and they demonstrate this understanding every day through their interactions with others. They are
conscientious of the impacts of their decisions on others and the environment around them. They think about
the near-term and long-term consequences of their actions and seek to act in ways that contribute to the
betterment of their teams, families, community and workplace. They are reliable and consistent in going
beyond the minimum expectation and in participating in activities that serve the greater good.

A444FA1CADBA47E1B2A4F18EEE2B5C95.description: Act as a responsible and contributing citizen and employee

27DDD44B69C8466B9E36DC6EC41DC27A.description: Disciplinary Core Ideas (Life Science, Earth & Space Science, and Engineering, Technology, & the Application of Science) for New Jersey

92A14DB15D5E42E3B92CA22059C28642.description:
Stability and change: For both designed and natural systems, conditions that affect stability and factors that control
rates of change are critical elements to consider and understand.

4A234959554E41DE988AF2EAAA162487.description: Structure and function: The way an object is shaped or structured determines many of its properties and functions.

A2B92632ABA64D0B9CA7FA49B4259D30.description: Energy and matter: Tracking energy and matter flows, into, out of, and within systems helps one understand their system’s behavior.

F0729FEAF43C4D848084DC815B35C886.description: Systems and system models: A system is an organized group of related objects or components; models can be used for understanding and predicting the behavior of systems.

DFFC97E9E88741408E63263A67A2BA1D.description:
Scale, proportion, and quantity: In considering phenomena, it is critical to recognize what is relevant at different size, time, and energy scales,
and to recognize proportional relationships between different quantities as scales change.

C31E858A70F34A6483A5855F6EAC1B29.description:
Cause and effect: Events have causes, sometimes simple, sometimes multifaceted. Deciphering causal relationships, and the
mechanisms by which they are mediated, is a major activity of science and engineering.

A1A2A961886F442D844931D34896478E.description: Patterns: Observed patterns in nature guide organization and classification and prompt questions about relationships and causes underlying them.

98E46E16B230485E9AE18B7D4576F657.description:
Obtaining, evaluating, and
communicating information: Scientists and engineers must be able to communicate clearly and persuasively the ideas and methods they generate.
Critiquing and communicating ideas individually and in groups is a critical professional activity.

B0765485190047D1A4F1B61F180FEB64.description:
Engaging in argument from evidence: Argumentation is the process by which evidence-based conclusions and solutions are reached. In science and engineering, reasoning and argument
based on evidence are essential to identifying the best explanation for a natural phenomenon or the best solution to a design problem.

06DB8B033E5B4E53818DB65FEFDD303E.description:
Constructing explanations
and designing solutions: The end-products of science are explanations and the end-products of engineering are solutions. The goal of science
is the construction of theories that provide explanatory accounts of the world. A theory becomes accepted when it has
multiple lines of empirical evidence and greater explanatory power of phenomena than previous theories.

0DFFC51BB1AC44238C7E454F6978AD55.description:
Using mathematics and
computational thinking: In both science and engineering, mathematics and computation are fundamental tools for representing physical
variables and their relationships. They are used for a range of tasks such as constructing simulations; solving equations
exactly or approximately; and recognizing, expressing, and applying quantitative relationships.

8D50DF11683949158EBFF3D7ADC96D46.description:
Analyzing and interpreting data: Scientific investigations produce data that must be analyzed in order to derive meaning. Because data patterns and trends are not always obvious,
scientists use a range of tools—including tabulation, graphical interpretation, visualization, and statistical analysis—to identify the significant
features and patterns in the data. Scientists identify sources of error in the investigations and calculate the degree of certainty in the results.

C841C63698F7484D8FA243A916590766.description:
Planning and carrying out investigations: Scientists and engineers plan and carry out investigations in the field or laboratory, working collaboratively as well as individually.
Their investigations are systematic and require clarifying what counts as data and identifying variables or parameters.

EAA1C1FA43594DAE810F81D3A8DDDD75.description:
Developing and using models: A practice of both science and engineering is to use and construct models as helpful tools for representing ideas and explanations.
These tools include diagrams, drawings, physical replicas, mathematical representations, analogies, and computer simulations.

E3531C94D6EA45599A223126761ACE1A.description:
Asking questions and defining problems: A practice of science is to ask and refine questions that lead to descriptions and explanations of how
the natural and designed world(s) works and which can be empirically tested.

727FE4C36655433A90E5F7229F869DC7.description:
The purpose of cleaning data is to remove
errors and make it easier for computers to
process.

3AF86388CC2E41EE963C42CD8BF26F37.description: Identify the appropriate tool to access data based on its file format.

5379FC945CF448CEBC4F93B2F96288F8.description: Explain the difference between how the computer stores data as bits and how the data is displayed.

61200B7098514182A0B7BEDE48AEB224.description:
Data is represented in many formats. Software
tools translate the low-level representation of
bits into a form understandable by individuals.
Data is organized and accessible based on the
application used to store it.

016CFCCBD08F48B598FF8FF4DD21D447.description: Organize and transform data collected using computational tools to make it usable for a specific purpose.

People use digital devices and tools to
automate the collection, use, and
transformation of data.

transformed is influenced by the type of digital
device(s) available and the intended use of the
data

change individuals’ behaviors.
Society is faced with trade-offs due to the
increasing globalization and automation that
computing brings.

networks can be protected from unauthorized
access and modification in a variety of ways.

understanding the key security measures and
best practices needed to proactively address
the threat to digital data.

135D27DDA884424D98F543425C5B52F2.description: Model how information is broken down into smaller pieces, transmitted as addressed packets through multiple devices over networks and the Internet, and reassembled at the destination.

22896F11CECD4AF5974230FB0CCEAE53.description:
Protocols, packets, and addressing are the key
components for reliable delivery of
information across networks.

Systematically apply troubleshooting strategies to identify and resolve hardware and
software problems in computing systems.

3C7A19E3B4DE4E09800E2B6BF0F016DD.description:

when knowledge of the specific device along
with a systematic process is used to identify
the source of a problem.

091BB988E467455681AFD7BA22B1B177.description: Justify design decisions and explain potential system trade-offs.

EBC2C04D6D4644E49F460514B654B0E1.description: Design a system that combines hardware and software components to process data.

8FBC24F7FA3144B29AAB49A2EB4017C7.description:
Software and hardware determine a computing
system’s capability to store and process
information. The design or selection of a
computing system involves multiple
considerations and potential trade-offs.

00F5E21D83884174A4D5029233D9A310.description:
The study of human–computer interaction can
improve the design of devices and extend the
abilities of humans.

making that is meaningful to the

Brainstorm and curate ideas to
innovatively problem solve during

Board of Education, and Roe v. Wade).

B37F046F5F134903999736483941388C.description: Analyze the motivations, causes, and consequences of the genocides of Armenians, Ukrainians, Jews in the Holocaust and assess the responses by individuals, groups, and governments and analyze large-scale atrocities including 20th century massacres in China.

481AE4E6B79D4D6DB72143094F47329D.description: Compare and contrast socialism, communism, fascism, and liberal democracy, analyze the extent to which they promote and protect civil, political, social and economic rights for people, and explain the reasons for their growth or decline around the world.

43B5F48EA34244A1B92D78AD3CBDAD11.description: Era 4 - Half-Century of Crisis and Achievement: The Era of the Great Wars

E0B828D1782645FBBF49AF588E95DCDB.description: Analyze the impact of the policies of different European colonizers on indigenous societies and explain the responses of these societies to imperialistic rule.

0B055E11E728422D83C93E058111F41A.description: Analyze the extent to which racism was both a cause and consequence of imperialism and evaluate the impact of imperialism from multiple perspectives.

A5A1A56C68B34006A78FE2E38DEA74CB.description: Explain how industrialization and urbanization affected class structure, family life, the daily lives of men, women, and children, and the environment.

572B377EE3AC45888B2CE6800EFE94A5.description: Compare the characteristics of capitalism, socialism, and communism to determine why each system emerged and its success in leading to economic growth and stability.

669B4B22EF0348A496CE889431343A21.description: Determine how, and the extent to which, scientific and technological changes, transportation, and new forms of energy brought about social, economic, and cultural changes in the world.

D8732227B60C40ADABC83D3ED091FAB1.description: Compare the impact of imperialism on economic development in Africa, Asia, and Latin America regarding barriers or opportunities for future development and political independence.

7DDE8119FA1C4F6D838A98361B2D1E7B.description: Construct a claim based on evidence regarding on the interrelationships between the Industrial Revolution, nationalism, competition for global markets, imperialism, and natural resources in different regions of the world.

8AEF197BE1284FBDB2928DDA4A219C2D.description: Analyze the interrelationships between the "agricultural revolution," population growth, industrialization, specialization of labor, and patterns of landholding in 19th century Britain.

A9596BE62B124EAABCADA5F18784BE63.description: Use geographic tools and resources to investigate the changes in political boundaries between 1815 and 1914 and make evidence-based inferences regarding the impact of imperialism.

860651BD855540559E2B0261EC21B06B.description: Debate if the role of geography or enlightened ideals had the greater influence on the independence movements in Latin America.

8F01AB2D2C9743758D1474EB9CF17362.description: Use data and evidence to compare and contrast the struggles for women's suffrage and workers' rights in Europe and North America and evaluate the degree to which each movement achieved its goals.

E7282DAFAE8A478196FE20B194C9F92F.description: Use a variety of resources from multiple perspectives to analyze the responses of various governments to pressure from the people for self-government, reform, and revolution.

0E79EFD872DF4A95B9EF410622057510.description: Cite evidence describing how and why various ideals became driving forces for reforms and revolutions in Latin America and across the world (e.g., liberty, popular sovereignty, natural rights, democracy, nationalism).

185DC0C4410E4FA6A5E6E3A75702ADD0.description: Analyze the relationship between industrialization and the rise of democratic and social reforms, including the expansion of parliamentary government.

21DB204A737D439E9C926198621C43B9.description: Era 3 - Age of Revolutions: Political and Industrial Revolutions, Imperialism, Reform and Global Impact (1750–1914)

0B74339D618F4C6A9AB0DC6CF1030147.description: Analyze the impact of new intellectual, philosophical, and scientific ideas on how humans viewed themselves and how they viewed their physical and spiritual worlds.

CB738FC99B8D4CE19538424C96FEC45D.description: Assess the impact of the printing press and other technologies developed on the dissemination of ideas.

8EDB3868A03042ACAC2E8B12B806E128.description: Explore the factors that laid the foundation for the Renaissance (i.e., Asian and Islamic, Ancient Greek and Roman innovations).

E77F4008050F4F879E6A2D311D922A15.description: Determine the factors that led to the Reformation and the impact on European politics.

B791AA6BA0CF4F94B137F6CF7CD421AF.description: Relate the development of more modern banking and financial systems to European economic influence in the world.

C16BF06E54D545B498EFCF150ED8EFFD.description: Make an evidence-based argument explaining the impact and development of religion in Europe on the political and cultural development of the colonies in the New World.

FF32F90FF97248BC8F2F9EC93F9A53F5.description: Determine the reasons for, and the consequences of, the rise of powerful, centralized nation states in Europe (i.e., the French absolute monarchy and the English limited monarchy).

B0D953E3B2C64C03B11E71EFA11813AA.description: Compare the principle ideas of the Enlightenment in Europe (e.g., political, social, gender, education) with similar ideas in Asia and the Muslim / Islamic empires of the Middle East and North Africa.

CCB4C434E65E495E879956A7596AFC10.description: Era 2 - Renaissance, Reformation, Scientific Revolution, and Enlightenment (1350–1700)

AE03C87AFE344344AC0350FA3DEE4766.description: Assess the impact of economic, political, and social policies and practices regarding African slaves, indigenous peoples, and Europeans in the Spanish and Portuguese colonies.

823797A985384C7A87133ADCBE76577E.description: Assess the political, social, and economic impact of the interactions between indigenous peoples and colonizers over different time periods (e.g., Columbian Exchange, forced labor, slave trade and slavery practices, spread of disease, lingering effects on cultures).

33A433EC3A4D4BD9B9A6A4BB65FEAB90.description: Compare and contrast the motivations for and methods by which various empires (e.g., Ming, Qing, Spanish, Mughal, Ottoman) expanded, and assess why some were more effective than others in maintaining control of their empires.

AF9A1B918E7D449AA65AB520311FF2F7.description: Compare slavery practices and other forms of coerced labor or social bondage common in East Africa, West Africa, Southwest Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

8AE401183C074E7D95A2582040F006F7.description: Explain how the new social stratification created by voluntary and coerced interactions among Native Americans, Africans, and Europeans in Spanish colonies laid the foundation for conflict.

B10C70E81F8343F4BF2C8F5FE4C8C284.description: Analyze various motivations for the Atlantic slave trade and the impact on Europeans, Africans, and Americans.

1E61A1ECD80C41A4BB0149B81B061530.description: Determine the extent to which various technologies, (e.g., printing, marine compass, cannonry, Arabic numerals) derived from Europe's interactions with Islam and Asia provided the necessary tools for European exploration and conquest.

2EB6C760429A473DA65B58FBC20B6ABB.description: Determine the effects of increased global trade and the importation of gold and silver from the New World on inflation in Europe, Southwest Asia, and Africa.

3F27E45B941F4C4E93A2027C990FAEFB.description: Assess the role of mercantilism in stimulating European expansion through trade, conquest, and colonization.

A47115FC15BA474BB1E43C48FCF6CAF5.description: Trace the movement of essential commodities (e.g., sugar, cotton) from Asia to Europe to America, and determine the impact trade on the New World's economy and society.

66F189D9B2EE4508A281823F4630C055.description: Compare and contrast the economic policies of China and Japan, and determine the impact these policies had on growth, the desire for colonies, and the relative positions of China and Japan within the emerging global economy.

6EB005B412104781B4B339A59AB6D877.description: Determine the role of natural resources, climate, and topography in European exploration, colonization, and settlement patterns.

80C88E43BF2047B89DC52132CF50AD02.description: Use geographic representations to assess changes in political boundaries and the impact of European political and military control in Africa, Asia, and the Americas by the mid-18th century.

0A0FC96B2FE44AAAAAB2984E6F4D4E66.description: Era 1 - The Emergence of the First Global Age: Global Interactions and Colonialism

standardSets.title: Visual Arts: By the end of  grade 8

document.title: 2020 NJ SLS

CE66AEA5CEE248BFB013A7EBF0DD7EE2.description: Analyze and contrast how art forms are used to reflect global issues, including climate change.

65D6ED23872B409EA907FA67F14BD4C6.description:
Analyze and contrast how art forms are used to represent, establish, reinforce and reflect
group identity and culture.

D7CB587C96D445E1A73832A5E37DD4DD.description:
Relating artistic ideas and works within societal, cultural, and
historical contexts to deepen understanding

4BD8951FDE1A426085AE4F53BDB31E92.description:
Generate ideas to make art individually or collaboratively to positively reflect a group's
identity.

99073B39F8734A1793667F8E8FFC3684.description:
Synthesizing and relating knowledge and personal experiences to
create products

63CA726CD5BC4789BC49F83083E4E247.description:
Create a convincing and logical argument to support an evaluation of art. Explain the
difference between personal and established criteria for evaluating artwork.

39D13DF2A2ED423CB69A48551D6CC230.description:
Interpret art by analyzing how the interaction of subject matter, characteristics of form
and structure, use of media, art making approaches, and relevant contextual information contributes to
understanding messages or ideas and mood conveyed.

E667A15A2705447BAB5024F136582641.description: Compare and contrast cultural and social contexts of visual arts and how they influence ideas and emotions.

569EB71E3EE6473D9772E8A4A7833448.description:
Explain how a person's aesthetic choices are influenced by culture and environment, and
how they impact the way in which visual messages are perceived and conveyed.

DE652DC096D04A098076A37CACD577E0.description:
Analyze how exhibitions in different venues communicate meaning and influence ideas,
beliefs and experiences.

76A720E322A841A78CCB373470A06F24.description:
Individually or collaboratively prepare and present theme-based artwork for display and
formulate exhibition narratives.

1DBAD427E52B4A57825908B8594952D2.description:
Developing and refining techniques and models or steps needed to
create products

9A2C634DA0624B8796B28D5B84377FB3.description:
Investigate and analyze ways artwork is presented, preserved and experienced, including
use of evolving technology. Evaluate a collection or presentation based on this criterion.

1F6409D2E2094D60820520FD38AADEF3.description:
Use criteria to examine, reflect on and plan revisions for a work of art, and create an
artistic statement.

7475A4BB45D8433A91B2E24AAA33B74C.description: Apply, organize and strategize methods for design and redesign of objects, places, systems, images and words to clearly communicate information to a diverse audience.

1CE8866BC2924B199EEC86143363E58F.description: Demonstrate an awareness of ethical responsibility as applied to artmaking including environmental implications, responsibility in sharing images online, appropriation, and intellectual property ethics.

0F0D2C97452342648D4779BE43DD11FA.description:
Demonstrate persistence and willingness to experiment and take risks during the artistic
process.

FD9296548B6E43DB97D90BB7341A7981.description:
Develop criteria, identify goals and collaboratively investigate an aspect of present-day
life, using contemporary practice of art or design

5D06EFAD857547BDA66BBA45C6ADC0AE.description:
Conceptualize early stages of the creative process, including applying methods to
overcome creative blocks or take creative risks, and document the processes in traditional or new
media.

standardSets.title: Dance: By the end of grade 12
standardSets.subject: Visual and Performing Arts (2020-)

document.title: 2020 Visual & Performing Arts Standards

2BDD88C140234F70831913D85D5706C9.description:
Analyze the role of dance in a global society. Examine various genres, styles,
historical time periods, societal changes, and perspectives. Evaluate how dance movement,
characteristics, techniques, and artist criteria relate to the ideas and perspectives of the people from
whom the dances originate.

C8CD33D8DB8A46CABFBD798C3FD35CE0.description:
Analyze how the role of dance in a global society has influenced various cultures,
societies and historical periods throughout history. Examine how innovations in the arts have impacted
dance-making in these communities in relation to the ideas and perspectives of the people from whom
the dances originate.

64E47E99EA8A42939DDE5D523FE880B8.description:
Analyze and discuss the role of dance in a global society. Examine genres, styles,
historical time periods, societal changes and perspectives and how those changes impact dance in
relation to the ideas and perspectives of the people from whom the dances originate.

93735D4B384547A18E1F4336F381FF64.description:
Relating artistic ideas and works within societal, cultural, and
historical contexts to deepen understanding.

915C2BF298C1469B91A594B23D9374B6.description:
Investigate and present ways in which dance can be used to communicate new
perspectives and/or realizations about global issues, including global warming

2F19270247DE49F3A686DC226376A518.description:
Formulate personal choreography with respect to its content and context. Reflect
and analyze the variables that contributed to the personal perspectives presented in the dance work,
and examine how exposure to various cultures influences individual, emotional, intellectual, and
kinesthetic responses to dance works.

E4D025FD7BBD4E4790FB14443DC7A0CD.description:
Collaboratively investigate global issues, including climate change, to inform the
development of an original dance project. Evaluate and present ways in which critical concepts are
communicated metaphorically through dance.

244280467C144C45A4615CA6792C5B24.description:
Evaluate personal choreography and how personal experiences and exposure to
various cultures influences individual, emotional, intellectual, and kinesthetic responses to dance
works.

80AAE429DAD343AFA01B9B8B1C68B9C7.description:
Research global issues, including climate change, using multiple research methods
to inform original dances expressed through multiple genres, styles, and varied cultural perspectives.

E3BC2CA0CC1147CFA502AC6E79E1CABD.description:
Analyze a dance to determine the ideas expressed by the choreographer. Explain
how the perspectives expressed by the choreographer impact personal interpretation. Consider how
personal background and experiences influence responses to dance works.

D47DF35A2FFF4471B40783175F39B549.description:
Synthesizing and relating knowledge and personal experiences to
create products.

581B24727D714AB78D6D68EE91F21352.description:
Define personal artistic preferences to critique dance and justify the point of view.
Consider content, context, genre, style, and/or cultural movement practice to formulate artistic
expression.

6592CE40E5C940F48AE1F11837616713.description:
Differentiate artistic criteria to determine what makes an effective performance and
justify the point of view. Consider content, context, genre, style, and/or cultural movement practice to
comprehend artistic expression. Use genre-specific dance terminology.

25613C3855914512A68CDE5115691DBC.description:
Analyze artistic criteria to determine what makes an effective performance. Consider
content, context, genre, style, and/or cultural movement practice to comprehend artistic expression.
Use genre-specific dance terminology.

3F8A50E34D7C4B7581026BC08250C078.description:
Analyze and interpret how the elements of dance, execution of dance movements and
context contribute to artistic expression across different genres, styles or cultural movement practices.
Use genre specific dance terminology.

5ABD4E9038884D8AAA31B890219D5E18.description:
Analyze and discuss how the elements of dance, execution of dance movements and
context contribute to artistic expression in a variety of genres, styles or cultural movement practices
using genre specific terminology.

E5CAF9326A48476C8524592E78EC948B.description:
Distinguish different dances and discuss their intent and artistic expression. Explain
how the relationships among the elements of dance, execution of dance movements and context
enhance meaning and support intent using genre specific dance techniques.

E33ED4C44D5E486D9C57124247BCC534.description:
Explain how dance communicates aesthetic and cultural values in a variety of
genres, styles and/or cultural movement practices. Use genre-specific dance terminology.

063AA889EB80490183199B550788DBCC.description:
Use genre-specific dance terminology to analyze dance works from a variety of
dance genres, reflecting on recurring patterns of movement and their relationships in well-structured
and meaningful choreography.

2FD9B1CB633247029FB37AE76EA3B980.description:
Analyze and compare the movement patterns and their relationships in a variety of
genres, styles, or cultural movement practices and explain how their differences impact
communication and intent within a cultural context. Use genre-specific dance terminology

CE95CB2B67E742F59CB023712E57FF64.description:
Use genre-specific dance terminology to analyze dance works, recurring patterns of
movement and their relationships that create structure and meaning in dance.

A19EE8A3678746139679A9355BE79A1C.description:
Analyze the use of elements of dance in a variety of genres, styles or cultural
movement practices within the cultural context to communicate intent. Use genre-specific dance
terminology to compare and contrast.

5945B1C288554498AA735A150F46DD3F.description:
Use genre-specific terminology to analyze recurring patterns of movement and their
relationships in dance in context of artistic intent.

D4FAB93C4D4E47A49C5772F27C49184C.description:
Design and organize the technical and production elements to collaboratively
produce and fulfill the artistic intent of dance works in a variety of performance venues.

7001717A06B04EDDB6EB6A7D81CF48E5.description:
Refine performance skills using a broad repertoire of strategies for dynamic
projection. Demonstrate and model leadership qualities, performance etiquette and performance
practice during class, rehearsal and performance. Develop a professional portfolio (e.g., resume, head
shot, social media platforms) that documents the rehearsal and performance process with fluency in
professional dance and production terminology. Analyze and evaluate the success of a performance.

EA1E4CB155B34DE8BFA03CCA58631BFD.description:
Initiate, plan and direct rehearsals with attention to technical details applying
rehearsal strategies for individual and ensemble work that enhance artistry, incorporate self-analysis,
and are solutions oriented to achieve performance excellence.

EAC725ED37994BF6879BAAECE2BF5FF6.description:
Research, develop and apply personal strategies of visualization, motor imagery, and
breath to become more aware of the relationships that exist between the body and mind.

6E48D3C591D840BD889576B150FDFBE5.description:
Select and organize, alone and with others, technical and production elements
necessary to fulfill the artistic intent of dance works in alternative performance venues.

D8800EC0B6BE435A95E8ACCE8D172DC2.description:
Implement performance strategies to enhance projection. Demonstrate leadership
qualities (e.g., commitment, dependability, responsibility, cooperation) and model performance
etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsal and performance. Accept notes from the
choreographer and apply corrections to future performances. Document the rehearsal and
performance process using dance and production terminology. Analyze and evaluate the success of a
performance.

D50F331BFC5C44B68151F59994A07EF4.description:
Apply rehearsal strategies to refine ensemble skills, performance accuracy,
consistency, and expressiveness. Develop personal rehearsal strategies to enhance artistry and achieve
performance goals.

A22A4E8A20234847AD60370918F1417C.description:
Embody the use of the senses and create imagery to envision a particular outcome,
projecting and completing movements to enhance dance performance.

D120D99322004E34B11D97E5700B104A.description:
Demonstrate a variety of technical elements (e.g., costumes, lighting, sound,
performance cues) of a dance performance. Utilize production and technical terminology to
communicate with performers and backstage personnel.

B191342726F84BC48F4E52607F7C6D45.description:
Adapt movements to performance area. Demonstrate performance etiquette and
performance practices during class, rehearsal and performance. Accept notes from the choreographer
and apply corrections to future performances. Document the rehearsal and performance process using
dance and production terminology. Analyze and evaluate the success of a performance.

122E10FA821F474DB2B54C2A2D00689E.description:
Rehearse a dance and apply specific feedback to refine performance accuracy,
consistency, and expressiveness. Demonstrate group awareness and develop personal rehearsal
strategies.

53CDE031D9D94D6AA8EFACBFEE85A86E.description:
Investigate visualization, motor imagery, and breath to apply and enhance the quality
of body mechanics and the energy related to the movement skill.

140DE6DDD8C4493393C7AD6B5A632289.description:
Articulate clarity of codified movement and intention through the execution of
prescribed vocabulary and techniques within styles/genres.

B1DD5CB7E3764F81A83BC58E5AF69ACB.description:
Analyze personal patterns of misalignment and develop prescribed conditioning
practices and corrective exercises to enhance optimal alignment in performance.

91F8B4CAA2D8440589EF02E8E871EC54.description:
Adjust oppositional pulls/tensions of the body while moving through vertical, off center, and non-vertical alignment. Maintain optimal alignment preceding and following floor and air
patterns. Modulate the placement and shifting of energy in the body.

8762AF8666394519B987B37CFFB32467.description:
Examine the muscular-skeletal system (e.g., attachments, origin, function) and
manipulate kinesthetic principles to enhance technical execution of dance movements.

82BFACC1D5F84EEEA2A44FDD602E2603.description:
Develop and implement healthful strategies for nutrition, injury prevention and
psychological wellness related to dance activities and everyday life.

9225C0F5D75445E6AEF5B95F9F0B222B.description:
Execute clarity of movement intention during complex movement sequences. Use
style/genre specific vocabulary and execute codified movements with style/genre specific alignment
and characteristics, through focused practice and repetition.

90F8A0AB6EE046F68012C9DE3D329E80.description:
Develop personal conditioning practices, using different body conditioning
techniques, that improve range of motion, muscular flexibility, strength, and endurance to enhance
performance.

59AF934646CB4F7697BFD2C183593565.description:
Maintain optimal alignment and adjust the placement and shifting energy of the body
while traveling through space, both preceding and following jumps.

6B288A2985F94365A46615ABF03BC8BC.description:
Investigate how kinesthetic principles and various body systems relate to the dancing
body. Examine how the muscles and bones animate the dancer's moving structure.

ED46F799C9084B1DBC55E3F015F46A00.description:
Research healthful strategies essential for dancers and modify personal practice based
on findings.

34E341612342453ABD939A5E96816715.description:
Demonstrate style/genre specific vocabulary and codified movements with
style/genre specific alignment. Demonstrate, through focused practice and repetition, breath control,
body part initiation and body sequencing.

B801B933311B4E22B7134B4AE30BCE31.description:
Explore movement that develops a wide range of motion, muscular flexibility,
strength, and endurance. Explore different body conditioning techniques (e.g., yoga, weight training,
aerobics, Pilates).

81DE53D14DC94A82AB805471D8CCE440.description:
Demonstrate body coordination while moving (e.g., elongated spine, vertical
alignment, release of tension from shoulders; use of vertical, off center, non-vertical alignment) the
body through space.

1478A09BCB72474C8E2D45E2F42B684C.description:
Demonstrate joint articulations and basic anatomical terms (e.g., muscles, bones,
tendons, ligaments) as they relate to dance. Apply kinesthetic principles and various body systems.

B304A4F39CF94517A1B45688F83BCBC5.description:
Evaluate and apply healthful strategies (e.g., nutrition, injury prevention, emotional
health, overall functioning) and safe body-use practices that are essential for the dancer.

3724E8B8F1004754901B10B7E6F6A59C.description:
Developing and refining techniques and models or steps needed to
create products.

F7F3AD4171A04E67AF02B2F8F288D7A4.description:
Perform planned and improvised movement sequences and dance combinations while
self-monitoring and adjusting dynamics and energy to the choreographic intent.

AA797B6A1F19474A98F667A812A78A76.description:
Modulate time factors for artistic interest and expressive acuity. Apply multiple and
complex rhythms (e.g., contrapuntal, polyrhythmic). Work with and against the rhythm of
accompaniment or sound environments.

F06388305BA74704A6E00471B26FE099.description:
Modulate and use the broadest range of movement in space for artistic and expressive
clarity. Use inward and outward focus to clarify movement and intent. Establish and break
relationships with other dancers and audience as appropriate to the dance.

FB0FE403E96146DCA5A181EC421AF1ED.description:
Perform planned and improvised movement sequences and dance combinations while
self-monitoring and adjusting dynamics and energy to the choreographic intent.

1FC6D4FCF0734B158099CECB12FA485A.description:
Use syncopation and accented movements related to different tempi. Take rhythmic
cues from different aspects of accompaniment. Integrate breath with metric and kinesthetic phrasing.

2DA3730426DA43F18BD58F19FAF7018D.description:
Expand partner and ensemble skills. Execute floor and air pathways while
maintaining relationships with spatial focus and intentionality. Dance alone and with others with
spatial intention.

16AD034D108E4BCDBDF1B2E3BACEA760.description:
Perform planned and improvised movement sequences and dance combinations with
variations that accurately demonstrate contrasting dynamics and energy (e.g., fast/slow, sharp/smooth,
strong/gentle, tight/loose).

510FE2E8725248A2ADD76FF5F0E04799.description:
Use syncopation and accented movements related to different tempi. Take rhythmic
cues from different aspects of accompaniment. Integrate breath with metric and kinesthetic phrasing.

B53344583AED406592A4838D0A25FC65.description:
Develop partner and ensemble skills that enable contrasting level changes while
maintaining a sense of spatial design and relationship. Use space intentionally during phrases and
through transitions between phrases.

210458D280614BD68F0D878E1492D5CD.description:
Create a portfolio of original dances using recognized systems of dance
documentation (e.g., writing, a form of notation symbols, using media technologies), providing a
complete picture of the creative process and product.

7D47A038FB1D47D288BC0BA1308F04BA.description:
Refine the artistic intent of a dance by manipulating choreographic devices, dance
structure, and artistic criteria (e.g., production elements, music/sound, props, costumes). Evaluate
self-reflection and feedback from others and apply when warranted. Document choices made in the
revision process and justify how the refinements support artistic intent.

5865D012CD0048698E76DF52219E1122.description:
Develop a strategy to record a dance using recognized systems of dance
documentation (e.g., writing, a form of notation symbols, using media technologies).

FBC5CF7350C740E8BB960C653E6994B5.description:
Clarify the artistic intent of a dance using established artistic criteria, self-reflection
and the feedback of others. Analyze and evaluate the impact of choices made in the revision process.
Justify the reasons for revisions.

ECD616F28ABD40828CF81186A36CDF9A.description:
Compare recognized notation systems to document a section of a dance using
writing, symbols, or media technologies (e.g., graphic symbols and figures, path mapping, numerical
systems, letter and word notations).

CC01AEF79C8A4481966740FFBF21CF15.description:
Revise a movement study based on self-reflection and feedback of others to improve
the quality of a planned movement sequence. Articulate movement choices and revisions. Analyze
and evaluate the impact of choices made in the revision process.

260B6294C2BE40EF8D099C0584FB6BA5.description:
Develop artistic statements that reflect personal aesthetics of self-generated dance
studies.

2F03D8187FDA463FBEA3AA59243B7AFA.description:
Demonstrate fluency and personal voice in designing and choreographing original
dances. Articulate an understanding of how choreographic devices and dance structures affect artistic
intent. Justify choreographic choices and explain how they are used to intensify artistic intent.

DD4D95F54A9049AB97A539E031FC661F.description:
Develop an artistic statement that reflects a personal aesthetic for an original dance
study or dance. Select and demonstrate movements that support the artistic statement.

BF0B739DF6304D5C8E440528E4A7FE94.description:
Work individually and collaboratively to design dance studies that integrate and
recombine movement vocabulary, choreographic devices and dance structures drawn from a variety
of dance genres. Explain how the dance vocabulary and structures clarify the artistic intent.

77FC34D254474CE387126DA503E6B7BB.description:
Choose a theme to develop a dance and create corresponding movements to
communicate the theme. Develop a dance study by selecting a specific movement vocabulary to
communicate a main idea. Discuss how the dance communicates non-verbally.

18E123929BCC484991464F2DAC373BFE.description:
Manipulate a variety of choreographic devices and dance structures to
collaboratively develop a dance study with a clear artistic intent. Use dance terminology to explain
how the dance structures clarify the artistic intent.

D8A2F70B6AEE48E888ECD27FEFDD13D5.description:
Expand personal movement preferences and strengths to discover unexpected

B56FCEE8D98B48B4B6784EDC02760383.description:

E9B99292B143423E8163BC65BCDC5228.description:

Apply theatrical elements and research to create a design that communicates the

19D6160348D44F25A8AF2A763E998530.description:
Refine a range of acting skills to build believable and sustainable characters in a

D9AC11C4F5EC47FBB55954169F58B8A4.description: Use technical elements to increase the impact of design for a theatre production.

Rehearse various acting exercises to expand skills in a rehearsal for devised or
scripted theatre performance.

726B5D2ECE6C4F3FAE8523C86B2C922A.description:
Originate and construct technical design choices that support the story and emotional

1BAB5DAF50AB4269BD61E82F2804C178.description:
Transform devised or scripted theatre work using the rehearsal process to re-imagine

861666AE39594015B5D900FDC7E6C91A.description:
Explore physical, vocal and psychological characteristics to create a

7504456F9249473EA9737BF88479EB17.description:
Re-imagine technical design choices during the course of the rehearsal process to

9BFC5D453BFE48948EEA412A34E26A33.description:
Use the rehearsal process to analyze and revise a devised or scripted theatre work

9F20B4C5A08E4B6988AB5331BFF4F89E.description:
Explore physical and vocal choices to develop a character that is believable and
authentic in devised or scripted theatre work.

09EF955B302F414EABCC29392AC336E6.description:
Explore technical design choices that support the story and emotional impact of a
scripted or devised theatre work.

125A51A3A1BF4CAFB94B5F2A8A407972.description: Practice devised or scripted theatre work using theatrical staging conventions.

D953E8923C8C4AF4B01D7FF882312616.description:
Use script analysis to inform choices impacting the believability and authenticity of

51A74063B6EF4E0E91AFDC27B21FB684.description:
Collaborate as a creative team to make original artistic choices in devised or scripted
theatre work.

01F076A2EDB74034ACC5088AD664623E.description:
Collaborate as a creative team to make informative and analytical choices for devised

35C18D2ADEC14A699DCB5A25C295CC14.description:
Cooperate as a creative team to make informative and analytical choices for devised
or scripted theatre work.

7143FC684DC1423097C43D879306DCE7.description:
Develop a dramatic interpretation to demonstrate a critical understanding of historical

1396DD1A7F0040DFA6ECD3EBA953DF78.description:
Examine the collaborative nature of the actor, director, playwright, and designers,
and explore their interdependent roles.

521B6C0E5113471E81A105C207277982.description:
Explore the function of history and culture in the development and subsequent
interpretations of devised or scripted theatre work.

is believable and authentic.

multiple elements of technology.

F09B1A0193A246578C15AF5C28E28E53.description:

Use personal experiences and knowledge to develop a character that is believable and

work.

A45633DCAABB408FB8C20065E42C4DC0.description:
Research to construct ideas about the visual composition of devised or scripted
