document.title: 2020 New Jersey Student Learning Standards - Computer Science and Design Thinking

176B6459FAF94687B2F6E92886CF9703.description: Research historical tensions between environmental and economic considerations as driven by human needs and wants in the development of a technological product and present the competing viewpoints.

78DBCA429BED4BDC89AC7520EBE86D5C.description: Synthesize data, analyze trends, and draw conclusions regarding the effect of a technology on the individual, culture, society, and environment and share this information with the appropriate audience.

F3F6D77A018941A0B84AD9196359A043.description: Assess the positive and negative impacts of emerging technologies on developing countries and evaluate how individuals, non-profit organizations, and governments have responded.

2AD0F8E01C2F4635B78982D5EA4CFC90.description: Analyze controversial technological issues and determine the degree to which individuals, businesses, and governments have an ethical roles in decisions that are made.

6C31B1FEE4D94B6AAE1527FBB4346D52.description: The ability to ethically integrate new technologies requires deciding whether to introduce a technology, taking into consideration local resources and the role of culture in acceptance.Consequences of technological use may be different for different groups of people and may change over time.Since technological decisions can have ethical implications, it is essential that individuals analyze issues by gathering evidence from multiple perspectives and conceiving of alternative possibilities before proposing solutions.

73FA1BE3812347708144291A3F902E22.description: Identify a complex, global environmental or climate change issue, develop a systemic plan of investigation, and propose an innovative sustainable solution.

4A704D2503C24074A5899E3E60D3C99A.description: Synthesize and analyze data collected to monitor the effects of a technological product or system on the environment.

74E430CA419341F5A70BF39FFE0FF36F.description: Evaluate ethical considerations regarding the sustainability of environmental resources that are used for the design, creation, and maintenance of a chosen product.

EF6B265F18F445708E65D79C1743E319.description: Development and modification of any technological system needs to take into account how the operation of the system will affect natural resources and ecosystems.Impacts of technological systems on the environment need to be monitored and must inform decision-making.Many technologies have been designed to have a positive impact on the environment and to monitor environmental change over time.

A7DF87D6163C466CA2095246DBDFE835.description: Effects of Technology on the Natural World

2855E69D5813402C984F75DB9623FAE7.description: Redesign an existing product to improve form or function.

0C6BC35955664CBDBC7FB5025ADC8897.description: Explain how different groups can contribute to the overall design of a product.

31F717F8984347D2A520731ABBD0D700.description: Engineers use science, mathematics, and other disciplines to improve technology. Increased collaboration among engineers, scientists, and mathematicians can improve their work and designs.Technology, product, or system redesign can be more difficult than the original design.

FD5A94B7E40A41158217394D6547EE63.description: Analyze the impact that globalization, social media, and access to open source technologies has had on innovation and on a society's economy, politics, and culture.

66CB57328FB34FFB8BA96A876ACAAA78.description: Propose an innovation to meet future demands supported by an analysis of the potential costs, benefits, trade-offs, and risks related to the use of the innovation.

98E16C5335D34458B0CE2276A70BF886.description: Changes caused by the introduction and use of a new technology can range from gradual to rapid and from subtle to obvious and can change over time. These changes may vary from society to society as a result of differences in a society's economy, politics, and culture.

6D9D3C3885CA418AB411E385BCA3FA43.description: Analyze a product to determine the impact that economic, political, social, and/or cultural factors have had on its design, including its design constraints.

4583EAFDF6154AE4830A1A5C8F31C7E5.description: Decisions to develop new technology are driven by societal and cultural opinions and demands that differ from culture to culture.

6AAD50C259BC4C30A4844B5675A364E2.description: Analyze the effects of changing resources when designing a specific product or system (e.g., materials, energy, tools, capital, labor).

F84DF98FE5264C88B74D8BBC558263AD.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of a product or system based on factors that are related to its requirements, specifications, and constraints (e.g., safety, reliability, economic considerations, quality control, environmental concerns, manufacturability, maintenance and repair, ergonomics).

3CB739A2292B45FF8C5FD74CFB5B7B05.description: Engineering design evaluation, a process for determining how well a solution meets requirements, involves systematic comparisons between requirements, specifications, and constraints.

70F2195F9DD14D80BFEF13D2A29526B2.description: Design a product or system that addresses a global problem and document decisions made based on research, constraints, trade-offs and aesthetic and ethical considerations and share this information with an appropriate audience.

528BBFC2BDC54DFE88410FD66AE94D80.description: Evaluate several models of the same type of product and make recommendations for a new design based on a cost benefit analysis.

BB5277A439264D22BEC4703DFE45DF4E.description: Create scaled engineering drawings for a new product or system and make modification to increase optimization based on feedback.

ED76B3AD5AD249DCB34EA3D0671D284C.description: Use research to design and create a product or system that addresses a problem and make modifications based on input from potential consumers.

D96FC6CFD2104BEF9072BACD15CC0D83.description: Engineering design is a complex process in which creativity, content knowledge, research, and analysis are used to address local and global problems.Decisions on trade-offs involve systematic comparisons of all costs and benefits, and final steps that may involve redesigning for optimization.

24901CF49C4A4F6A9F54C8C0E8DD0F26.description: Collaboratively document and present design decisions in the development of complex programs.

F098570F84134E89AB9DA22BBEB4E4EB.description: Evaluate and refine computational artifacts to make them more usable and accessible.

1B7662E7F9924A12A72BE32CF39A8630.description: Collaboratively design and develop programs and artifacts for broad audiences by incorporating feedback from users.

B8126D66627F4C18A6449F445527A73A.description: Complex programs are developed, tested, and analyzed by teams drawing on the members' diverse strengths using a variety of resources, libraries, and tools.

123F68CD67E9474C91711B6B81C9C872.description: Create artifacts by using procedures within a program, combinations of data and procedures, or independent but interrelated programs.

59DFAAB67EAE476E8CB71F362BC4820D.description: Decompose problems into smaller components through systematic analysis, using constructs such as procedures, modules, and/or objects.

19D6797E18C54F9BB3A14DC3190CE45F.description: Complex programs are designed as a system of interacting modules, each with a specific role, coordinating for a common overall purpose. Modules allow for better management of complex tasks.

9B107FA795764B8F9EC71ACF597CD478.description: Design and iteratively develop computational artifacts for practical intent, personal expression, or to address a societal issue.

31B58C7BC64049F8AA90C0148B83F8A5.description: Select and combine control structures for a specific application based upon performance and readability, and identify trade-offs to justify the choice.

776CEB62A28A49C8A0EE1E3609B0DF79.description: Trade-offs related to implementation, readability, and program performance are considered when selecting and combining control structures.

8D554227783A4E99AA96F1A9C8ED50DD.description: Create generalized computational solutions using collections instead of repeatedly using simple variables.

3F8544D114434ADD8B0ACC8FCA6B1926.description: Programmers choose data structures to manage program complexity based on functionality, storage, and performance trade-offs.

8E9F1F5664B940A3B90FCB508B696887.description: Design algorithms to solve computational problems using a combination of original and existing algorithms.

D87994D859A841CA9685EEECD1F37626.description: Individuals evaluate and select algorithms based on performance, reusability, and ease of implementation.

AE1AE9CC84FF4702B288B403EC1D2FCA.description: Create and refine computational models to better represent the relationships among different elements of data collected from a phenomenon or process.

9336E286579F411B8EA884BAF5F800C5.description: The accuracy of predictions or inferences made from a computer model is affected by the amount quality, and diversity of data.

311773AE879047B39635933DAA848671.description: Create data visualizations from large data sets to summarize, communicate, and support different interpretations of real-world phenomena.

74AB23B01FD048F68760A4A9CEF24AF6.description: Large data sets can be transformed, generalized, simplified, and presented in different ways to influence how individuals interpret and understand the underlying information.

02A2F446CE594AAF9668B2AA61DE92B7.description: Explain the relationship between binary numbers and the storage and use of data in a computing device.

5E72AE9D31914411B0D277E2D4BA05F6.description: Translate between decimal numbers and binary numbers.

50C39EE1C191432CA24581E944D89DD8.description: Describe the trade-offs in how and where data is organized and stored.

DB4A739DE9C04DC5A37740399F3ABCCA.description: Choices individuals make about how and where data is organized and stored affects cost, speed, reliability, accessibility, privacy, and integrity.

F946E8E1CC1749FBA7F9B9098C01B2AA.description: Create interactive data visualizations using software tools to help others better understand real world phenomena, including climate change.

7353B7FE88934A5397BA9CB4395330C0.description: Individuals select digital tools and design automated processes to collect, transform, generalize, simplify, and present large data sets in different ways to influence how other people interpret and understand the underlying information.

DFCC843B76FC412891355C84207F6C00.description: Predict the potential impacts and implications of emerging technologies on larger social, economic, and political structures, using evidence from credible sources.

6E054D5E2DFB4032AE2EC8B2DF559B7B.description: Test and refine computational artifacts ot reduce bias and equity deficits

D4EF5B4797B24ED192AE864C3041B4A8.description: Evaluate the ways computing impacts personal, ethical, social, economic, and cultural practices.

2A7544F8C102426C88520158C365B851.description: The design and use of computing technologies and artifacts can positively or negatively affect equitable access to information and opportunities.

A06B4ABF6490451EAA6DEA737399C96B.description: Explain how decisions on methods to protect data are influenced by whether the data is at rest, in transit, or in use.

0CDA558C31E44409A1D0EB28C015391C.description: Explain how the needs of users and the sensitivity of data determine the level of security implemented.

3D5D20EB79DF465980DBD2EE79B475C5.description: Evaluate security measures to address various common security threats.

A33DF1A1824D4A61852EA2F851532F72.description: Network security depends on a combination of hardware, software, and practices that protect data while it is at rest, in transit, and in use.The needs of users and the sensitivity of data determine the elvel of security implemented. Advanced attacks take advantage of common security vulnerabilities.

5C1F68E3F83D40EFAC76BA496F519023.description: Evaluate the scalability and reliability of networks, by describing the relationship between routers, switches, servers, topology, and addressing.

00FE66F702A34DA99B75E3EE04672E23.description: The scalability and reliability of the Internet are enabled by the hierarchy and redundancy in networks.Network topology is determined by many characteristics.

A014394446E246AC92FA11547543DC1F.description: Develop guidelines that convey systematic troubleshooting strategies that others can use to identify and fix errors.

0ECECC20A22F4D1E8448FE2697B12D26.description: Successful troubleshooting of complex problems involves multiple approaches including research, analysis, reflection, interaction with peers, and drawing on past experiences.

BDE5141041E74E0A91DAE65B78A74BF8.description: Compare the functions of application software, system software, and hardware.

087DE291DE6D4F32A1545A6185F2639A.description: Model interactions between application software, system software, and hardware.

AFB5B294FBD6429F8DAF067FD30CC641.description: A computing system involves interaction among the user, hardware, application software, and system software.

4D34ABBDDD514FA1A06BE054D44B6EB6.description: Describe ways in which integrated systems hide underlying implementation details to simplify user experiences.

F139A68FC4CE483C8F3FBC8AE6C3A588.description: The usability, dependability, security, and accessibility of devices within integrated systems are important considerations in their design as they evolve.

historical contexts to deepen understanding

6C6A953A05184053B2D66E521C1062C2.description:

B77D1CE2B02D4B109DB6EE1AB29E09A5.description:
Identify the various types of resources that are available in the community and
online to assist individuals who struggle with alcohol, tobacco, and drug use/abuse (e.g.,
school nurse, counselor, peer leadership group).

CB4D1EE32F494F758C22DF732EA78216.description:
Demonstrate strategies for seeking assistance for someone impacted by an
individual who is struggling with the use/abuse of alcohol or drugs.

30AB96D6534A4F93825A8D7A4179DDD1.description:
Demonstrate effective refusal skills of alcohol, e-cigarettes, vaping products,
cannabis products, opioids, and other substances that can negatively impact health.

BF33BD21A89141B487394F60CF8E9099.description:
Identify signs and evaluate evidence that a person might have an alcohol,
tobacco, and/or drug use problem.

B71BF0799EA14A539F7B0E24912F49B9.description:
Differentiate between drug use, misuse, abuse, and, prescription and illicit
drugs.

3246BBBB0C03402BBA84C7D3644CFF9B.description:
Describe the behaviors of people who struggle with the use of alcohol and drugs
and identify the type of assistance that is available.

E55AB564C3A14C9EAC9381435016BA8A.description:
Describe health concerns associated with e-cigarettes, vaping products,
inhalants, alcohol, opioids and other drugs, and non-prescribed cannabis products.

84C71CF2D441435D825F263C4E0F9B49.description:
Identify products that contain alcohol, tobacco, and drugs and explain potential
unhealthy effects (e.g., substance disorder, cancer).

36E1CE41C5994EE98D2FE71E9DD39AA3.description:
Examine how mental health can impact one’s wellness (e.g., depression,
anxiety, stress, phobias).

A03CEF3466BF41C7A1486A1E5ED4B567.description:
Describe how to prevent the spread of communicable and infection diseases
and conditions (e.g., Lyme Disease, influenza)

C7E0FE9B6B4A40E69480E7E57BC25CC9.description:
Identify conditions that may keep the human body from working properly,
and the ways in which the body responds.

5E012A3CF4EE43008338D02DC877897D.description:
Identify strategies a person could use to call attention to or leave an
uncomfortable or dangerous situation, including bullying, teasing, teen dating violence,
sexual harassment, sexual assault, and sexual abuse.

149EF33CF40448C58FDD978DF835C689.description:
Communicate personal boundaries and demonstrate ways to respect other
people’s personal boundaries.

694386B90AE54010B617AED0969FCD66.description: Develop strategies to safely communicate through digital media with respect.

A76283CDBD474EFE9949546905396C8B.description:
Examine the impact of unsafe behaviors when traveling in motor vehicles and
when using other modes of transportation.

7A574657F808487E83FC3E50E8DD11ED.description:
Demonstrate first aid procedures for choking, bleeding, burns, poisoning, and
stroke (F.A.S.T.).

6913F91934CC4E03BF5DEC17AD1CA68E.description:
Develop strategies to reduce the risk of injuries at home, school, and in the
community.

872C99E722B04FCB81DDD31474E116B2.description:
Develop a plan to attain a personal nutrition health goal that addresses strengths,
needs, and culture.

C9EDB6DB60CA4D6F93BBF3D2C714D05F.description: Create a healthy meal based on nutritional content, value, calories, and cost.

3C15A833C5E94486B87F687177EE7307.description:
Explain how healthy eating provides energy, helps to maintain healthy weight,
lowers risk of disease, and keeps body systems functioning effectively.

9ABC24122FD140D2BEA8874F18B37FFA.description:
Describe how community resources could be used to support participation in a
variety of physical activities, sports and wellness.

6AC69E0CA58644C58E310F203123C3A9.description:
Perform and increase the range of motion in dynamic stretching and breathing
exercises (e.g., dynamic cardiovascular warm-up exercises, martial arts, aerobics, yoga).

81EC439213164E5198874EE1E60B986F.description:
Proactively engage in movement and physical activity for enjoyment individually
or with others.

2465DD069CD34B02BAD8654BF4131E98.description:
Develop a movement vocabulary that is flexible and adaptable for personal
physical activity and wellness.

0BEADFE8204E487FA4DF01E3CA898123.description:
Explain the need to engage in physical activities on a voluntary basis for
emotional and physical enjoyment.

4B5079811BA6494C94F4CAD8B351806C.description:
Determine how different factors influence personal fitness and other healthy
lifestyle choices (e.g., heredity, physical activity, nutrition, sleep, technology)

0052723DADE04574975FD8624C883F01.description:
Develop a short term and/or a long-term health-related fitness goal (e.g.,
cardiorespiratory endurance 'heart & lungs', muscular strength, muscular endurance,
flexibility, body composition, nutrition) to evaluate personal health

DD9895228C5C4933A2047C8FD5EBCCBA.description:
Participate in moderate to vigorous age-appropriate physical fitness activities and
build the skills that address each component of health-related fitness (e.g., endurance, strength,
speed, agility, flexibility, balance).

BB642F870F854B0DA16D688A418BEF8D.description: Accept and respect others of all skill levels and abilities during participation.

D67B115206904732BE20A7CDA32F0A40.description:
Identify the physical, social, emotional, and intellectual benefits of regular physical
activity that effect personal health.

2932BC6268974F0F8AECB33FF4DE51C7.description:
Apply specific rules, strategies, and procedures for specific physical activity,
games, and sports in a safe active environment.

E05BA948111B48CCBC5AE20F3B001E2E.description:
Execute appropriate behaviors and etiquette while participating as a player and
viewing as an observer during physical activity, games, and other events, contributes to a safe
environment.

DD7B4E72FCAB416A8A393279438C0DD9.description:
Correct movement skills and analyze concepts in response to external feedback
and self-evaluation with understanding and demonstrating how the change improves
performance.

53E4A3EF7F784A0C811169D5941FEA26.description:
Develop the necessary body control to improve stability and balance during
movement and physical activity.

56B54B24770D4EFA9D8235C1ED61A09E.description:
Demonstrate and perform movement skills with developmentally appropriate
control in isolated settings (e.g., skill practice) and applied settings (e.g., games, sports, dance,
recreational activities).

A9474324DBD340F384E0911F1E44B228.description:
Explain and demonstrate movement sequences, individually and with others, in
response to various tempos, rhythms, and musical styles.

E84A25468CE248ABBDA80FA3BD8E4D43.description:
Demonstrate body management skills and control when moving in relation to
others, objects, and boundaries in personal and general space (e.g., coordination, balance,
flexibility, agility).

78B94DF63E56436FAA2B1A4A6D084845.description:
Describe strategies that are useful for individuals who are feeling sadness,
anger, anxiety, or stress.

C2B7E1A589FB47CBBCB6C699D25E877D.description:
Individuals will benefit from an awareness of
coping strategies that can be used when
facing difficult situations.

38D9F29FFF234DACB5EB4E71401EEE54.description:
Describe how business, non-profit organizations, and individuals can work
cooperatively to address health problems that are affected by global issues, including climate
change

968B94333FC04324A7BC6077300EEF4B.description:
Identify health services and resources available and determine how each assist
in addressing needs and emergencies in a school and in the community (e.g., counselors,
medical professionals).

320E9298989E4E2FA2AFF0A489B99F09.description:
Community professionals and school
personnel are available to assist and address
health emergencies as well as provide reliable
information.

C692F5AD8E6E423695A886C2521C40B4.description:
Define teasing, harassment and bullying and provide examples of inappropriate
behaviors that are harmful to others.

5743DE9E2CF04FD7990D4DC4CD1C1B5D.description:
Describe the characteristics of healthy versus unhealthy relationships among
friends and with family members.

983E3AE11C8945C2B7860ED837C6DCFA.description:
People in healthy relationships share thoughts
and feelings, as well as mutual respect.

8B4FF836472D44FC95E24176204ECB55.description:
Explain the importance of communication with family members, caregivers and
other trusted adults about a variety of topics.

5FB077E464974236803D9CD51DD54453.description:
Describe how families can share common values, offer emotional support, and
set boundaries and limits.

656CCEA01C2B430BBDCF812E3069C55D.description:
Family members impact the development of
their children physically, socially and
emotionally.

1058C79C2BE646768874F5098D7C37B1.description:
Demonstrate ways to promote dignity and respect for all people (e.g. sexual
orientation, gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, socio-economic status, differing
ability, immigration status, family configuration).

BCC72FE8E27F41C290DE4D8D8A19EC83.description: Differentiate between sexual orientation and gender identity.

FEDFE512613741C7BFA0F88D735858DF.description: Describe gender-role stereotypes and their potential impact on self and others

355F22A9999C4BD1842C0C03E23B9954.description:
All individuals should feel welcome and
included regardless of their gender, gender
expression, or sexual orientation.

2A83B7E9E9E24B638FFE293C4B0D8525.description:
Identify behaviors that help to deal with difficult situations that can occur at
home, in school, and/or in the community and where to go for assistance.

44DB99482D8740B682C6547A1E9E97AD.description:
Identify different feelings and emotions that people may experience and how they
might express these emotions (e.g., anger, fear, happiness, sadness, hopelessness, anxiety).

C6D82FA406794B4CA3472E61190AB37B.description:
Resiliency and coping practices influence an
individual’s ability to respond positively to
everyday challenges and difficult situations.

D181CA4BEB57495CBFA2A3574BA7920F.description:
Explain how to cope with rejection, loss, difficult learning situations and/or
separation from family or others.

FBEE0CF0F32948A1AF007B50C2966055.description:
Discuss the impact of one’s feelings and thoughts that lead to healthy and unhealthy
behaviors.

A20B7C9CFFD84DAF889C8F3F0643381D.description:
Self-management skills impact an
individual’s ability to recognize, cope, and
express emotions about difficult events.

97F39CCA461848EF8187986DFD1E5E04.description: Explain the range of ways pregnancy can occur (e.g., IVF, surrogacy).

88991E746BAE4E828DDC051937EA060A.description: Explain the relationship between sexual intercourse and human reproduction.

7684BCE73A0C4487B604A395A12AD6BF.description:
Pregnancy can be achieved through a variety of
methods.

61D5FCD7EA9D464C9FD035880425030F.description:
Identify trusted adults, including family members, caregivers, school staff, and
health care professionals, whom students can talk to about relationships and ask questions
about puberty and adolescent health.

57A39969142A4FEFA4B08F3D5F3FE2C7.description:
Explain common human sexual development and the role of hormones (e.g.,
romantic and sexual feelings, masturbation, mood swings, timing of pubertal onset).

578BE6DB73E0434E904C0A304095C9A4.description:
Explain the physical, social, and emotional changes that occur during puberty
and adolescence and why the onset and progression of puberty can vary.

6D99B17A1EB84368A4405772541DCF6E.description:
Examine how the body changes during puberty and how these changes
influence personal self-care.

9047089C6FF84AC7A52B7794DC8564C0.description:
Puberty is a time of physical, social, and
emotional changes.

B5423765B18B42C1ADF9A0CDAE73866C.description:
Identify effective personal health strategies and behaviors that reduce illness,
prevent injuries, and maintain or enhance one’s wellness (e.g., adequate sleep, balanced
nutrition, ergonomics, regular physical activity).

5E1F591980B944FB9658B367D5910169.description:
Health is influenced by the interaction of body
systems.

create products.

06D51E4BCA4C4DDB86EF5D489BF483B8.description: Synthesize knowledge of social, cultural, historical, and personal life with art- making approaches to create meaningful works of art or design.

C9711D6E533F43CBBD3DC6FF116E0186.description: Utilize inquiry methods of observation, research and experimentation to explore other subjects through artmaking

BDB65E17A0344B19A32CBC7CFD7B7A94.description: Document the process of developing ideas from early stages to fully elaborated ideas.

145CD84569AB4A2E9A97E47FE6B16D25.description: Synthesizing and relating knowledge and personal experiences to create products.

0DE0734307DC425DB95EF6576881176B.description: Construct evaluations of a work of art or collection of works based on differing sets of criteria.

454751CE7DC94B9A8A5B7D642ACCBC2B.description: Determine the relevance of criteria used by others to evaluate a work of art or collection of works.

52D865B19DE948F1A68127E2364CD670.description: Establish relevant criteria in order to evaluate a work of art or collection of works.

91BCA8779DD44A96BFB3CDBCDCD6D334.description:
Analyze differing interpretations of an artwork or collection of works in order to
 select and defend a plausible critical analysis.

44565EFEF4E0414499800B4F107258D3.description:
Identify types of contextual information useful in the process of constructing
 interpretations of an artwork or collection of works.

484D793EB7BC47B08AF1AF0DA2BFC129.description: Interpret an artwork or collection of works, supported by relevant and sufficient evidence found in the work and its various contexts.

E2C14A69B92142E98EEC571A79EBB1C7.description: Determine the commonalities within a group of artists or visual arts attributed to a particular type of art, timeframe, or culture

BB966622920D48D09595E99587AB6624.description:
Analyze how responses to art develop over time based on knowledge of and
 experience with art and life.

B706D2FECF3E4FA0984594335FA4BBD9.description:
Evaluate the effectiveness of visual artworks to influence ideas, feelings, and
 behaviors of specific audiences.

6B76C38541D046B7BB0547403CAF50DE.description:
Recognize and describe personal aesthetic and empathetic responses to the natural
 world and constructed environments.

392D38FD2CDE46E1B04446D106A78F4B.description:
Analyze how one's understanding of the world is affected by experiencing visual
arts.

2F969E19FD9C46A88EF25FD64A8DF18A.description:
Hypothesize ways in which art influences perception and understanding of human
experiences.

A5A667191F89458B9CCE671FD8281A55.description: Curate a collection of objects, artifacts or artwork to impact the viewer's understanding of social, cultural and/or political experiences.

CBE97A0A5DE24CB2BB6B93001B43DA39.description:
Make, explain and justify connections between artists or artwork and social, cultural
 and political history.

F6091DC3D8AF4C55BEA75E3E5FF84F1E.description:
Analyze and describe the impact that an exhibition or collection has on personal
 awareness of social, cultural or political beliefs and understandings

15174133DEB64FAB997190BA3123884D.description: Investigate, compare and contrast methods for preserving and protecting art.

479D9C776DC1497EADF88C0E2E070B07.description: Evaluate, select and apply methods or processes appropriate to display artwork in specific place

5BEB77854D83471CAC0C18DB079331B1.description: Analyze and evaluate the reasons and ways an exhibition is presented.

2DB83A48216143ADAD8FB954B84BBB57.description: Developing and refining techniques and models or steps needed to create products.

5062B334F46147F7B05C436550543A2A.description: Critique, justify and present choices in the process of analyzing, selecting, curating, and presenting artwork for a specific exhibit or event.

BB7C50E57DF54C65BC9541F15AA9049D.description: Analyze, select and critique personal artwork for a collection or portfolio presentation.

A24999CE8DE44838BD70FA0C54000452.description: Analyze, select and curate artifacts and/or artworks for presentation and preservation.

17F4E8962CB94FD2B905EB7425093703.description: Reflect on, re-engage, revise and refine works of art or design considering relevant traditional and contemporary criteria as well as personal artistic vision.

BCD86065586642D0A5FA1E6651E422C1.description: Engage in constructive critique with peers, then reflect on, re- engage, revise, and refine works of art and design in response to personal artistic vision.

26A88423D7C641168E201274EB18B16F.description: Apply relevant criteria from traditional and contemporary cultural contexts to examine, reflect on and plan revisions for works of art and design in progress.

AA69216AB28548DDB40AE7E20F2A2BB4.description: Demonstrate in works of art or design how visual and material culture defines, shapes, enhances, inhibits, and/or empowers peoples' lives

E822491D00274FE5BBEB8527FC64BC2C.description:
Demonstrate understanding of the importance of balancing freedom and
 responsibility in the use of images, materials, tools and equipment in the creation and circulation of
 creative work.

D2421A8F81A34107A9D5063405747FEC.description:
Experiment, plan and make multiple works of art and design that explore a
 personally meaningful theme, idea, or concept.

795401B0E44747E5869F103CCBAACCBE.description: Redesign an object, system, place, or design in response to contemporary issues.

91B42886BFE046B8B2FDB71BB48C845B.description: Demonstrate awareness of ethical implications of making and distributing creative work.

161893A33A7E4674BC0B9FA14DF2227F.description:
Through experimentation, practice and persistence, demonstrate acquisition of skills
 and knowledge in a chosen art form.

557CDBA8C91F47049315199099DF4C61.description:
Collaboratively develop a proposal for an installation, artwork, or space design that
 transforms the perception and experience of a particular place.

207BFCD2792F49BC973FADBBE444836B.description:
Explain how traditional and non-traditional materials may impact human health and
 the environment, and demonstrate safe handling of materials, tools and equipment.

F548F5E7C7BD4A85AA723FC3597D800F.description: Engage in making a work of art or design without having a preconceived plan.

86B4F2368C064589A8F777D5D643FD4C.description: Choose from a range of materials and methods of traditional and contemporary artistic practices, following or breaking established conventions, to plan the making of multiple works of art and design based on a theme, idea or concept.

BC4C13B90A5B4C989FB11593B1666E21.description: Visualize and generate art and design that can affect social change.

9B75D413F44F4DFFB194F1AF71AF6700.description:
Choose from a range of materials and methods of traditional and contemporary
 artistic practices to plan works of art and design.

A373962F24FA41B2AC92E0F171FAC375.description:
Individually and collaboratively formulate new creative problems based on student’s
existing artwork.

CA8A702BF6A44E66B5315982B3A14A52.description:
Shape an artistic investigation of an aspect of present-day life using a contemporary
 practice of art and design.

DC4F42B438A144EA8E48BC45C9C37515.description: Use multiple approaches to begin creative endeavors.

Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide
requested detail or clarification.

E8463DE7F7C341919E607701504D42B7.description:
Use multimedia; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences
when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

AD6D9473709C48C78F8661777472685F.description:
Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details,
speaking audibly in coherent sentences.

98E6F4B6CCE64ECC9B504E1C56E65520.description:
Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather
additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

83D4F5FA620741DCBB4EDE8E5FBC4E11.description:
Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally
or through other media.

D55562C4963D4AAF8AD5F55F0F8C8D7F.description:
Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under
discussion.

EEF3E02D1B484A7FB743BEEFFCB7A093.description:
Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their explicit comments to the remarks of
others.

5EC171C5C2FB4700B8CF34EDE34BF498.description:
Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening
to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

A2AFB98DD28E4C83BCF7F99FA7A874E5.description:
Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts
with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

C16EB0E51DD446BEA8D52D79B733A506.description:
Engage in both collaborative and independent writing tasks regularly, including extended and
shorter time frames.

7E87AC041F4B473BBB663135ACEEF1A8.description:
Prioritize information provided by different sources on the same topic while gathering ideas
and planning to write about a topic.

97CAA90BC7E44FB4BE17F8DB0A091760.description:
Generate questions about a topic and locate related information from a reference source to
obtain information on that topic through shared and independent research.

2EB8B1150AF542D9A96CE9808EF8606C.description: With feedback and digital or print tools such as a primary dictionary, find and correct errors.

0B25282D9D5B45A8BFEEB471B271C98D.description: Participate in self-evaluation of written work.

522D281E54F34B3D848D899C985A696C.description: Identify audience and purpose before writing.

AF8B6EE9394A4855B5534A620F540C97.description:
With guidance and support from adults and peers, develop and strengthen writing as needed
by planning, revising and editing.

4B2A6480070B496AA13F17458F1D70B7.description: Provide a conclusion or sense of closure related to the narrated experiences or events.

3672B7E59FCD4E1E91682EAB4454206E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experience and events.

Provide dialogue and description of experiences and events and/or show the responses of
characters to situations.

A957D0DCF9DE43D7845B01FA2C82496D.description:
Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing characters; organize an event
sequence.

CF81501A4ECA4EA39431685A88A67EA4.description: Write narratives based on real or imagined experiences or events with basic story elements.

95FF6A2E55BE4799ABDAD135EA3353EB.description:
Develop a topic with facts definitions, concrete details, text evidence, or other information
and examples related to the topic.

AE417278AF1D4E9486D51124556FFD86.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information.

9051A7C0A4FB41E4B35802F2798CCCBC.description:
Support the opinion with facts, definitions, concrete details, text evidence, or other
information and examples related to the topic.

9442362254224165AAE25E72FEA184F0.description:
With prompts and support, write opinion pieces to present an idea with reasons or
information.

AF8E5DCD098143AEBBC0BC88E95F7EAF.description:
Compare and contrast two informational versions of the same idea or topic by different
authors or authors from different cultures.

1FBBBFE5654B41E0954AA542759D7753.description:
Compare and contrast literary versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different
authors or from different cultures.

506CAF582F2F4872A7B2371B19A42573.description:
Describe and identify the logical connections of how reasons support specific points the
author makes in a text.

1B36E2B0944B47D196C240DDEEF48B0E.description:
Explain how specific illustrations and images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works)
contribute to and clarify a text.

5E3821A2C4BB47D9B4BCA968E4575A3D.description:
With prompting and support, use information gained from the illustrations and words in a
print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.

1EAE65E90C0048A284494211B6D9BDC1.description:
Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author seeks to explore, answer,
explain, or describe.

FA3EF4228D3A4B228D3A236F0CA582D3.description:
Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a
different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

945B277345344FDD98B7E5D694AA4CAC.description:
Describe the overall structure of a text and effectively use various text features (e.g., graphs,
charts, images, captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate
key facts or information.

00DD22C0286C4EF3BCD02C8F7567FC75.description:
Describe the overall structure of a text, including describing how the beginning introduces the
story and the ending concludes the action, identifying how each successive part builds on earlier
sections.

5749A9F2B64D49E4BA1E99FD90C8F6D9.description:
Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or
steps in a sequence within a text.

9E5F6EDAE89B4378BEB03D27B3D01997.description:
Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges using key details
within a text.

AA9A3C16FAB248E2A2F05CF7FC46BC07.description:
Recount a text in oral and written form and determine main topic (in multi-paragraph
informational text, focusing on specific paragraphs).

C589FBEB14EF4A2890E9BD621490D032.description:
Recount a text in oral and written form and determine central message (in literary texts, e.g.
fables and folktales from diverse cultures) .

2400870E81D944F7A400551A99246E93.description:
Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of key details in an informational
text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

44CB1CF9DF4B4CA88AC8299A5ECEE49F.description:
Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of key details in a literary text,
referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

C22F2AE18F3C486EA357490C99762B63.description:
Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines)
supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.

C0322317BF324A3CAA7FF4F65DA0BDDE.description:
Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and
closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

826AC512E61B4A1D95EF16134370EF2C.description:
Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are
spicy or juicy).

19D32D8F3033413EA813CBC7D170314E.description:
Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word
meanings.

0B33A570646E486FBA18ADAAA9BBCFC3.description:
Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the
meaning of words and phrases.

B19D2C44543F4FB785B360376CF555CD.description:
Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound
words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

F8D0D52CC93F42FC8D7A463AAB6DBB43.description:
Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root
(e.g., addition, additional).

63C8310D86AC4ED79CF3EE953B8F25BB.description:
Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known
word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).

BA2E3BB95AF64FF0A73F6C78CD57BAC1.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

B06AB1164EBD4A13AB5F102BAE913F42.description:

on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

CC4F3745635E457A8E2D8A805AE95A82.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

F93E220FDC6E40178980E0E7320407F3.description:
Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and
responding to texts.

18FFD523F792446784786E1C3FEA03CF.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

6BCC746779024C3F94A690EBD23D0A5E.description: With assistance, link sentences into a simple, cohesive paragraph with a main idea.

CD7D97AFE16341A3A5514CE1C4020DC8.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

E5D830BED5794883B180246A0182E2DA.description:
Punctuate dates, abbreviations, greetings and closings, initials, important words in a title,
and items in a list.

51C45BE5363441B5BE06533977364D7F.description:

past, present, and future tenses.

9CB2E6C0E3944E379E538643359B53C0.description: Supply adjectives in noun phrases to make them more precise or engaging.

9A5D711645C24581B2DB16F31ADAE07F.description: Capitalize holidays, product names and geographic names.

0A2BDBFF49A641D790B916925BF17412.description:
With modeling or prompting, separate run-on sentences and identify fragments, supplying a
subject or predicate as necessary.

EC3064D0DD0E4AC3AD994D14BEBF27CF.description:
Demonstrate command and use of the conventions of writing including those listed under
grade one foundational skills.

6238F47D76604243BEAD4B442BA00236.description:
Most often used words in English:
i. Irregular words (against, many, enough, does).
ii. Pattern-based words (which, kind, have).

C4B97251E31A466E8D947C2E3F1560ED.description:
Words with suffixes that require:
i. consonant doubling (penning, slimmed).
ii. dropping silent-e (smiled, paving).

E57B127D06BB41BC85EE46BAFAF52D67.description:
Regular two- and three-syllable words that:
i. Combine closed, open, vowel team, vowel –r and CVe syllables (compete; robot;
violet; understand).
ii. Are compounds comprising familiar parts (houseboat; yellowtail).
iii. Include the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes (un, re, en; -ful, -ment,
-less).

669356C47DB742C1B82F406BB9B7FF3B.description:
Regular, single-syllable words that include:
i. Position-based patterns (ch, -tch; k, -ck; -ge, -dge).
ii. Complex consonant blends (scr, str, squ).
iii. Less common vowel teams for long vowels (ow, oo, au, ou, ue).
iv. Vowel-r combinations (turn, star, third, four/for).
v. Contractions (we’ll; I’m; they’ve; don’t).
vi. Homophones (bear, bare; past, passed).
vii. Plurals and possessives (its, it’s).

Write the most common graphemes (letters or letter groups) for each phoneme, for
example:
i. Consonants: /s/ = s, ss, ce, ci, cy; /f/ = f, ff, ph; /k/ = c, k, -ckii. Vowels: /ō/ = o, oe, oa, ow; /ā/ = a, a_e, ai, ay, eigh.

8A6812F426CF4CE4A1C50B2DF09C315F.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of writing.

3CF515B5D63A4A06AB2052A105DB80CD.description:
Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as
necessary.

F8BD6FBC694B462889982AB3DD279857.description: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

EC0E728775514D978A4A965CE9D12DD1.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

11096FBB145A4187B9D0323C44966810.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

4C313B3111D2430DAF7F36B5FF3BDEFC.description: Identify the parts of high-frequency words that are regular and the parts that are irregular.

D63889CB41784B24B55A73F31CEE6B4C.description:

0D3B0B6320B04512B1FC5615F697BE62.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

1BB9F47C1F9248DC9349399984776D05.description: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

B6A9C5C5B7834A58BC37805853D0174B.description: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.

BC54A8D2A43B43CB8124AC621C084247.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for common vowel teams.

E8A37EFA71614AA3A4283AD7C2B77054.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

6A25932DDE674EDD880C95492E8A9546.description:

828757E931CD414FA5870608F3488C11.description:
Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in

5776780BE3FF4F7CB8658394800508B1.description:

316B89F0BAF54C46BCDFD91641BA5B1A.description:

Compare and contrast the authors’ approaches across two or more literary texts within the

Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text,

Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs,
diagrams, timelines, animations, or interactive elements on web pages) and explain how the information

58DF261181464975A0018785885A62C5.description:
Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a
text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

8F99A0F6DC274ACC8B6FA90B2B72C3A8.description:
Describe how a narrator’s or speaker’s point of view influences how events are described, and

1DB0243FA4944825810099FDD5A56374.description:
Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect,

1FDD387838224C1785424351AB9BA65F.description:

structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

C77C149BB5B3441AA96EEBC08D938BDD.description:
Analyze the impact of two or more individuals and events throughout the course of a text,
explaining the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts

A195578E28AA47149FDC2B170D7B061D.description:
Analyze the impact of two or more individuals and events throughout the course of a text,
comparing and contrasting two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on

Determine the central idea of an informational text and explain how it is supported by key

F7EE766D4657463CA9229E513D4DBB11.description:

CE9F78F065AB481D85C9AB2AB2B4C019.description:
Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to

6B395C5C947F440281DF7D0E7115D680.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

4B78D70F624A4AC4A26F54D94C9CA720.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

F5DF82581BA4407689E562AE7159CA98.description:
Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word
meanings.

12ED3C6558D3482E8833705971D51C98.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and
digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words
and phrases.

8C18951589904D8CA750846E46EF6FD4.description:
Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of
a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

8771309D1F5F4C3780D44FD9A905736E.description:
Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the
meaning of a word or phrase.

63D4ECB0BFED40639F9407291264E275.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning academic and
domain-specific words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range
of strategies.

99A72D1E19FE4DFBA11CF8EBB5C9D595.description:
Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories,
dramas, or poems.

275D970B683C4FEB8BE20A2BF84A90FC.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

EDE7D69B4A574F07829C9B683B993D03.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words
and phrases.

68D709DE0BA8412F8A6D06FAF97CA2EC.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

08BD2B6A39EB4D0D8501117D75026155.description: Spell grade appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

F5DCEBDE3D734E5AB0FF474CAD0B3EEB.description:
Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence; use a
comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It’s true, isn’t it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that
you, Emma?).

1B24938F32DE4162815357B1FCB7CFAA.description: Use punctuation to separate items in a series; use commas in a series of phrases or clauses.

E109ED5D954A40B1929E482863C520B9.description: Use idiomatic language and choose words for effect; use punctuating for meaning and effect.

55C27841EA0C4DE6BA9E33F65C206E86.description: Ensure agreement between subject and verb and between pronoun and antecedent.

1DB2313406B148A0B1C0C1C95FA24744.description:
Maintain consistency in verb tense; place phrases and clauses; choose between adjectives
and adverbs.

44A55215D9F84848945C3E2D036CB5EE.description: Avoid fragments, run-ons and rambling sentences, and comma splices.

6B93626E90264F1D8EA88FA0A063DD44.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of writing, including those listed under grade four
foundational skills.

8EA30192B994414DA32141F86F061429.description:
Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as
necessary.

8F4BD1512136464DB3B5A4CA1CAA0074.description: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

7683FC4C57F5415CBB0DE5D3A933DF4B.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

51A51E8D03D04C89834E83D977337ADD.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

when indicated or appropriate.

5889B48C00654ABAA7D28BD1A26CB139.description:
Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in
presentations to clarify information.

Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts,

adequate volume, and clear pronunciation).

B839F0B471D74DBAA967FF4BDC3BB2FF.description:
Deconstruct a speaker’s argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported
by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

CBBEB8011DD44D2ABE1A6F6F2398D2C5.description:
Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively,
orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.

8BB1BA6E20E34F72891004439BE89F45.description:
Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives
through reflection and paraphrasing.

B7E8C5A066C14498A0615BBA1FC6FCD2.description:
Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments
that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

4C340A4E08794AC280F4AFA9562C5F28.description:
Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual
roles as needed.

that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on

Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and
teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others’ ideas and
expressing their own clearly.

BADFE17508C449C68FC8E15B65728B07.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, metacognition/self-correction, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of

9E3B7DF79AF840C9B3053E614E420A8C.description:

each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and
providing basic bibliographic information for sources.

0214C7065E834D37B579D53635B34FB0.description:
Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and
refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

09EF4C2A18FC4D6F953C3DD2025F42A6.description:

needed by planning; flexibly making editing and revision choices; sustaining effort to fit composition

36B524E029404002B382EE62EC586E95.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

8F81AA52FF62400EB34BF3E5A1E768C4.description:
Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey

039733DA83EF4331AE805D1EAD24C69E.description:
Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts
from one time frame or setting to another.

A4740A5132A441A1A4187B665FD82FF0.description:
Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences,
events, and/or characters.

C9E02FBEA0054A318FD6EA372B441A78.description:

75D51D51261342B1BB5B59E4FC2FDCB8.description:
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique,
relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

9C1E9DE045D5494F986B893322958192.description:
Provide a concluding statement or section (e.g., sentence, part of a paragraph, paragraph, or
multiple paragraphs) that follows from and supports the information or explanation
presented.

8B1F9D381FBA417A92C05CDC02C0AA96.description: Acknowledge and attempt a formal/academic style, approach, and form.

6A5C609E64C144FD9113BB9C78C38B54.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other
information and examples.

74698E548ECD44E5AC7BAEA1EA383263.description:
Introduce a topic and organize ideas, concepts, and information, using text structures (e.g.,
definition, classification, comparison/contrast, cause/effect, etc.) and text features (e.g.,
headings, graphics, and multimedia) when useful to aid in comprehension.

0A1A1E17973C439DBA611BAFF654FC73.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts (including the narration of historical events, scientific
procedures/ experiments, or technical processes) to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and
information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

199BAECA203B4F03AFD085113445A98D.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.

77976058495D4453AFD923017E3DDF60.description: Establish and maintain a formal/academic style, approach, and form.

Use words, phrases, and clauses to link and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons
and evidence.

7C75AFBCEFF04ECE9D086A11BC99EA78.description:
Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence, that
demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

7B0E85AC351F4E9E87C07607215E3AB5.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

42CA68AD812F48CBA77DEA4675A22B93.description:
Write arguments on discipline-specific content (e.g., social studies, science, math, technical
subjects, English/Language Arts) to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

EF72863E0C9A43F8A6C2B6AA986239B6.description:
Compare and contrast informational texts in different forms, by different authors, or from
different genres (e.g., a memoir written by and a biography on the same person, historical novels and
primary source documents, infographics and scientific journals) in terms of their approaches to similar
themes and topics.

3039C53A177B49D3A983EA8D60781D90.description:
Compare and contrast literary texts in different forms, by different authors, or from different
genres (e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and primary source documents, scientific journals and
fantasy stories) in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.

D262D3034E22485286A9B81D62D64725.description:
Trace the development of and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text,
distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

B1FF06FC39CC47A1B2077BCAF244E548.description:
Integrate information when presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually,
quantitatively) to develop a coherent understanding of a topic or issue.

A9C34AEB6FA34CDF9ED44766F1EE6EDB.description:
Compare and contrast information or texts to develop a coherent understanding of a theme,
topic, or issue when reading a story, drama, or poem to listening to or viewing an audio, video, or live
version of the text.

D978B45A970047EE8708199A7121E330.description:
Identify author’s purpose perspective or potential bias in a text and explain the impact on the
reader’s interpretation.

54A2B8279FB649E7871509720375C5B3.description:
Determine how an author conveys or develops perspective in a text (through the narrator or
speaker when appropriate).

0B0F86272E1A4F6581525AB68D1FB620.description:
Use text structures (e.g., cause-effect, problem-solution), search tools, and genre features (e.g.,
graphics, captions, indexes) to locate and integrate information.

B1869BADCD294CF18073BD7D30AE59D2.description:
Analyze how a particular piece (e.g., sentence, chapter, scene, stanza, or section) fits into the
overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas, theme, setting, or plot.

9593D5F21E6E4319A463404E53D05FBE.description:
Analyze how a particular text’s (e.g., article, brochure, technical manual, procedural text)

0BF71AA473174207B38F1BCA47535634.description:
Describe how a particular text’s structure unfolds in a series of episodes and use textual
evidence to describe how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.

0995684D54C144EABA131C921EE58FAA.description:
Determine the central idea of an informational text and explain how it is supported by key
details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

7EC039190E0A4815B807653DD1D4E167.description:
Determine the theme of a literary text (e.g., stories, plays or poetry) and explain how it is
supported by key details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

3DA3958B0E334DDBB7FF1E67CE32FEB7.description:
Cite textual evidence and make relevant connections to support analysis of what an
informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

356723129DDE4D43821F810C2E6527BA.description:
Cite textual evidence and make relevant connections to support analysis of what a literary text
says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

AD108C38E8134904A1F77A12DDCB3E80.description:

(definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

4612DD429F6243F286BC463D39B895CC.description: Analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

3619FEF6FE824588883BD494E6C1D9E0.description:
Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole,
item/category) to better understand each of the words.

5EFCE8B513D449948E39E014C685D224.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

E854F59E30554919BCF4B272745880D8.description:
Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word
meanings.

454680D06E4D4F85A6792FF8B42A535D.description:
Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking
the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

6B6549FCC80E408C8454206DC270C56D.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and
digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its

5D86602A71514338AFA14D6982019B0E.description:
Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a
word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

9C835595CA3843968729873BDCAE0A3D.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used, including figurative,
connotative, and technical meanings.

6899F3B1C5984E16B703977D3F7C75AA.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word’s position or
function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

56774B616E2F43DE9AC81952904DE87A.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based
on grade 6 reading and content, including technical meanings, choosing flexibly from a range of
strategies.

DBDF6327C37F4E0C955E25DE126C2954.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

1F878FD8C231487ABAF1B615298ABEDB.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning (syntax), reader/listener interest, and style/voice.

0F6DE1E890FB4E65835D159E1BE3C0D1.description:
Gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to
comprehension or expression.

6C4B10D908294AFEAA0194734EFA5094.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words
and phrases.

48267C37C62A45CA91E1A36BEF0A4D17.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

2FAAA14EAAF042F6928384B0334A40F4.description:
Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive and parenthetical
elements.

E3CDD5A3007741C9B0B62C627CB1C563.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

5E1D36ED982B49158657049C3BCA8D8E.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

68601F00EAF54E87A219A4989F057890.description:
Demonstrate command of the system and structure of the English language when writing or
speaking.

Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to
create a coherent whole.

DA2F45E1D9494C9A9A32751BEF6725BE.description:
Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple
plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

380078D16F524F6FA90943F565A28ED6.description:
Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation,
establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or
characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

3463C0C96BAB4484AA84BBE99EE96DB3.description:
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective
technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

1594ECB6BF544891AD7E22B3C4D59F17.description:
Provide a concluding paragraph or section that supports the information or explanation
presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

8962A6BE7B0F4E9484B50607A7C0070C.description:
Establish and maintain a style and tone appropriate to the audience and purpose (e.g.,
formal and objective for academic writing) while attending to the norms and
conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

748F0647107E4566AF469581B26090CC.description:
Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the
topic.

CE7797262A63461EA71BB82AD1267B6B.description:
Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important

DC50173D1E024C37A8C88D185A66016B.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts (including the narration of historical events, scientific

58318D46D2FE410BB40508CFF7FEC443.description:
Establish and maintain a style and tone appropriate to the audience and purpose (e.g.,
formal and objective for academic writing) while attending to the norms and

64EA4D9346BE461095239E5423618AED.description:
Use transitions (e.g., words, phrases, clauses) to link the major sections of the text,

Develop claim(s) and counterclaims using sound reasoning, supplying data and evidence

knowledge level and concerns.

7D4C195B6CC84BDE8D821FAFBE263A98.description:
Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims,

Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid

Analyze and reflect on (e.g., practical knowledge, historical/cultural context, and
background knowledge) seminal and informational text of historical and scientific significance, including
how they relate in terms of themes and significant concepts.

047AC9E6443140EDA0121E2336740AA7.description:
Analyze and reflect on (e.g., practical knowledge, historical/cultural context, and
background knowledge) how an author draws on, develops, or transforms source material historical and

text) and how they relate in terms of themes and significant concepts.

2F0D70DB6ED6466FB99BD75EB0E461CE.description:

whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and

Analyze, integrate, and evaluate multiple interpretations (e.g., charts, graphs, diagrams,

words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

971E4693053742C183D86684B6E84C0B.description:
Analyze integrate, and evaluate multiple interpretations (e.g., recorded or live production
of a play or recorded novel or poetry) of a single text or text/s presented in different formats (visually,
quantitatively).

277746A0E0AA4445BBA6305D34B29C73.description:
Determine an author’s purpose in a text (including cultural experience and knowledge

A694ABB8573F49E7B0261A32F4EB2A78.description:
Determine an author’s lens in a text (including cultural experience reflected in a work of

631D7754D73B450FBE91EB89531CA85D.description:
Analyze in detail the author’s choices concerning the structure of ideas or claims of a text,
and how they are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text
(e.g., a section or chapter).

EBC30EA0B5C045AFB0668D3D61179AF0.description:
Analyze how an author’s choices concerning the structure of a text, order of the events
within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulation of time (e.g., pacing, flashbacks) create specific effects

B506B0C3D4E944F3BE21B9FCA047FC61.description:
Analyze how an author unfolds ideas throughout the text, including the order in which the
points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between
them.

D29AA8850CF94A5FB633DAE704D52125.description:
Analyze how an author unfolds and develops ideas throughout a text, including how
complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop, interact with other
characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

47647CEC3F2F4FAB893D4DFA65204116.description:
Determine one or more central ideas of an informational text and analyze how it is
developed and refined over the course of a text, including how it emerges and is shaped by specific
details; provide an objective summary of the text.

37EA1C186D7D4092A143D092F0390308.description:

refined over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped by specific details; provide an
objective summary of the text

BD985D1314A54F909C29B154BC6E5DFB.description:
cite a range and thorough textual evidence and make clear and relevant connections, to
strongly support an analysis of multiple aspects of what an informational text says explicitly and
inferentially, as well as interpretations of the text.

307276F8E5C14344A9460368739BE1DC.description:
Cite a range of thorough textual evidence and make relevant connections to strongly
support analysis of multiple aspects of what a literary text says explicitly and inferentially, as well as
including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

AFFEC0E0BF784AFCB8F8271D8FCCEB53.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

068A763E9BE5412DB6D329D66F385E69.description:
Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism, oxymoron) in context and analyze their
role in the text.

7B06A23C9EA6424181CB15B18EDA2CF1.description:
Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word
meanings, including connotative meanings.

F789A13D8EC940D0B810330F741CC308.description:
Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by
checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

0F24D7C4C5094EF292EDC02D9EE23457.description:
Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries,
thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or
clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

4A5DAA8EC9CC49FAAA53FB2083DABA52.description:
Analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how
the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

E10CE0CE7C2A40099E12DA7722D283CF.description:
Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or
parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

242808F4F45A4009B0B85A8F5F7AD07E.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word’s
position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

1E585E0D46AD4DACA82ABBF0DF1B6B9F.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases
based on grades 9–10 reading and content, including technical meanings, choosing flexibly from a range
of strategies.

FAD465C2DF244576A11EF91170A56D08.description:
Demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a
word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

D051AA561DDF4F058B083E68D004C11F.description:
Vary word choice and sentence structure to demonstrate an understanding of the
influence of language.

6FF0E5A49C9A4501A7079FA880E61D0F.description:
Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases,
sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness

57F3E4B708BD40F3AF5F97851317826F.description:
Apply knowledge of language to make effective choices for meaning, or style, and to

870B2EA5D746414EA32D2413A93A542F.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

31B34662639D4298B79CE894FC3215F0.description:

15928BE1E1094D809D6DB42B3CCFAA8F.description:

20C79CB357E94F9A80E5234FC5BDEB0F.description:
Synthesize complex information across multiple sources and formats to develop ideas,
resolve conflicting information, or develop an interpretation that goes beyond explicit text information
(e.g., express a personal point of view, new interpretation of the author’s message).

52CFDB9B91764E30AF986A134AEF0FC2.description:
Analyze how the meaning of a key term or terms develops or is refined over the course

5D4BFF1C6CAE48C5AC206A0362450F4A.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

the text.

D8C4C25EBE274CB3A0DD0DAD70FAC07B.description:

word meanings, including connotative meanings.

CC9EE7E2329F44CA8DC66248860A4CBA.description:
Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by
checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

BA167E546ECC4CE7B151F171F8D74D5D.description:

over the course of a text or discussion.

637BC2D3EF134E6E8D1E71E716F60FAB.description:
Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or
parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

B9C73128A6C14EBC943BCE98B50D9837.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word’s
position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases
based on grades 11–12 reading and content, including technical meanings, choosing flexibly from a range

717C8A5340E9423CB0ABEA97468ED721.description:
Demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a
word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

1F77DBDC56464188B5A7B1DEAD2BAE22.description: Vary syntax for effect, apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts.

F222526FE29D4874832CBE0FB13CBE05.description:

sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness

CCE9C3CD5C884B33A9F6B5500E95FE44.description:
Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts,
to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EC4CBB53BB6B4731892865B0007EEA7B.description:

8AD244984DFB4A159180A8E241F6BCBE.description:
Demonstrate command of the system and structure of the English language when writing
or speaking.

AE4C134B57544A9CBA4B3FF345BABEA1.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

579038BDD5924E3A81791E95829F7A25.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

A687FAA18D144B86830C82815F3CEE6F.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

9CC9EA9963804CDA92B22FEB25DA2F9A.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

C6BC81032313445DAD2DB6C86D7995B8.description:
Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of
letters.

0D6D7C2A2C334BA8AC93F672BD73716A.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

D4BA7FC176D64B0FBA1D40A362C4F4A7.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

EE0CD484F9E243E699858FD48FEC0AF2.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, “Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?”.

D0A8B5054648400ABE746C94127686E4.description:
Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay
balls) and drawing shapes.

6CA87582A9DF4DEFB8E367EB7A77FE13.description:
Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and
orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g.,
number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal
length).

CAA0B1C095A84F4B8507FB0E6D2F4385.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes

78E030ADF5F144C19A6A4E0932A7CB9A.description:
Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional
(“solid”).

9DB10F9755DD4FDD84514A6918D6E5BB.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

FBF0ED3C16AB4515BB35C4E4334D2A00.description:
Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative
positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind,
and next to.

C7EC5AFAF02540D7BA8FB94129FB8E5A.description:
Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones,
cylinders, and spheres)

2BCC353C934A40249177A2EB5708C5DA.description:
Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and
sort the categories by count. (Clarification: Limit category counts to be less than or equal
to 10)

14C2645334F24574B3F7CC728DF8989B.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category

75630AADC396425191D28A5B59767D4B.description:
Understand that certain objects are coins and dollar bills, and that coins and dollar bills
represent money. Identify the values of all U.S. coins and the one-dollar bill.

06B27479A5B44AE4BBDD7D7400ED73A0.description:
Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object
has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference. For example, directly
compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.

DE5D37856ACA4C8B98DD5272C54EBCC8.description:
Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several
measurable attributes of a single object.

B9C0D48C157843C3AD942B743A0DBD56.description:
Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones,
e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a
drawing or equation (e.g.,); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and
one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

F811FD0FE7964A3E85856E6FCB060CB4.description: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value

03EB51293E7C409DBBDF6EC8D1BE86D6.description: Number and Operation in Base Ten

5DD5F03A165943CFB071BB80CCAAD770.description: Demonstrate accuracy and efficiency for addition and subtraction within 5.

7D37054C53634A6294E51DD6451F1978.description:
For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given
number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or
equation.

AF5BD368BEA64D558BFAF63EF5BD5C45.description:
Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by
using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

E60C9C8B5DC441E2AF49325292EACB21.description:
Represent addition and subtraction up to 10 with objects, fingers, mental images,
drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or
equations.

BD3C1C1E791644F9B018ABC1CF895E1D.description:
Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking
apart and taking from

1041258491B045BEB907214A504B4A80.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

E345EA20F0924A8D8286495894C0F296.description:
Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to
the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.
(Clarification: Include groups with up to ten objects.)

06858679D9374A3AA8B868E5ABFD0511.description:
Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a
rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a
number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

AC32EFBF944F4F96913C79EC23E752BF.description:
Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one
larger.

0293AA127DAC4A6AA3964AFED843697F.description:
Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted.
The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in
which they were counted.

E6A21527F81B49F6B1EA85A9D20501B3.description:
