Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and
every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If q and r are
integers, then - (p/q) = (-p)/q = p/(-q) . Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real world
contexts.

D26CA3065BC049EABCF5A1CF15871EB7.description:
Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by
requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations,
particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1) = 1 and the rules for
multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing
real-world contexts.

11564D05A91E4CF7AE0B4B86BAFE66E2.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions
to multiply and divide rational numbers.

27C2637A56C14AABAF49B8F0E203328B.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

23620A5202364332813BD3BEDD597A84.description:
Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q) . Show
that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute
value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

636DDFE806EB4604819B176BD937C9A5.description:
Understand p + q as the number located a distance from q, in the positive or negative
direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and
its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational
numbers by describing real-world contexts.

3A05096093984B8381634A22B064D517.description:
Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0. For example,
in the first round of a game, Maria scored 20 points. In the second round of the
same game, she lost 20 points. What is her score at the end of the second round?

3978B61E6DCC4E00B3DB92F79F73AD6B.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract
rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number
line diagram.

B92717C816924203B0491581FE2C648A.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract,
multiply, and divide rational numbers

80B4C3C795A14EF89E96FAE746D9DA4D.description:
Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems. Examples:
simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent
increase and decrease, percent error.

EF5870CCB64B4EA68FC97E99B2389BFD.description:
Explain what a point (x,y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms
of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1/r) where r is the unit
rate.

9CD511A8035243C5893BE73670CD4733.description:
Represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is
proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the
relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn .

57A385179A0D4CCB9DDC4F570A9D839C.description:
Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations,
diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

02E1CBE169C3489AA9DB57C8EDD7BB87.description:
Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing
for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing
whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

F32C7A4863CB41219EC051256CDE336C.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

04229753DC33490B8EA94563CC62F5F3.description:
Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas
and other quantities measured in like or different units. For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction (1/2) / (1/4) miles per hour,
equivalently 2 miles per hour.

0FE9E772C13043FB9216C61E30AA1DA7.description:
Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical
problems

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

3CC384CDC08447F2A1C79006FD2DFD22.description:
Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by
displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and
interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from
the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe
possible association between the two variables. For example, collect data from students in
your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they
have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to
have chores?

A0DC842E28004657A5F29D026C43DBAE.description:
Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate
measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. For example, in a linear model for
a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of
sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

8CD9E6C8BBE943BBA0E5465A1D36A251.description:
Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative
variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line,
and informally assess the model fit (e.g. line of best fit) by judging the closeness of the
data points to the line.

1A8EA58B1A884B8591A148F0C7C394D5.description:
Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns
of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers,
positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

4AFFD0D5ADFC4187A612ED6345D500F2.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data

F3CE4D8C96904E70B55EF4FF1BB29E59.description:
Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to
solve real-world and mathematical problems.

49D07FB1917A42B583C112C8E7391027.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and
spheres

5349DCD449A34C1698F737BD1718B3B4.description:
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate
system.

B6D9DE5B82F44A61A1398DBFC4D3416B.description:
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in
real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

56511ADDBC5E4C21BCD3D720D8CD5A6B.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

73A882D7B3B948EF9B1C075AEB3E7D1A.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem

D5139C7CA49B4E9C856FBA8CE4D742DE.description:
Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of
triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the
angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the
same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an
argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

DA10959C730946C6986F65761DF57618.description:
Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be
obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations;
given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the
similarity between them.

DFC02AF425EE4D009736465A203AFDC4.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on twodimensional figures using coordinates.

CAD091524637415E8656A3E2302CA7A2.description:
Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be
obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two
congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

4D9DF7EB370943A3BC55DD1D692CAE97.description: Parallel lines are transformed to parallel lines.

19BC570507D54012ADBCE24D3899B36C.description: Angles are transformed to angles of the same measure.

6FCC6A0F3CCB48978F6F4B55DB459D71.description:
Lines are transformed to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same
length.

28869BED6060420896682B7C2C782075.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

A15CE06E4E5B4CF1AD9C29EE8F66749B.description:
Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry
software

7F3D9FF4C3A541538DD226ED6ACB46A7.description:
Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a
graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a
graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

414E842C50DB49A9B2C4A83B963FC6CF.description:
Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the
rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from
two (x,y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change
and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its
graph or a table of values.

339B9F00FDF241F2A2E5D52C61513A41.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities

DE7CA4AA835441C8A083DD7304BD132E.description:
Interpret the equation y = mx+b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give
examples of functions that are not linear. For example, the function A = s^2 giving the area of a
square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points
(1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.

76C1AA03EF054A639ACD437964DC507E.description:
Compare properties (e.g. rate of change, intercepts, domain and range) of two functions
each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or
by verbal descriptions). For example, given a linear function represented by a table of
values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

1211514077F44BB38342CBF4B10EB242.description:
Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The
graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding
output.
(Clarification: Function notation is not required in Grade 8)

05B0D18175C7443193BA395B0C5B77EC.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two
variables. For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the
line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

42DF609E0EDE4667986DE354DAB8B5AE.description:
Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables using the substitution method
and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
For example: by inspection, conclude that 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot
simultaneously be 5 and 6. Solve 3x + y = 30 and y = 2x using the substitution method; Solve y = 3x + 1 and y = -2x+7 using
the substitution method.

879E70E24CC9495780350FFFF11876A9.description:
Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond
to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both
equations simultaneously.

D5FD23ACFE5C4D9485E3726334565259.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

D358C105AC12427C82AF6E174B2FD52E.description:
Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations
whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and
collecting like terms.

493D0B57CED1418F8E6EF1B43217839C.description:
Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely
many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by
successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an
equivalent equation of the form x=a, a=a, or a=b results (where a and b are different numbers).

C07F8A7985E24F1D8841ABD159932FF9.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

4B7DF386075945FAA8C4A035461FA6C7.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations

27D1819CEDE14716A7AA753DB7C1822D.description:
Use similar triangles to explain why the slope is the same between any two distinct
points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y=mx for a line
through the origin and the equation y=mx+b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

04C521B06A284B6A95423F7A5A7E17E0.description:
Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph.
Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For
example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which
of two moving objects has greater speed.

BD29F06D706244F2AA5D428F66366908.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations

E0CEA51A383F4F86A5F5BFF6B42440FF.description:
Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems
where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose
units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use
millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been
generated by technology.

7CE248F74CF34F398C727924CFBEBF22.description:
Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to
estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one
is than the other. For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 x 10^8 and the
population of the world as 7 x 10^9 and determine that the world population is more than 20 times
larger.

9716259D305A408B8E3EB747D572FA57.description:
Simplify numerical radicals, limiting to square roots (i.e. nonperfect squares). For
example, simplify √8 to 2√2.

DC5B9F3FD43E4E21B18A29FBDF464600.description:
Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect
cubes. Know √2 that is irrational.

D63630B57C3A4710AE07CAB5BF4C00D5.description:
Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x^2 = p and x^3 = p and
where p is a positive rational number.

8F807242F7D04CA19DB8D4027C1736B0.description:
Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical
expressions. For example, 3^2 x 3^(-5) = 3^(-3) = 1 / (3^3) = 1/27.

F13AC48C81E146E893DDC5D4DB0ADA60.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents

5F9A0E939E0A4BA4BB593CE867EC8F6D.description:
Understand that the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a
rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero
rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

FC81F56A90564F3796DC238C0A7A9D9D.description:
Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational
numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of
expressions (e.g., π^2). For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is
between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better
approximations.

4E32905A00044B2E8C3E170E59E261BC.description:
Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that
every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal
expansion repeats eventually and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually
into a rational number.

07834A306A7E46028B06EB76889BB6ED.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational and approximate them by rational numbers

document.title: 2020 New Jersey Student Learning Standards – Computer Science and Design Thinking

636114C9C9C649B1961D95820F774375.description:
Identify and compare technology used in different schools, communities, regions, and
parts of the world.

0856C96B6C8642AE82F86BD6A3FB6602.description:
The availability of technology
for essential tasks varies in
different parts of the world.

81CA71A549F34D17AD8980937CA3E606.description:
Ethics and Culture concerns the profound effects that technologies have on people, how those effects can widen or narrow disparities, and the
responsibility that people have for the societal consequences of their technological decisions.

EFA23EBA39A948A3861714C3772D67C0.description:
Explain how the disposal of or reusing a product affects the local and global
environment.

719A4A49CFBC4198AA8D65B1F0465CC6.description: Describe or model the system used for recycling technology.

63F1FE86172B48CC99B2D3ECA8F60AB3.description: Identify the natural resources needed to create a product.

AF813FA149994406A15E803A8AE1874E.description: Classify products as resulting from nature or produced as a result of technology.

14816C23ED6E41919B79391B16E76C6F.description:
The use of technology
developed for the human
designed world can affect
the environment, including
land, water, air, plants, and
animals.Technologies that use natural sources can have negative effects on the environment, its quality, and inhabitants.Reusing and recycling materials can save money while preserving natural resources and avoiding damage to the environment.

98761709815F47A08C04664CB5E31195.description:
Many of engineering and technology’s impacts on society and the environment are widely regarded as desirable. However, other impacts are regarded
as less desirable. Effects of Technology on the Natural World concerns the positive and negative ways that technologies affect the natural world.

25193F567DF047B38077BFD8C290F2F2.description: Effects of Technology on the Natural World

1DAAE472A3DB46FD98D969361011CC0E.description:
Brainstorm how to build a product, improve a designed product, fix a product that
has stopped working, or solve a simple problem.

EC5AC388A95B457A9EF23867398D78A4.description:
Model and explain how a product works after taking it apart, identifying the
relationship of each part, and putting it back together.

B549A66CDABD46DD8676A8EF34C56C8E.description:
Innovation and the improvement
of existing technology involves
creative thinking.

F7BFA0C99F904F4EAE78374CE72460F5.description:
Human population, patterns and movement focus on the size, composition, distribution, and movement of human populations and how they are
fundamental and active features on Earth’s surface. This includes understanding that the expansion and redistribution of the human population affects
patterns of settlement, environmental changes, and resource use. Patterns and movements of population also relate to physical phenomena including
climate variability, landforms, and locations of various natural hazards and their effects on population size, composition, and distribution.

D23466B8DBF14C3C8BE094140008FFDE.description:
Design a solution to a problem affecting the community in a collaborative team and
explain the intended impact of the solution.

30EED776BFB84919B3B14349D99973C9.description: Identify how various tools reduce work and improve daily tasks.

30B764ACB3924841B6066012B44CFE25.description: Identify how technology impacts or improves life.

D04DD17A215F40EB9F16423735E05080.description:
Technology has changed the
way people live and work.Various tools can improve daily tasks and quality of life.

CBC86A6687844CE3BF41A3E04EEBC9E2.description: Explain the purpose of a product and its value.

5C45E724000A44FE9F41374C6A08E7D7.description: Identify products that are designed to meet human wants or needs.

152D09BA48DB453BB105754DFB5A5521.description:
Human needs and desires
determine which new tools
are developed.

BDFE87BE95084C2B88AF3E30F71A5EB1.description:
Societies influence technological development. Societies are characterized by common elements such as shared values, differentiated roles, and cultural
norms, as well as by entities such as community institutions, organizations, and businesses. Interaction of Technology and Humans concerns the ways
society drives the improvement and creation of new technologies, and how technologies both serve and change society.

654A1640E8754F45AC2AFC51417A2575.description: Identify constraints and their role in the engineering design process.

13DF25FEDB7B462EA199D4B0FFC64ADB.description:
Limitations (constraints)
must be considered when
engineering designs.

7CA061A3E736456F8503CC406A78CD58.description:
Select and use appropriate tools and materials to build a product using the design
process.

99E05211BE8746ED883358DFB1A85B5F.description:
Collaborate to solve a simple problem, or to illustrate how to build a product using
the design process.

6B96C660E96E4D5BAB0BC2713056EFFF.description: Communicate the function of a product or device.

CC5A2E6A20054EA9B54393A6223BCDFA.description:
Engineering design is a
creative process for meeting
human needs or wants that
can result in multiple
solutions.

333A423C055449A1837E37D905DF07CF.description:
People design for enjoyment and to solve problems, extend human capabilities, satisfy needs and wants, and improve the human condition. Engineering
Design, a systematic approach to creating solutions to technological problems and finding ways to meet people’s needs and desires, allows for the
effective and efficient development of products and systems.

8EF4C1C7AC7F4469B0CB380487E49CDF.description: Debug errors in an algorithm or program that includes sequences and simple loops.

A9E09D5960B0401381BD355E1EF614E0.description: Describe a program’s sequence of events, goals, and expected outcomes.

B06D1DBC3A2A4DA8874B92C4C140382F.description: People work together to develop programs for a purpose, such as expressing ideas or addressing problems.The development of a program involves identifying a sequence of events, goals, and expected outcomes, and addressing errors (when necessary).

BBE9E3D04A564140A1AF4B59964BD37F.description: Break down a task into a sequence of steps.

13B9F98A543C4A8B985CEC92819E7DED.description: Complex tasks can be broken down into simpler instructions, some of which can be broken down even further.

738B8B18B2274595857C29C607B92BB3.description: Create programs with sequences and simple loops to accomplish tasks.

E1DAB74A89384F79A3C17F43E4D2807F.description:
Computers follow precise
sequences of steps that
automate tasks.

D76A09C596A741CC9E2A60B5D43543B9.description:
Model the way programs store and manipulate data by using numbers or other
symbols to represent information.

921766E0AD6F43AEA4B39F707719F996.description: Real world information can be stored and manipulated in programs as data (e.g., numbers, words, colors, images).

CB8D7241B93B4BE494EE6152C380BDFD.description: Model daily processes by creating and following algorithms to complete tasks.

A5E568774C7C4BC19FD80B73793C04A5.description:
Individuals develop and
follow directions as part of
daily life. A sequence of steps can be expressed as an algorithm that a computer can process.

8CDBFC18255D433C91ED85BBCAD6351B.description:
An algorithm is a sequence of steps designed to accomplish a specific task. Algorithms are translated into programs, or code, to provide instructions for
computing devices. Algorithms and programming control all computing systems, empowering people to communicate with the world in new ways and
solve compelling problems.

CBF8AB3200FE487291317B1D957F2114.description: Make predictions based on data using charts or graphs.

CB8B5844309D4D42A78ADD365D197573.description: Identify and describe patterns in data visualizations

86796A9A0AA6462288EB2AF76B1CFD0E.description:
Data can be used to make
predictions about the world.

3561F8D0551E46F7AED190E7EEC48520.description: Store, copy, search, retrieve, modify, and delete data using a computing device.

5ABE90F7EF5A4678B5B9D905D779D173.description:
Computers store data that
can be retrieved later. Data
can be copied, stored in
multiple locations, and
retrieved.

49A8E24B45B648C0959A4D8899B4DAE5.description: Collect and present data, including climate change data, in various visual formats.

6FF49EF6A7C3426F8BF0413F18F8D247.description:
Individuals collect, use, and
display data about
individuals and the world
around them.

F318DF63D07C4CFBA4F36EFD7878BE8E.description:
Computing systems exist to process data. The amount of digital data generated in the world is rapidly expanding, so the need to process data effectively
is increasingly important. Data is collected and stored so that it can be analyzed to better understand the world and make more accurate predictions.

67CDA713BBDB485F9599C5B7DB7468A3.description:
Compare how individuals live and work before and after the implementation of new
computing technology.

9717621EC5064FADB2AE1A25E7805275.description:
Computing technology has
positively and negatively changed
the way individuals live and work
(e.g., entertainment,
communication, productivity
tools).

D124E232BBF24762AA3D0D5589C62893.description:
Computing affects many aspects of the world in both positive and negative ways at local, national, and global levels. Individuals and communities
influence computing through their behaviors and cultural and social interactions, and, in turn, computing influences new cultural practices.

78D303D7FBEA4C8DA93473C51489B4B3.description: Create a password that secures access to a device. Explain why it is important to create unique passwords that are not shared with others.

75BF551961D14273A092F7136C67DD68.description: Create a password that secures access to a device. Explain why it is important to create unique passwords that are not shared with others.

2DEB512B647342EA88A438D3381E7871.description: Connecting devices to a network or the Internet provides great benefits, but care must be taken to use authentication measures, such as strong passwords, to protect devices and information from unauthorized access.

E8797FB7060D4EAEA863821098F3F63B.description: Describe how the Internet enables individuals to connect with others worldwide.

6861C5D6A03E4348A11F3F62472F4D2C.description:
Model and describe how individuals use computers to connect to other individuals,
places, information, and ideas through a network.

C4ECFD46713D4CCEAD961F35F01A73CB.description:
Computer networks can be
used to connect individuals
to other individuals, places,
information, and ideas. The
Internet enables individuals
to connect with others
worldwide.

E98A5AA00CF049E38494337D9A55E3A3.description:
Computing devices typically do not operate in isolation. Networks connect computing devices to share information and resources and are an
increasingly integral part of computing. Networks and communication systems provide greater connectivity in the computing world.

F41EDA2AC84A4E018303EB35BFCC2975.description: Describe basic hardware and software problems using accurate terminology

FA35D6E544D54DC498A30BE9101351FB.description:
Describing a problem is the
first step toward finding a
solution when computing
systems do not work as
expected.

2A631F4910CB4D5FAC6743BD3BB9E0E6.description:
Explain the functions of common software and hardware components of computing
systems

AFB472E057294009A855C4A589A3DD85.description:
A computing system is
composed of software and
hardware.

C02DB2024DCF475D97C32DC8B14C1090.description:
Select and operate computing devices that perform a variety of tasks accurately and
quickly based on user needs and preferences.

0A823CBC370D43D19B272789B67F86BA.description:
Individuals use computing
devices to perform a variety
of tasks accurately and
quickly. Computing devices
interpret and follow the
instructions they are given
literally.

5E588456E5C74CD9AAEC2A9474B77D8D.description:
People interact with a wide variety of computing devices that collect, store, analyze, and act upon information in ways that can affect human
capabilities both positively and negatively. The physical components (hardware) and instructions (software) that make up a computing system
communicate and process information in digital form.

document.title: 2020 New Jersey Student Learning Standards – Computer Science and Design Thinking

77A9849108DF40169D004B9F4C10468E.description:
Analyze how technology has contributed to or reduced inequities in local and global
communities and determine its short- and long-term effects.

EAEFF83A8BCD442E93C21D1541F22BA7.description:
Technological choices and
opportunities vary due to factors
such as differences in economic
resources, location, and cultural
values.

05C6985D7F544CB68B00AD73CE5C3004.description:
Ethics and Culture concerns the profound effects that technologies have on people, how those effects can widen or narrow disparities, and the
responsibility that people have for the societal consequences of their technological decisions.

D969C7D45E284EA89064D0A59584F3A0.description: Identify the impact of a specific technology on the environment and determine what can be done to increase positive effects and to reduce any negative effects, such as climate change.

3A8A2FDA3F9546D48CDBB65C208B33FC.description: Explain the impact that resources, such as energy and materials used to develop technology, have on the environment.

3F604E3DAFE545BBBB22DEEB7A71EE91.description: Explain why human-designed systems, products, and environments need to be constantly monitored, maintained, and improved.

7E1258C3CE9F4821B2640ADE8422F691.description: Describe ways that various technologies are used to reduce improper use of resources.

325A89F8A6C640EFBF0ED66B98B18CEC.description:
Describe how resources such as material, energy, information, time, tools, people,
and capital are used in products or systems.

4E6B4680E6A845A1AD558C4AD3440E38.description:
The technology developed
for the human designed
world can have unintended
consequences for the
environment.Technology must be continually developed and made more efficient to reduce the need for nonrenewable resources.

B5F75F35C09E4F5586F55B516A3FAAC4.description:
Many of engineering and technology’s impacts on society and the environment are widely regarded as desirable. However, other impacts are regarded
as less desirable. Effects of Technology on the Natural World concerns the positive and negative ways that technologies affect the natural world.

B94E5813545A4D77A005EA70FBCCC4A3.description: Effects of Technology on the Natural World

0FCDC44759A0455EAC87E15DF6BB4303.description: Identify how improvement in the understanding of materials science impacts technologies.

A50E89A0424C400B97E82D839BAFF652.description: Redesign an existing product for a different purpose in a collaborative team.

435C54497E2A4FAC873C755011692909.description:
Identify new technologies resulting from the demands, values, and interests of
individuals, businesses, industries, and societies.

41188DD9C06A488A95D02E1C0EE60E33.description:
Troubleshoot a product that has stopped working and brainstorm ideas to correct the
problem.

6E77498803004170A653A716FA864A24.description:
Technology innovation and
improvement may be
influenced by a variety of
factors.Engineers create and modify technologies to meet people’s needs and wants; scientists ask questions about the natural world.

3DD86D14CE284FF19B4DDB5F9E00EACF.description:
Human population, patterns and movement focus on the size, composition, distribution, and movement of human populations and how they are
fundamental and active features on Earth’s surface. This includes understanding that the expansion and redistribution of the human population affects
patterns of settlement, environmental changes, and resource use. Patterns and movements of population also relate to physical phenomena including
climate variability, landforms, and locations of various natural hazards and their effects on population size, composition, and distribution.

FCA0A8E0381E402291B3DE648F70EE7A.description:
Describe a technology/tool that has made the way people live easier or has led to a
new business or career.

2089A0A14E824106B0E1C8539790F40B.description:
Analyze the effectiveness of a new product or system and identify the positive
and/or negative consequences resulting from its use.

EB2294372C3C447D8598905B3CF5DDE6.description:
Evaluate how well a new tool has met its intended purpose and identify any
shortcomings it might have.

5734F97B414E48CB83D6791E1AA0F4A5.description:
A new tool may have
favorable or unfavorable
results as well as both
positive and negative effects
on society. Technology spurs new businesses and careers.

79BA89FDD20548D896131098955A78C0.description:
Explain how societal needs and wants influence the development and function of a
product and a system.

5FDD397E4D6B40C8BC8A16CA38766688.description:
Societal needs and wants
determine which new tools
are developed to address
real-world problems.

9D159181366244BE9EF48CF6D8D786EC.description:
Societies influence technological development. Societies are characterized by common elements such as shared values, differentiated roles, and cultural
norms, as well as by entities such as community institutions, organizations, and businesses. Interaction of Technology and Humans concerns the ways
society drives the improvement and creation of new technologies, and how technologies both serve and change society.

FDDBDA52F0464215B1F6D5D53F838FA7.description:
Evaluate and test alternative solutions to a problem using the constraints and trade-
offs identified in the design process.

CBF6CD3E2E60424DA7CC0AA95CE4416F.description: Describe how specifications and limitations impact the engineering design process.

7AC9C7EB169D478EA2737CC1702AE8E0.description:
Explain factors that influence the development and function of products and systems
(e.g., resources, criteria, desired features, constraints).

1AAF78B742C54147848B06593824E31B.description: Engineering design requirements include desired features and limitations that need to be considered.

F21522E3DDD64E54A73AE3C1CBB7F539.description:
Follow step by step directions to assemble a product or solve a problem, using
appropriate tools to accomplish the task.

B36DA00BA3114CBB93F19A724C3FB1F7.description:
Collaborate with peers to collect information, brainstorm to solve a problem, and
evaluate all possible solutions to provide the best results with supporting sketches or models.

52CA34283B91409EB55BD582668403D9.description: Explain the functions of a system and its subsystems.

2CE887CE5DD1468DAC6E6D0A2EE45FB2.description:
Engineering design is a
systematic and creative
process of communicating
and collaborating to meet a
design challenge.Often, several design solutions exist, each better in some way than the others.

173E9417D24D4ADD8A84070A81325ED7.description:
People design for enjoyment and to solve problems, extend human capabilities, satisfy needs and wants, and improve the human condition. Engineering
Design, a systematic approach to creating solutions to technological problems and finding ways to meet people’s needs and desires, allows for the
effective and efficient development of products and systems.

ACC0F1DD42CE43C8B7B40FD1E97E2813.description:
Develop programs using an iterative process, implement the program design, and test
the program to ensure it works as intended

10C97D938AEC4B54832DC6D7B5282CA6.description:
Individuals develop
programs using an iterative
process involving design,
implementation, testing, and
review.

70CB72E8F56B4046A69EAED6D4AD3EB6.description: Modify, remix, or incorporate pieces of existing programs into one’s own work to add additional features or create a new program.

8EF799E8C6F747E7996B4F47AA828F7C.description:
Break down problems into smaller, manageable sub-problems to facilitate program
development.

8B37BDAAC2FC49D9B282CE6EEB0D5CC7.description: Programs can be broken down into smaller parts to facilitate their design, implementation, and review. Programs can also be created by incorporating smaller portions of programs that already exist.

62ECD23F2C494391B5F2B608FF6CD032.description: Create programs that include sequences, events, loops, and conditionals.

2F92E038351B4E71AC7F3A7CB3395E2B.description: A variety of control structures are used to change the flow of program execution (e.g., sequences, events, loops, conditionals).

9EDFC08A0AEB4E3682BFCEC5CC833BD3.description: Create programs that use clearly named variables to store and modify data.

D213DE0631694DEB9F62ACBD7385331E.description: Programming languages provide variables, which are used to store and modify data.

343CB97CC3404E7BB535FAC70F34B3D9.description:
Compare and refine multiple algorithms for the same task and determine which is the
most appropriate.

A882805D8550436EAF8FBEF3E1DD87D6.description:
Different algorithms can
achieve the same result.Some algorithms are more appropriate for a specific use than others.

4D7361B2F76546C89B177BD96D7FBAE6.description:
An algorithm is a sequence of steps designed to accomplish a specific task. Algorithms are translated into programs, or code, to provide instructions for
computing devices. Algorithms and programming control all computing systems, empowering people to communicate with the world in new ways and
solve compelling problems.

5B40F320F00144398364077A83FEE5F1.description:
Propose cause and effect relationships, predict outcomes, or communicate ideas
using data.

0C7C7A89EA184CD291D06BEEE863EFA8.description:
Many factors influence the
accuracy of inferences and
predictions.

39BD2403DD5D4ABFBBE2C6458F980177.description: Organize and present climate change data visually to highlight relationships or support a claim.

C14CE10550A447EC9FDF2B7C7F5E0EB3.description:
Organize and present collected data visually to communicate insights gained from
different views of the data.

9CB3E78D83FD42DC95791D7EF11AD7E6.description:
Individuals can select,
organize, and transform data
into different visual
representations and
communicate insights
gained from the data.

596789BEEAA4407AA9824A866D5475DE.description: Compare the amount of storage space required for different types of data.

27E3830E99AE4F038468F395586A621A.description:
The type of data being
stored affects the storage
requirements.

AF52ABBFE2274C1581DA477CF300788A.description:
Collect, organize, and display data in order to highlight relationships or support a
claim.

9A62D6F22EAD428084E14EF01350D498.description:
Data can be organized,
displayed, and presented to
highlight relationships

0B8B93686AC94B1E87D69168AAF0FBF1.description:
Computing systems exist to process data. The amount of digital data generated in the world is rapidly expanding, so the need to process data effectively
is increasingly important. Data is collected and stored so that it can be analyzed to better understand the world and make more accurate predictions.

900DFE4EE34C4A9FB678DEE6209E57C4.description:
Identify possible ways to improve the accessibility and usability of computing
technologies to address the diverse needs and wants of users.

1E7D6614A3494B6287DD721575FEF3AE.description:
Identify computing technologies that have impacted how individuals live and work
and describe the factors that influenced the changes.

84F4B25F9DED461F960974190E51E37E.description:
The development and
modification of computing
technology is driven by people’s
needs and wants and can affect
individuals differently.

31D0F19351574984BA685C01C52717E4.description:
Computing affects many aspects of the world in both positive and negative ways at local, national, and global levels. Individuals and communities
influence computing through their behaviors and cultural and social interactions, and, in turn, computing influences new cultural practices.

5A18320BB44E4ACA8FF59CBBF516BD28.description:
Describe physical and digital security measures for protecting sensitive personal
information.

91F3933F03F14A59A0425B618FBEE041.description:
Distinguishing between
public and private
information is important for
safe and secure online
interactions.Information can be protected using various security measures (i.e., physical and digital).

A2DC36D0225540F9B2592483A9DD564B.description:
Develop models that successfully transmit and receive information using both wired
and wireless methods.

C2772E09F6174171B50B9E0E29A87F51.description:
Information needs a physical
or wireless path to travel to
be sent and received.

A4335F184AAA4CA392AA1F0A42BA16A9.description:
Computing devices typically do not operate in isolation. Networks connect computing devices to share information and resources and are an
increasingly integral part of computing. Networks and communication systems provide greater connectivity in the computing world.

D43F1AEEC335405E9439B7C5239D2D71.description:
Identify potential solutions for simple hardware and software problems using
common troubleshooting strategies.

F00F1B5AE1FC4857A96A2472705DE973.description:
Shared features allow for
common troubleshooting
strategies that can be
effective for many systems.

FBDEA34E7C8B41C9BFBD71C87E08B237.description:
Model how computer software and hardware work together as a system to
accomplish tasks.

6596FB6249884CCF8DF2055EE625969C.description:
Software and hardware
work together as a system to
accomplish tasks (e.g.,
sending, receiving,
processing, and storing units
of information).

5E5AC1CEDB5E4A8C94FE4129DA814422.description: Model how computing devices connect to other components to form a system.

8F0AA857F8E240EBB8A81947A2D0A866.description:
Computing devices may be
connected to other devices
to form a system as a way to
extend their capabilities.

4D1C651B189E4FBDB877232E74312E0A.description:
People interact with a wide variety of computing devices that collect, store, analyze, and act upon information in ways that can affect human
capabilities both positively and negatively. The physical components (hardware) and instructions (software) that make up a computing system
communicate and process information in digital form.

document.title: 2020 New Jersey Student Learning Standards – Visual and Performing Arts Introduction

Collaborate on the creation of a short scene based on personal perspectives and
understandings.

With prompting and support, identify similarities and differences in stories and various
art forms from one’s own community and from multiple cultures in a guided drama (e.g., process
drama, story drama, creative drama) experience about global issues, including climate change.

Relating artistic ideas and works within societal, cultural, and
historical contexts to deepen understanding.

3CEF5ACBEE6842A096E8D72031EF0208.description:
With prompting and support, identify similarities between characters in dramatic play or
a guided drama experience and relate character emotions and experiences to personal experiences of
self and peers (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

BBE5761D00944814BF51CD1AD6D03735.description:
Synthesizing and relating knowledge and personal experiences to
create products.

9083B8AF57B047D8823F3FBDF87C7820.description:
Explain or use text and pictures to describe how personal emotions and/or others'
emotions and choices compare to the emotions and choices of characters in a guided drama
experience. (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

76DFB302CA05461BB0902856C74E7C51.description:
With prompting and support, name and describe settings and identify causes of character
actions in a guided drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

31869734909B4DC09C335D855B3D05C9.description:
With prompting and support, identify and explain preferences and emotions in a guided
drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama), or theatre performance, and
explain how personal preferences and emotions affect an observer's response in a guided drama
experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama), or theatre performance.

FEC2FD9A3B42468EBEF34376930BDD06.description:
Compare and contrast how characters respond to challenges in a guided drama experience
(e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

806AA4DB80AF4EDD94E1F00B7DC6CF44.description:
Identify and use props and costumes that might be used in a guided drama experience
(e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

D9EB635B696647A580654DE2C6504FD5.description:
With prompting and support, actively engage and build on others' ideas in dramatic play
or a guided drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

FB6705EC982A425BBF9CF41CE849945F.description:
Express emotional responses to characters to recall and recognize when artistic choices
are made in a guided drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

7B3844D2D29C4070808B3CA694C004AE.description:
Use voice, sound, movement, and gestures to communicate emotions in a guided drama
experience; informally share guided drama experiences (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative
drama) with peers.

0D1225F320794E249E719C7831BE452B.description:
Utilize body and facial gestures with a change in voice to communicate character traits
and emotions in a guided drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

53349D96C2E2472593CA6AB4BFF9DC8C.description:
With prompting and support interpret story elements (e.g., character, setting) in a guided
drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

F258C3C549D94160922ADA267DE51B2B.description:
Developing and refining techniques and models or steps needed to
create products.

1512D039804C48418507F865154E1E06.description:
Explore and experiment with various technical elements in a guided drama experience
(e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

56A1902E2ABC4CD0BD7E0F60C90E473A.description:
With prompting and support, demonstrate the physical movement, voice and sound which
are fundamental to creating drama experiences (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

E6867D7706404896BF782CBFCBD7EC14.description:
Independently imagine multiple representations of an object in a guided drama experience
(e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama) and collaboratively create multiple representations
of an object in a guided drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

A435AB03BDC440C3AC25EF61AB0E7381.description:
Identify similarities and differences in sounds and movements in a guided drama
experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

DDA9F394B67F4F5DB37F616F0A0E5F60.description:
With prompting and support, contribute to the adaption of plot and dialogue in a guided
drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

71BFBDB025CF442B862F53B54E695687.description:
Contribute original ideas and make decisions as a group to advance a story in a guided
drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

1044169C0DE449D4BE57C64A3608E9B0.description:
Contribute to the development of a sequential plot; collaborate with peers to devise a
meaningful dialogue in a guided drama experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

C0217AA878A1458FA0E912912A404997.description:
Identify ways in which voice, gestures, movements, and sounds may be used to create or
retell a story in guided drama experiences (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

3105E8DD22F94F87A05C5018296C0124.description:
Collaborate with peers to conceptualize props, costumes and scenery in a guided drama
experience (e.g., process drama, story drama, creative drama).

FE24252B83F7464B9A6FE20A41C989A8.description:
Propose potential character choices and plot details in a guided drama experience (e.g.,
process drama, story drama, creative drama).

B834CB5B10A04DAAA32431CE2ECD4572.description: Compare the drama/theatre conventions of a given time period with those of the present.

9E18D505BDA84D48A4AD14152B42719B.description:
Identify, respond to and investigate connections to global issues including climate
change and other content areas in a dramatic/theatrical work.

79E8F3693E7C4D72834AEDF19BB83AE8.description:
Relating artistic ideas and works within societal, cultural and
historical contexts to deepen understanding.

2CFE385E50C740B4A14DFC5E7C2B57A3.description:
Explain how drama/theatre connects oneself to a community or culture and identify the
ways drama/theatre work reflects the perspectives of a community or culture.

2FDEA333A2DE4FE8A1425EAA0650FFB1.description:
Synthesizing and relating knowledge and personal experiences to
create products.

Identify and discuss physiological changes connected to emotions on posture, gesture,
breathing, and vocal intonation in a drama/theatre work.

2910B9B9F09E4EBE83421CD5A1BED947.description:
Explain responses to characters based on cultural perspectives when participating in or
observing drama/theatre work.

11177DC15A0C4862B6C6CD14179E0342.description:
Compare and contrast multiple personal experiences when participating in or observing a
drama/theatre work and justify responses to drama/theatre work based on personal experience.

113897A28C674368A09F38EF5A90CF6A.description:
Evaluate and analyze how a character’s choices and character's circumstances impact an
audience’s perspective in a drama/theatre work.

7280FD9506764526897539FF741F7A06.description:
Analyze technical elements from multiple drama/theatre works and assess how the
technical elements may support or represent the themes or central ideas of drama/theatre works.

E852BB4E27FB4C6FAF3317316F116D15.description: Develop and implement a plan to evaluate drama/theatre work.

25D2A81D2A864CAC95179AAEE826C50F.description:
Identify, explain and demonstrate an understanding of both artistic choices and personal
reactions made in a drama/theatre work through participation and observation.

872A2EB9F79440D1948A30B60B799AF6.description:
Practice drama/theatre work and share reflections individually and in small groups, and
informally with an audience.

1AF881E4CDDB49AA8BD7979F0CCF20D6.description:
Physically and intellectually investigate how movement and vocal choices are
incorporated and make meaning in drama/theatre work.

96239025E71C4B2A92D412CA2CE7D3D5.description:
Describe and apply dramatic elements of dialogue, action, character emotion, and theme
in the performance and/or creation of a drama/theatre work.

D9A177640F804B529B7CF22E802CB1A5.description:
Developing and refining techniques and models or steps needed to
create products.

AAD87DACC00A4B5DA0EC8C4D805978F9.description:
Identify and utilize basic technical/design elements that can be used in drama/theatre work
to demonstrate an understanding of the elements.

CC745FCD288F48A9A6ED96DACF51B966.description:
Participate in, propose, and practice a variety of physical, vocal, and cognitive exercises
that can be used in a group setting for drama/theatre work.

9F817ACC75634CEAA7DE508A418D76D9.description:
Refine technical choices by creating innovative solutions to design and technical
problems that arise in rehearsal for a drama/theatre work.

89F6F0A315004D26B33C7981DE0EEA96.description: Use and adapt sounds and movements in a guided drama experience.

A94793F5435C4EE19F08A8A36D7C90E3.description:
Collaborate with peers to revise, refine, adapt and improve ideas to fit the given
parameters of an improvised or scripted drama/theatre work through self and collaborative review.

Participate and identify defined responsibilities required to present a drama/theatre work
informally to peers/audience and participate in the process.

D77B9B3AE6C642CAB58D41BE0D1E44F8.description:

characters, plots and their given circumstances.

determine how characters might move and speak to support the story and given circumstances in
drama/theatre work.

given circumstances, and characters in a drama/theatre work.

12A5EA14CE4C4EEA801B060E5547280C.description:
Create roles, imagined worlds and improvised stories in a drama/theatre work articulating
the physical qualities of characters, visual details of imagined worlds, and given circumstances, of
improvised stories in a drama/theatre work.

Identify and examine artifacts from a time period and geographic location to better
understand performance and design choices in a theatrical work.

B2CD67DA38584189905BBB44AC483C04.description:

create products.

discuss a theatrical work.

61826EF5311C4795AA5C0C628C86CF18.description:
Identify and interpret how different cultural perspectives influence the evaluation of

B2EB70CD017A4AD0BBA2FC61CC5B6C8B.description: Assess the impact of a theatrical work on a specific audience.

work.

F947E8E337654155B2A3183EC86AE6D5.description:
Investigate various critique methodologies and apply the knowledge to respond to a

7D3B96CADE544EFBAD012D1F38CC2B66.description: Describe and record personal reactions to artistic choices in a theatrical work.

D8DF01786A8D4B3A8E4A3FA42FCB01B8.description: Perform a rehearsed theatrical work for an audience

61F8D448D4EB4118B672F1C5A89AD6D8.description:
Use various character objectives and tactics in a theatre work to identify the conflict and

B9171F75A4E64D11B08B26C2556DD15C.description:
Examine how character relationships assist in telling the story of devised or scripted
theatre work.

13B040AF51BC43A9B86F0A8694864EA9.description:
