conditions that are common in young adults in the United States and in other countries (e.g.,
hepatitis, stroke, heart attacks, cancer,).

D5783BACA10D4D4F95CF11E7525E7E64.description:
Evaluate the benefits of biomedical approaches to prevent STIs (e.g.,
hepatitis B vaccine, HPV vaccine) and HIV (e.g., PrEP, PEP).

895405B3B1D64CF0A7C300D6AE9E9E89.description:
Provide examples of how drugs and medication mimic or block the action of
certain cells in the body, and how abusing drugs can affect the human body.

586F7652835A4D559EC62F1140833E06.description:
Develop a health care plan to help prevent and treat diseases and health
conditions one may encounter (e.g., breast/testicular exams, Pap smear, regular STIs testing,
HPV vaccine).

C438B8F4EF8F44A4A7B91F4385071671.description:
Analyze the short- and long-term consequences of sharing sexually explicit
images (sexting) or messages with individuals or posting online.

34A201FA8099435A8F48DB1B70440682.description: Evaluate strategies to use social media safely, legally, and respectfully.

6375838DB61C4C57A4D63CD2A18DBD0F.description:
Develop strategies to communicate effectively, safely, and with empathy when
using digital devices in a variety of situations (e.g., cyberbullying, sexting).

E0E954A0B0B349AEA1B364EAA887EC03.description:
Analyze recruitment tactics that sex traffickers/exploiters use to exploit
vulnerabilities and recruit youth.

656EAFECF7274B8ABC464BE59DE8DA61.description:
Describe the types of abuse (e.g., physical, emotional, psychological, financial,
sexual) and the cycle of violence as it relates to sexual abuse, domestic violence, dating
violence, and gender-based violence.

3308D0B0AC6D43368FB6FC4E28CF4D5C.description:
Identify the state and federal laws related to intimate partner and sexual violence
(e.g., sexual harassment, sexual abuse, sexual assault, domestic violence).

ED01133773DD4E618E2D653E60CF126B.description:
Investigate the relationship between alcohol, drug use, and motor vehicle crashes
and analyze the short- and long-term consequences of these actions.

4E3314315FFE42AAB583F5296EE0BBAB.description:
Summarize New Jersey motor vehicle laws and regulations, Safe Stops, and
determine their impact on health and safety (e.g., organ/tissue donation, traffic safety, avoid
driving distractors, seatbelt use, the use of hand-held devices).

3935FE36867D464C9E4DB7675BA5B355.description:
Analyze the short- and long-term consequences of sharing sexually explicit
images (sexting) or messages with individuals or posting online.

B51180D543664C4494A03F8FC24CEBDE.description:
Apply a thoughtful decision-making process to evaluate situations and influences
that could lead to healthy or unhealthy consequences (e.g., peers, media).

10F449A44FB04D1CBCECBCBA992F4519.description:
Research present trends in plant based and organic food choices and industries that
have shown an impact on lowering heart, cancer, diabetes, and other diseases.

B9EE4304CC054551BCF504DEBB5A7E47.description:
Implement strategies and monitor progress in achieving a personal nutritional
health plan.

8CE3C4384D48496CB23AC499EE7CABD8.description:
Analyze the unique contributions of each nutrient class (e.g., fats, carbohydrates,
protein, water, vitamins, minerals) to one’s health and fitness.

0D4AC45F9E114D4D93598C533FDE8F17.description:
Determine the relationship of nutrition and physical activity to weight loss, gain,
and maintenance.

B0D8EE660AB8405CBAE8C31EE01E371F.description:
Compare and contrast the nutritional trends, eating habits, and the impact of
marketing foods on adolescents and young adults nationally and worldwide.

1F840267A6E0452C9C148953677AF2D9.description:
Identify personal and community resources to explore career options related to
physical activity and health.

DCC559B15B334D3FB6D8D747B8652FBE.description:
Analyze the current and future impact of globalization and technology on the
influences of participation in sports, games, physical fitness activities, dance, gaming, outdoor
adventure, viewing sports, and social and emotional connections.

EBC76067F5814F8CA8DB17C63AAB46A4.description:
Implement a financial plan for participation in physical activity in the community
for self and family members.

2A6ADD73A2EF4017AC2BADE2A967A3D6.description:
Describe the social benefits gained from participating in physical activity (e.g.,
meeting someone, making friends, team work, building trust, experiencing something new).

0AA6DB3F847C4440BB373883E74F8CE0.description:
Exhibit responsible social behavior by including and cooperating with classmates
of all skill levels, assisting when needed, and collaborating respectfully to solve problems in
groups, teams, and in pairs during physical activity.

A9261260A19D46BD98DB6728A306C79A.description:
Examine building to a level of fitness to successfully participate in a range of
different physical activities during a lifetime.

A75BC02A0FB645DEBAB0DE801DDC47D1.description:
Develop a sense of openness and willingness when participating in physical
fitness activity to share and learn experiences from your own and other cultures.

27BCB38A54B34FAF8879D5DCC4B4D53A.description:
Apply and share a movement and physical fitness vocabulary that is intrinsic to
motivate oneself, to impact family, and others in a community.

616BBE76BF0249E297C55EC5FFF2BD94.description:
Analyze fitness knowledge in strength, conditioning, agility, and the
physiological responses of the energy systems effects on the mind and body before, during,
and after physical fitness activities.

EF5ADEA882E44188A8D2DD5C9D3402C3.description:
Determine the role of genetics, age, nutrition, sleep, the environment, and
exercise type on body composition and personal health (e.g., anabolic steroids, human growth
hormones, stimulants).

12B053107F0A460C8F6AB2A08E4E1CB1.description:
Design and implement a personal fitness plan, using evidence and evaluate how
that reflects knowledge and application of fitness-training principals (FITT) and the
components of skill related fitness.

03D2BE9A28F44E89BE5337A09A94F17E.description:
Respect and appreciate all levels of ability and encourage with care during all
physical activities.

CFFCB5232BD4426191053C3C65BDFE94.description:
Compare the short- and long-term benefits of physical activity and the impact on
wellness associated with physical, mental, emotional fitness through one's lifetime.

A73F1BD0CBE54CECA7A55CC14FFB7D32.description:
Develop rule changes to existing games, sports, and activities that enhance
participation, safety, and enjoyment.

6855692A32014CAEBA5E0E5DD96054BA.description:
Analyze etiquette, responsibilities, and preparation of players, officials,
trainers, and other participants and recommend strategies to improve their performance,
participation, and behavior.

658327AFB3F444B496AFBECE12C6A053.description:
Design, lead and critique rhythmic and physical activity that includes
variations in time, space, force, flow, and relationships (e.g., creative, cultural, social,
aerobics dance, fitness).

29312FB126C845CCAEC2965504D698A1.description:
Analyze application of force and motion (e.g., weight transfer, power, speed,
agility, range of motion) and modify movement to impact performance.

0093A3D95C054163A5C3A037DCBD7694.description:
Explain and demonstrate ways to apply movement skills from one game,
sport, aerobics, or recreational activity to another including striking skills (e.g., tennis,
badminton, ping pong, racquetball, pickle ball).

E5D76BE58A7A4C63A8A685A7C3C3A280.description:
Develop an action plan to assist individuals who have feelings of sadness, anxiety,
stress, trauma, or depression and share this information with individuals who will benefit.

5550ED06CE1646F48D8EC0E79EE39DFE.description:
Investigate how local, state, and global agencies are addressing health issues
caused by climate change and share this information in an appropriate setting.

81E2CDA5960A42B285A798B69BFDE942.description:
Describe how individuals and local, state, and global advocacy organizations
can collaborate to address common local and global health and social issues (e.g., hunger, clean
water, organ/tissue donation).

172FF2533C9A4298A1FE98586F48A78B.description:
Evaluate the validity of health information, resources, services, in school, home
and in the community.

7FCCCFB3AD8B4814B6C5159FBDE75349.description:
Analyze a variety of health products and services based on cost, availability,
accessibility, benefits and accreditation in the home, school, and in the community (e.g., suicide
prevention, breast/testicular self-examination, CPR/AED, life skills training, menstrual
products).

C504CB34B4F1446EBC23E383297F137A.description:
Identify medically accurate sources of information and local services that
provide contraceptive methods (including emergency contraception and condoms) and
pregnancy options (including parenting, abortion, safe haven, adoption, and prenatal care).

0C80D545114842CAB54F5785D8371B3A.description:
Explain the purpose of the Safe Haven Law and identify locations in your
community.

3BB08DA69DC44E129A4CAA276E6DBEB9.description:
Develop an advocacy plan for a health issue and share this information with
others who can benefit.

0CB581383002424E8392091FE3B47A74.description:
Analyze the opportunities available at home, in school, and in the community to
support the mental health of oneself or an individual.

3D27F2EB13DE475A8F5C1E02D0EA9811.description:
Analyze the state and federal laws related to minors’ ability to give and receive
sexual consent and their association with sexually explicit media.

F5AA685A46954310AE505E5FD116EB98.description:
Analyze the personal and societal factors that could keep someone from leaving
an unhealthy relationship.

1F23260B3BE643B8B1D4F53E2E99F55D.description:
Describe the human sexual response cycle, including the role of hormones and
pleasure.

62AE3714CD764539BBD45FBC7AADDB84.description:
Analyze factors that influence the choices, and effectiveness of safer sex
methods and contraception, including risk-reduction and risk-elimination strategies.

304370C7C5DF4334868EAEA54304D9F0.description: Analyze the benefits of abstinence from sexual activity using reliable resources.

602DC76CD63644A1813A6D3A39DA21A9.description:
Demonstrate ways to show respect for the boundaries of others as they relate to
intimacy and sexual behavior.

026BB2ECFD964247A75DC0BAEA3824B2.description:
Demonstrate strategies to prevent, manage, or resolve interpersonal conflicts
without harming self or others (defining and understanding the laws of consent and dating
violence).

306B3A961ECD4EA89DBB4CE47B6864EC.description:
Analyze current social issues affecting perceptions of sexuality, culture,
ethnicity, disability status and make recommendations to address those issues.

BDE159B5135040C199E9A607F5ABAAF0.description:
Advocate for school and community policies and programs that promote dignity
and respect for people of all genders, gender expressions, gender identities, and sexual
orientations.

5648DE78602742E5BEEDAD60C1DC9619.description:
Analyze the influences of peers, family, media, social norms and culture on the
expression of gender, sexual orientation, and identity.

5C0A6C59B3D1425DBD79F0189BF1EAE0.description:
Analyze and adapt mental and emotional health messages and communication
techniques to peers and other specific target audience (e.g., dimensions of health).

4A1D0D1DCD324988982FB79D59372068.description:
Describe strategies to appropriately respond to stressors in a variety of situations
(e.g., academics, relationships, shootings, death, car accidents, illness).

9264F7A4451C479698CDBAA5D4CC264B.description:
Analyze factors that influence the emotional and social impact of mental health
illness on the family.

69A6AE6272854E6F8C8007C386C41141.description:
Recognize one’s personal traits, strengths, and limitations and identify how to
develop skills to support a healthy lifestyle.

96F05945D54F42B0B33DEFEA5B71543C.description:
Evaluate parenting strategies used at various stages of child development
based on reliable sources of information.

79ADB5914D974393B0C87F9CB8C380D5.description: Assess the skills needed to be an effective parent.

61E4DB9FB1004AE18D1DAE3EE86640FE.description:
Analyze the emotional, social, physical, and financial effects of being a teen or
young adult parent.

89834722CEA24479B825070BA8DF9B11.description:
Analyze personal and societal factors that can influence decisions about
pregnancy options, including parenting, abortion, safe haven, and adoption.

0AA332D80C774EC39DD41B547AFAB160.description:
Analyze factors that can impact the health of a baby (e.g., fetal alcohol
syndrome, sudden infant death syndrome, low birth weight, premature birth, genetics).

43690084545A4EFA909D43C099B75EC9.description:
List the major milestones of each trimester of fetal development utilizing
medically accurate information.

2EC477B61E2D44B68F13ACB216C9933E.description:
Identify trusted adults, including family members, caregivers, school staff, and
health care professionals to ask questions and discuss pregnancy and other health topics.

5BCE8C09C2C54EDAAD22B386F6DBD34A.description:
Develop a plan to eliminate or reduce risk for unintended pregnancy and/or
STIs (including HIV) and identify ways to overcome potential barriers to prevention.

045D029134A14CC8BDC624A1CBA7DAFE.description:
Compare and contrast the advantages and disadvantages of contraceptive and
disease prevention methods (e.g., abstinence, condoms, emergency contraception, dental
dams).

5E446E828FF34C5496E4C6BE5B82708F.description:
Predict how healthy and unhealthy behaviors can affect brain development
and impact physical, social and emotional stages of early adulthood.

4591EDDBC8834C5AB109A0402AC35A55.description:
Develop a health care plan that includes practices and strategies designed to
support an active lifestyle, attend to mental health, and foster a healthy, social and
emotional life.

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

92C155F9447647D8B57688E783EAB6F2.description:
Work with 2 × 2 matrices as a transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute
value of the determinant in terms of area.

ABF5B6F96F19449D80D477011AA8CE4D.description:
Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable
dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

DB6C4E21496C4D47AF45C0B07C3A7E64.description:
Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and
multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a
square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

489B7FB4A9B74541950410F383B87675.description:
Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square
matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive
properties.

A3A5D8F8A58C41DDB9261696F2F3CEC3.description: Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

B318D8B147CF4B1EB9E3ABFFC1582DE9.description:
Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs
in a game are doubled.

59B3682E173B428ABD2CB9AFF0A74FF9.description:
Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence
relationships in a network.

655214D8BA9A45AFA978AE04ACA0AF4A.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications

1C9FF14BCE4B4FF7AAD2631F30BE136A.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ‖cv‖=|c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v≠0, the direction of cv is either  along v (for c >0) or against v (for c < 0).

7A0B831DB10E4A58BD63AEDCA0154D1C.description:
Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly
reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(v_x,v_y)=(cv_x,cv_y).

7AD431D5635145E89CD2FE19A4320BA7.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

D21DCA6A00064E488983B6354620F736.description:
Understand vector subtraction v - w as v + (-w), where -w is the additive inverse of w, with the same
magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction
graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector
subtraction component-wise.

6B06C578D3F44128A0ED0427E41D74F8.description:
Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and
direction of their sum.

5CC3BC7108514B0C9A95E3A1C6D7541B.description:
Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule.
Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of
the magnitudes.

67EC5EC2D8CC43CBA325FEB9357B0D6A.description:
Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by
vectors.

67AC0EE61E8E4DA2A6251AF0E3F89CE8.description:
Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from
the coordinates of a terminal point.

1D14EB6F359142E5BB472BBEA01B3393.description:
Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their
magnitudes (e.g., v,|v|,‖v‖,v).

7E17ED4599044BF3922B3FFC46E67687.description: Represent and model with vector quantities

DE8408D398094DA691E21B64F4E09A2A.description:
Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic
polynomials.

0086C971D43E4B3294BC8A7D5317D752.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers. For example, rewrite x^2+4 as (x+2i)(x-2i).

AEF3B593DF914D7CB1FEBD5FB614761F.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

768A464D84F54E7283E0440426BB895E.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations

DC43B3ED8CFB43EFB1332686144F9451.description:
Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the
difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

D7F37C3625454E4DB6A911F8651F8F35.description:
Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers
geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for
computation. For example, (-1+√3i )^3=8 because -1+√3i has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

79FF920375084B58BB143DD80C00A5AA.description:
Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form
(including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms
of a given complex number represent the same number.

D41483EF99BE48A09CCCC492C3798579.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane

F27CAA00945248D8BD62C94FDE310573.description:
Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients
of complex numbers.

AE4B6363F5124F9FB0B2886DB7FC5A65.description:
Use the relation i^2=-1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add,
subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

31138CD8EEB24F95A01F80B58E50693B.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i^2=-1 and every complex number has the form a+bi with a and b real.

E9E5D003DB5747238046389BED9D1668.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers

95D96A9BA9B6452D983D8D48624A5DCD.description:
Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting
quantities.

16BF66521019403B9A874AFDC76ED481.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

9D602BA407514DEF971FBAB17A948FB7.description:
Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step
problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the
scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

586D9DB83651436A8BDF1BE678DF48BC.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems

B17F4815496247DCBF6EA1AF8C3AB410.description: Simplify radicals, including algebraic radicals (e.g. ∛54=3∛2, simplify √(32x^2)).

AA27C53926EF4BFC831B609181087C5B.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

71B09761A66847A5AD2041BA07E92FB6.description:
Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending
the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in
terms of rational exponents. For example, we define 5^(1/3) to be the cube root of 5 because we
want (5^(1/3) )^3=5^((1/3)^3) to hold, so (5^(1/3))^3 must equal 5.

197862FCE9A846DF9AE371955BE81EB4.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

0AD54B3BA451411FAC611254626C6D5C.description:
Derive and/or explain the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the
common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate
mortgage payments.

559119A0F2114BD09FDF03D88820BB6D.description:
Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential
functions. For example, the expression 1.15^t can be rewritten as (1.15^(1/12) )^12t≈1.012^12t to reveal the
approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

EC2776FC006845568E89BD480628F790.description:
Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or
minimum value of the function it defines.

9A83F714FF8F493DA31C2974F049C30D.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

42E07529C0F94C9FB9FEC17288B3A3F0.description:
Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties
of the quantity represented by the expression.

44A28CF4B82C4499A627BCCD210A1A89.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

8856A8F78EE042BAA7CAD830CF054F6B.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x^4-y^4 as (x^2 )^2-(y^2 )^2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x^2-y^2 )(x^2+y^2).

E3CABA204B1A474381B14CA4B0C0153E.description:
Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a
single entity. For example, interpret P(1+r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending
on P.

D34DBD0CE2A04B15B197D9F3F262C0D7.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

98D2698068BC4FE5B270EF2DB1FEA74F.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

887FA0619C574D4F851A014BF33A9D0F.description:
Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half plane (excluding the
boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear
inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

F635C6BF2AF74E75AA9072216A061FE2.description:
Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y=f(x) and y=f(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x)=g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using
technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive
approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute
value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

3EEC4FA1DC9D4A45BF7667174B59D3E5.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions
plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

77B3E1B91F114D558B0E3CB22994782E.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

32F508547D1F497CABE70819467F0838.description:
Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations
(using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

04B682586ED24104BF9611A809D913FF.description: Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

05B3471C10554EDA843711A489B7B375.description:
Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two
variables algebraically and graphically. For example, find the points of intersection
between the line y=-3x and the circle x^2+y^2=3.

7DC06B95FE784CE684C6255744ADCDC5.description:
Solve systems of linear equations algebraically (include using the elimination method)
and graphically, focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

03018FEFEBBD4C2A872EAE4A8FB4F208.description:
Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by
the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same
solutions.

4F2ED87853094907A7ECD9C42D4D51BB.description:
Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x^2=49), taking square roots,
completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the
initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex
solutions and write them as a±bi for real numbers a and b.

2B5CCAA8AFD4454BAC400F6E623C7048.description:
Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x
into an equation of the form (x-p)^2=q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic
formula from this form.

48FA6AD8DFFF44FF924B2381BB7CA455.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

EB6E40E81F0A4A27B85786ECD993BEAA.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with
coefficients represented by letters.

61ACC12F78354A2797E66DAD6481FE02.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

6DDFA0D26FF24D58A9335C65E5B49E13.description:
Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing
how extraneous solutions may arise.

C16DBC8D8F3D438EB471099A377E6DA0.description:
Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers
asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a
solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

334682DBAFC74349A24E7CD798F2D0F2.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

5EE4AE06094848E198D84C0777B5C424.description:
Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in
solving equations. For example, rearrange Ohm’s law V=IR to highlight resistance R.

0FEA69145EC249FA85C31BA76E79E40B.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or
inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on
combinations of different foods.

A2D58659CBC04A12981608013916D474.description:
Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities;
graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

CE471A3857D64BE3AA44B45A98751E86.description:
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include
equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential
functions.

043BE8BAC69F412E9C0D7F8EEBED73FD.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

EA38298388E14E6D89137C9AFDEA874E.description:
Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers,
closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational
expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

048826D5E32E4D5FB773241E207B3E0B.description:
Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write (a(x))/(b(x)) in the form q(x)+(r(x))/(b(x)), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x) using inspection, long
division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

2703A283B2C4487480E764DC5FE7C82E.description:
Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x+y)^n in powers of x and y for a
positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example
by Pascal’s Triangle. (Clarification: The Binomial Theorem can be proved by
mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.)

DB5CAF96240C4B7AA28648BBBABEEFEB.description:
Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For
example, the difference of two squares; the sum and difference of two cubes; the
polynomial identity (x^2+y^2 )^2=(x^2-y^2 )^2+(2xy)^2 can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

4FB0621535DF435EB840032997BCEEB2.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems

9E11D018E01448FFAD443C95F8866478.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

B62FD3A1625C46D58C3E1EC2B1BFF303.description:
Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the
remainder on division by x-a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if x-a is a factor of p(x) .

701BF7C9DEE54F1BB9AE98EEA5807804.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials

8340288CF0134D35887D009C7F77DD56.description:
Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are
closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and
multiply polynomials.

0028675C4F0B45BDBD521D495541795C.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

1870EB43826549848761D9D7FF7EF388.description:
Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them
to solve problems.

059AC99145AE4843ABAD24D61E7872A0.description:
Prove the Pythagorean identity sin⁡^2(θ) + cos^2⁡(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin⁡(θ), cos(θ) or tan⁡(θ) given sin⁡(θ),cos⁡(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the
angle.

CFE5D32DFBAB4D4CB61F83C1AF4D872A.description:
Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts;
evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

79A0713F8C2242B1B69BBFEFF34545EC.description:
Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always
increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

97BF2399A837406283099BD318F48A3F.description:
Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified
amplitude, frequency, and midline.

66C51F97EE514462A7125C1512CD625A.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions

E87F33A39BDC4B15964C72026B62DA26.description: Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

847276832C354C9D86EEE1EBA30D77B6.description:
Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4 , and π/6 and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosines, and tangent for π-x, π+x and 2π-x in
terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

221CB74B2F264E23995D5AEDA7C4BBCA.description:
Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of
trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles
traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

1D62A39FF5F54A67AC688B3429B0C0F8.description:
Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle
subtended by the angle.

F46CB0AC2D154804950781C24CB8AB6D.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle

AC3BE40ACBC0483BBFAF44BD0F577104.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

DB077E7884484AD09ACDAF2B88A048F7.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model

AE240F70140A4229A1A0D532F7E4EE88.description:
Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms. For exponential
models, express as a logarithm the solution ab^ct=d to where a c, and d are numbers and the base b
is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

3C7D46200AC743CFA6EF1934D4D5F8DD.description:
Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually
exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial
function.

3612BE54300F44BD8715BB791613B79B.description:
Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric
sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs
(include reading these from a table).

18DF7C20E98F464CBBDB9350960E3C14.description:
Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent
rate per unit interval relative to another.

0FB4AC3D151049EFAFDFBBDFFDDC21E5.description:
Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit
interval relative to another.

B4B383AB67654CC1A1964A7520DFCA74.description:
Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and
that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

2AC087C7C2834247B0CFBE3F1204A171.description:
Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with
exponential functions.

9FCEE768E5D34B2082F1976737863E00.description: Construct and compare linear and exponential models and solve problems

BAF444100A724AF39B3D88E70CF215E2.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph
of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the
larger maximum.

66CFC97A37AB408EB4E861F04522BB5B.description:
Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. For
example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y=(1.02)^t, y=(.97)^t, y=(1.01)^12t, y=(1.01)^(t/10) and classify them as
representing exponential growth or decay.

62C81AB766524D36BD598A296AEC55B7.description:
Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show
zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a
context.

5DA7ADF543A847E295BA44CF55EC6FAA.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and
explain different properties of the function.

6DBFD97646B2434C89C0FB6F57B536BA.description: Graph trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

DCAD943EBEE74237B28387DEBDE61837.description:
Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end
behavior.

C21B8C1813394945BB827073FB0F6BB6.description:
Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable
factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

018A4CDD15F14286AF2AD2233EC07AA0.description:
Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are
available, and showing end behavior.

03C02656EA8F47769A673F6B46A286B4.description:
Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step
functions and absolute value functions.

D04E652CA38F4AA1A12B9633B7742D1A.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

B168006598A14A70944D92B7B3F3F523.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in
simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

36D031297590484FB119E4F672AD9716.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically
or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

680C952528F94BEC82DE24B34F4C4B3C.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative
relationship it describes. For example, if the function gives the number of person-hours it
takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an
appropriate domain for the function.

2B043E62ECC747F6A82A9DD0EF6EABF6.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of
graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features
given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals
where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums
and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

A9AB647ED55E4F8C80044012A04E5DB1.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context

5697F449A17E4825A4382F0F1D9F3E8B.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is
a subset of the integers. For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0)=f(1)=1, f(n+1)=f(n)+f(n-1) for n≥1.

E9650A1B90F04D40AD32CF0A5A4ECF2E.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret
statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

9D1764FD9AE24C0ABB946137568C8AA9.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the
range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a
function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to
the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y=f(x) .

46EA753CA6534A039FECE4685AF8DFF2.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

91838D891B9E41858EF3795B7B668A41.description:
Use the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms to solve problems
involving logarithms and exponents.

8119F809ED16442380A3CD169B89EEB9.description:
Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the
domain.

B5F5BE006F394CB6AB3E01BDC8EF872A.description:
Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the
function has an inverse.

BF2D1A4239F5482FB4A5A600BD2CE510.description: Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

BB8C2087704A4D44B9F06899432EE0A2.description:
Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and
write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x)=2x^3 or f(x)=((x+1))/((x-1)) for x≠1.

271CA0F2A2B3484EABAE45A01A914672.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x+k) for specific values of k (both
positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and
illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing
even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

115009E225AB4B7E8F7EA3BD175BF326.description: Build new functions from existing functions

35D034321D19438F93B9F77A0B6BA426.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

C63F0BEA5EBC45D587D5C90C8F743348.description:
Compose functions. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a
function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time,
then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of
time.

BC909CA6B245449E849B2D24DCC96837.description:
Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build
a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant
function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

C13E8D955C0F4C03BAD9D8836999AF38.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

9949AA98A2AD4E8ABFF0558EF847F87C.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

D0A3767B86B1415F93C620464D225DBC.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

46114E78603341BFBAB584E11B20B09C.description:
Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown
measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

6C21BBAF93674678B93A7B86AF61B894.description: Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

74DE289378034C9B933E26C2B1A096D0.description:
Derive the formula A=1/2 ab sin⁡(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex
perpendicular to the opposite side.

4029385619CC45748F262EF4B0727832.description:
Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied
problems.

D9B7B9695702464680EBA39D607DDED5.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

EC67A8C15E4E4A8DB44AA0FE7FD47C66.description:
Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in
the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

2E492E1FDFF146848DCA84FACC7B76C6.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles

F6C5C418B70043BEBFA2554050DFDE70.description:
Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove
relationships in geometric figures.

A0ECBC316CAD4E9998E299FEA87197C0.description:
Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle
divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved
using triangle similarity.

F1F80EC74FCB42FEAC8A9268E32B0989.description:
Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two
triangles to be similar.

F51F86AB2A3245AC91D45DEFD1FE91B5.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations
to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of
similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the
proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

0BA864ADFB0C44918C5FCF7E2657F974.description:
The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale
factor.

1BBC2FD09B064A958BD59B37976F4F84.description:
A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel
line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

6BA53859461F43A79697F175EED4D1F8.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor:

0B7CCD58405142ED99B1020B1E619972.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations

FAA4C35481624BB79B9A8ABF35663974.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure
to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems
based on ratios).

6FCB7E02FD6F44DF8EBA97986E5B3245.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons
per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

B2F97D09682A4EDFBFDF56F143FE98AF.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g.,
modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

DFF6940406FE4AF095AA55D3824445B7.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations

9D786FD50A8E4575924D4E45578EC5DE.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles,
e.g., using the distance formula.

E1452AF3B0EE4EC9AA803EE9423F1D83.description:
Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the
segment in a given ratio.

0C73D58F3BE84A83881C72153419D4B0.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve
geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given
line that passes through a given point).

85243890B7E14DA8988DAF19AAC0AB61.description:
Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. For example, prove or
disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle;
prove or disprove that the point (1,√3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing
the point (0, 2).

F6B75B0754284949A42EB6129ADA2374.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically

DD3F79E6F9AB4ADA95E7BFBC477FB8D4.description:
Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the
sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.

DA1DCF30089E428D9B1D9CFFE495BA52.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

13790E1696094601AE2C9198B26E7475.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean
Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an
equation.

1844055026B443ACB12A34B41D546F2C.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section

DEEAD3E4A44F4E93841C1FEEF44F014F.description:
Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and
identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

74483CAD7CD4417D9C3EFF279EA40B68.description: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects

7201597CE668443F90DADB82BA32B314.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

7E2A40D777644B18B2A1765331BF93A7.description: Give an informal argument using Cavalieri’s principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

CEDE12414618437B8566885E3CDA0E6B.description:
Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a
circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri’s
principle, and informal limit arguments.

F8CD4CC880874BD7AB1D0A835AC00312.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems

590BECE926C24B2D9B52012D1D604394.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

193C34D7D8B44439A4B531C51DAA363D.description:
Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent,
opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and
conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

93F38C22AAC64F128B6A0E8E0057EC78.description:
Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a
triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining
midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the
medians of a triangle meet at a point.

0EBEDD3190CB4A17962396264416ABCA.description:
Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent;
when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and
corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment
are exactly those equidistant from the segment’s endpoints.

9443088FCA954ADEAF11605AEA1C23D4.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the
definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

43E75EDEEB1D4E14A0405FF510181A3C.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are
congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles
are congruent.

C64AB75EE95345E1BA872CBCDC6E9412.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect
of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of
congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

CE4FB94DDE86437495B03D5C993CAD32.description: Understand Congruence in terms of rigid motions

68179E2A70D143AD939936843058D013.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of
transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

75F5710D249C400585A88F52BA1434A1.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles,
perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

521C5F789D2049A5B43E9D654E78F2E4.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations
and reflections that carry it onto itself.

111EA9289F9245F0BB73BA204B0AA5ED.description:
Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software;
describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other
points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that
do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

A89F651A050C4D4BABF30F360FA84CE5.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line
segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance
around a circular arc.

655FDB4D260245F89DE260DCC1893F20.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane

433D7238EC2D46889027CC44A1132683.description:
Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is
proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of
proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

6588C54C63DF41378C6A151B3A12AEC3.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles

C83C6E2EA63E4A788DAD2B00F3361200.description: Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

6BB159F3A3A842D185F9EF76CE64A70C.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of
angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

3423F436061A4554B89685C020EA5CC6.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the
relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a
diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the
radius intersects the circle.

E6C187926E244EE4A6CAAFAB45C6D494.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

067E58AF667443359CCB191C982471DF.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles

document.title: New Jersey Student Learning Standards Mathematics (NJSLS—Mathematics)

ECC0123D0BFB41E5BDFCDBD5326BA4F7.description:
Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing,
medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

81BF1265E9924D38A81420F2E327E3B1.description:
Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number
generator).

BF88BD92522D49E1B84367D7C5D00EC8.description:
Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values. For example,
compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy
using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.

9A91F6ADB25743A7BFD8C5FB5D296A0D.description:
Find the expected payoff for a game of chance. For example, find the expected
winnings from a game at a fast food restaurant.

A6DA5B9550C04BBA9FC194D203CD6225.description:
Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values
and finding expected values. For example, find the forecasted value of an investment.

4F135366BE59431785F3BA13B3F78DD3.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions

8D8968B0A956412DAC10B1D18B6F8405.description:
Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in
which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value. For example, find a
current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and
calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you
expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?

216A04CD19EE4B6FA6C0D0FB5EE8D2C1.description:
Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in
which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value. For example,
find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by
guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four
choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

E4B38EC24F6749C68CE9B2CF7EA73611.description:
Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the
probability distribution.

9345218BB79F4ED9A69C11B4AD048039.description:
Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to
each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

CFA69A4B5DD24155AE75EDAEDC45F48F.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems

3C444D7260C842C28C0064A4F86C7D15.description:
Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and
solve problems.

0818D92E347F4EAD863BFA65C3CAD81A.description:
Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(AandB)=P(A)P(B|A)=P(B)P(A|B) and interpret
the answer in terms of the model.

153704A30D0146268CF064426A5FCB44.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(AorB)=P(A)+P(B)-P(AandB), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

73E9048DB9E14873836CC5DA9259BBC8.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B’s outcomes that also belong
to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

F8CD061628004D7689A6AEE15316544D.description:
Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform
probability model

F3409499E2B34BE6986B7E19182BC30A.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in
everyday language and everyday situations. For example, compare the chance of having
lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung

(e.g., color, texture, type of material) and measurable attributes (e.g., length, capacity, height).

891F8D63466E4AA68CE7B45194846D98.description: Children begin to conceptualize measurable attributes of objects.

11E78BEE4C2343A5871B4624ACDC3F65.description:
Begin to represent simple word problem data in pictures and
drawings.

23C6CDE125874C2C8F819EE2D95B097E.description:
taking apart and taking from (“I have four carrot sticks.
I’m eating one. Now I have 3.”).

093BCF2DA86746D8B760230E0B128726.description:
putting together and adding to (e.g., “3 blue pegs, 2 yellow
pegs, 5 pegs altogether.”); and

C4A8D5EA3D31482E95C150ADF0D224CE.description:
Represent addition and subtraction by manipulating up to 5
objects:

8D8A36BAD0714B0998F3F6BEADF62693.description: Children demonstrate an initial understanding of numerical operations.

C8EA3D0FD01D4FFC8625E19C5FA6BF08.description:
Compare groups of up to 5 objects (e.g., beginning to use terms
such as “more,” “less,” “same”).

3ED8A89DFB1F4456B2B53D22394BF4F1.description:
Use one to one correspondence to solve problems by matching
sets (e.g., getting just enough straws to distribute for each juice
container on the table) and comparing amounts (e.g., collecting
the number of cubes needed to fill the spaces in a muffin tin
with one cube each).

672B7649E18449C9A2B509C6D37C5FD1.description:
Instantly recognize, without counting, small quantities of up
to 3 or 4 objects (i.e., subitize).

6F62F52C15C2432695F9C04B0BBBB032.description:
Arrange and count different kinds of objects to demonstrate
understanding of the consistency of quantities (i.e., “5” is
constant, whether it is a group of 5 people, 5 blocks or 5 pencils).

1B79708722454E5EA07062A6A3F894B2.description:
Accurately count quantities of objects up to 10, using one-to
one-correspondence, and accurately count as many as 5 objects
in a scattered configuration.

0D13D64F5C3348C9AAAC6CBB5368DBF1.description:
Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities
(i.e., the last word stated when counting tells “how many”):

C227CEF7A75F407FAA793BF08EC9030A.description:
Know that written numbers are symbols for number quantities
and, with support, begin to write numbers from 0 to 10.

50C2C6A797884505B1D9E62622DE347D.description:
Recognize and name one-digit written numbers up to 10 with
minimal prompting.

BBF61E8EB2B2481F83635B1B95812615.description: Count to 20 by ones with minimal prompting.

738B8A67E89F443FA247A6BBCFEFC1B7.description:
Children begin to demonstrate an understanding of number and
counting.

document.title: Preschool Teaching and Learning Standards 2014

0AA615A8936043B2BF2D1038DA3605F6.description:
Identify and use basic tools and technology to extend exploration
in conjunction with science investigations (e.g., writing, drawing,
and painting utensils, scissors, staplers, magnifiers, balance
scales, ramps, pulleys, hammers, screwdrivers, sieves, tubing,
binoculars, whisks, measuring cups, appropriate computer
software and website information, video and audio recordings,
digital cameras, tape recorders).

8C8D4A2365544F50B4F6A92EC8D0B1CB.description: Children gain experience in using technology.

CC2F29F6EFCE4AE7AEFF57AE9E8CDAED.description:
Demonstrate emergent awareness of the need for conservation,
recycling, and respect for the environment (e.g., turning off
water faucets, collecting empty yogurt cups for reuse as paint
containers, separating materials in recycling bins, re-using clean
paper goods for classroom collage and sculpture projects).

43CC6338AA424C77A0390CF3ACB9D524.description:
Observe and record weather (e.g., chart temperatures
throughout the seasons or represent levels of wind by waving
scarves outdoors).

A73A2CD14B6247D0A46830EF88BDF27E.description:
Explore the effects of sunlight on living and nonliving things
(e.g., growing plants with and without sunlight, investigating
shadows that occur when the sun’s light is blocked by objects).

353BD9A48EBE40179C599948E8D1EF26.description:
Explore and describe characteristics of soil, rocks, water, and air
(e.g., sorting rocks by shape and/or color, observing water as a
solid and a liquid, noticing the wind’s effect on playground
objects).

5C8F1471A5834BBE89D93C15996AF2B6.description: Children observe and investigate the Earth.

10B594D0B99644B3B84B901F216571B8.description:
Observe and record change over time and cycles of change that
affect living things (e.g., monitoring the life cycle of a plant,
using children’s baby photographs to discuss human change
and growth, using unit blocks to record the height of classroom
plants).

933ADEEEE6FE47AB999D31CC92C90D43.description:
Observe and describe how natural habitats provide for the basic
needs of plants and animals with respect to shelter, food, water,
air, and light (e.g., digging outside in the soil to investigate the
kinds of animal life that live in and around the ground or
replicating a natural habitat in a classroom terrarium).

359925A25783494F97B7EA8F2891338B.description:
Observe similarities and differences in the needs of living
things, and differences between living and nonliving things
(e.g., observing and discussing similarities between animal
babies and their parents; discussing the differences between a
living thing, such as a hermit crab, and a nonliving thing, such
as a shell).

B8823C2873D444F2885DB69BF6F4DE31.description:
Investigate and compare the basic physical characteristics of
plants, humans, and other animals (e.g., observing and
discussing leaves, stems, roots, body parts; observing and
drawing different insects; sorting leaves by shape; comparing
animals with fur to those with feathers).

C542F50CA133409088912DD6FA430895.description: Children observe and investigate living things.

90963D23AA274235A368C36EF2C73CD7.description:
Investigate how and why things move (e.g., slide block, balance
structures, push structures over, use ramps to explore how far and
how fast different objects move or roll).

F76B50029D584E42B52FF4ED4D1D7E9B.description:
Investigate sound, heat, and light energy through one or more of
the senses (e.g., comparing the pitch and volume of sounds made
by commercially made and homemade instruments, recording
how shadows change during the course of a day or over time,
using flashlights or lamp light to make shadows indoors).

0E82C745859C48468093F86265E9EF04.description:
Explore changes in liquids and solids when substances are
combined, heated, or cooled (e.g., mixing sand or clay with
various amounts of water; preparing gelatin; mixing different
colors of tempera paint; and longer term investigations, such as
the freezing and melting of water and other liquids).

CA468B33A9924C99813F7BA40953FADB.description:
Observe, manipulate, sort, and describe objects and materials
(e.g., water, sand, clay, paint, glue, various types of blocks,
collections of objects, simple household items that can be taken
apart, or objects made of wood, metal, or cloth) in the classroom
and outdoor environment based on size, shape, color, texture,
and weight.

7834AD15FE534B3F948A708C8D2359BA.description: Children observe and investigate matter and energy.

4A70813C5228476FACB5CE3386951F6A.description:
Represent observations and work through drawing, recording
data, and “writing” (e.g., drawing and “writing” on observation
clipboards, making rubbings, charting the growth of plants).

CB10BFB80A2A4CA28CDF850DA8818678.description:
Communicate with other children and adults to share
observations, pursue questions, make predictions, and/or
conclusions.

F1695A9E99B8490FA2A144BB8FBA7DD3.description:
Use basic science terms (e.g., observe, predict, experiment) and
topic-related science vocabulary (e.g., words related to living
things [fur, fins, feathers, beak, bark, trunk, stem]; weather
terms [breezy, mild, cloudy, hurricane, shower, temperature];
vocabulary related to simple machines [wheel, pulley, lever,
screw, inclined plane]; words for states of matter [solid, liquid];
names of basic tools [hammer, screwdriver, awl, binoculars,
stethoscope, magnifier]).

B521E0FB97A54D549C51941D359D09E2.description:
Observe, question, predict, and investigate materials, objects,
and phenomena during classroom activities indoors and
outdoors and during any longer-term investigations in progress.
Seek answers to questions and test predictions using simple
experiments or research media (e.g., cracking a nut to look
inside; putting a toy car in water to determine whether it sinks).

C7E518F2EF164C6EB3E6456914CD6EC0.description:
Display curiosity about science objects, materials, activities, and
longer-term investigations in progress (e.g., ask who, what,
when, where, why, and how questions during sensory
explorations, experimentation, and focused inquiry).
